One day, a chubby rubber duck was floating in a pond. He was happy and quacking away. Suddenly, he heard a snap in the distance. He stopped swimming and looked around. It was a dragonfly! The dragonfly had its wings open and was snapping them shut. It was so fast! The rubber duck was amazed. He wanted to be able to fly too. He started whistling and the dragonfly came closer. The dragonfly snapped its wings again and the rubber ducks eyes lit up. He stretched out his wings to try and do the same, but they wouldn't move. He was too chubby! He sighed and sank down in the pond. The dragonfly flew away, and the chubby rubber duck was left alone. Suddenly, another snap echoed through the air! It was louder this time. The rubber duck looked up, and there was a bigger dragonfly! This dragonfly was much bigger, and it came in for a closer look. Then it blew a soft breeze at the duck, and it was enough for his wings to move. He started flapping them faster and faster, until he rose above the pond. His wings were stronger than he had thought! The rubber duck was so happy he could fly. He quacked with joy as the bigger dragonfly flapped alongside him. He was no longer chubby and unhappy - he was free!

"Hello, hello!" they shouted.

The people on the boat waved back. They smiled and said, "We are going to the island. Do you want to come with us?"

Lily and Max looked at each other. They had never been to the island. They wondered what it was like.

"Yes, please!" they said.

The people on the boat helped them get on board. They gave them life jackets and hats. They told them the island was very beautiful. It had many trees, flowers, birds and animals.

Lily and Max were very excited. They held hands and looked at the water. They saw fish, dolphins and turtles. They heard the wind and the waves.

Soon, they reached the island. The people on the boat helped them get off. They said, "You can explore the island for a while. We will come back for you later. Have fun!"

Lily and Max thanked them and ran to the shore. They saw a big palm tree with coconuts. They saw a colorful parrot on a branch. They saw a monkey swinging from a vine. They saw a butterfly on a flower.

They sat under the palm tree and ate the fruits. They looked at the sky and the sea. They saw the sun shining and the clouds moving. They saw the boat waiting for them.

They said, "This island is very beautiful. We had a lot of fun. But we miss our home and our family."

They hugged each other and said, "We are best friends. We love each other."

They got up and ran to the boat. They said goodbye to the island and the animals. They said thank you to the people on the boat. They put on their life jackets and hats. They held hands and looked at the water.

They saw the fish, the dolphins and the turtles. They heard the wind and the waves.

They smiled and said, "We had a great adventure. But we are happy to go home."

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their bikes. One day, they saw a big ladder near a tree. Lily wanted to ride the ladder and see the birds. Ben was scared of the ladder. He said, "No, Lily, don't ride the ladder. It is too high and you can fall."

But Lily did not listen to Ben. She said, "I am brave and I want to ride the ladder. You are a baby and you are afraid." She left her bike and climbed the ladder. Ben stayed with his bike and watched Lily.

Lily reached the top of the ladder and saw the birds. She was happy and shouted, "Look, Ben, I can see the birds. They are so pretty and they sing so nice." But then, a big wind came and shook the ladder. Lily was scared and lost her balance. She fell from the ladder and hurt her knee. She cried and cried.

Ben heard Lily cry and ran to help her. He said, "Lily, are you okay? I am sorry you fell. I will get help." He left his bike and ran to find a grown-up. He found a lady who was walking her dog. He said, "Please, lady, help my friend. She fell from the ladder and hurt her knee." The lady followed Ben and saw Lily. She said, "Oh, poor girl. Let me see your knee. I have a band-aid and some water." She cleaned Lily's knee and put a band-aid on it. She said, "There, there. You will be fine. But you should not ride the ladder. It is dangerous and not for children."

Lily was still crying and upset. She said, "I am sorry, Ben. I was wrong and you were right. I should have listened to you. You are a good friend and not a baby. Can you forgive me?" Ben smiled and hugged Lily. He said, "Of course, I forgive you, Lily. You are my best friend and I love you. But next time, please be careful and don't ride the ladder. We can ride our bikes and have fun." Lily nodded and said, "Thank you, Ben. I love you too. And thank you, lady, for helping me." The lady smiled and said, "You are welcome, children. Now, go and play, but be safe." Lily and Ben took their bikes and rode away. They learned their lesson and never rode the ladder again.

Tom and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to make shapes with their blocks and pretend they were animals or cars or houses. Tom had a big orange circle that he used as a wheel for his truck. Lily had a small lock that she used as a necklace for her doll.

"Can I have your circle, Tom?" Lily asked. "It is so bright and pretty. I want to make a sun for my doll."

"No, Lily, it is mine!" Tom said. "You have your lock, that is enough. Go away!"

Lily felt sad and angry. She wanted to play with the circle too. She thought Tom was being mean and selfish. She waited until Tom was not looking and grabbed the circle from his truck. She ran away with it to her doll.

"Hey, give it back!" Tom shouted. He chased after Lily and tried to take the circle from her. They both pulled and tugged on the circle, but neither of them would let go.

Suddenly, the circle broke in half. The two pieces fell to the floor with a loud noise. Tom and Lily looked at the broken circle and started to cry.

"Look what you did!" Tom said. "You broke my circle! It was my favorite toy!"

"No, you did!" Lily said. "You were not nice to me! You did not share your circle!"

They both blamed each other and kept crying. They did not notice that their mom had come into the room. She saw the broken circle and the two children.

"What happened here?" she asked. "Why are you crying? Why did you break the circle?"

Tom and Lily told their mom what had happened. They both said it was the other's fault. They both wanted the circle.

Mom shook her head and sighed. She picked up the two pieces of the circle and showed them to Tom and Lily.

"Look, children, this is what happens when you do not share and play nicely. You break things and hurt each other. The circle was a toy for both of you, not just one of you. You could have taken turns or played together with it. But instead, you fought over it and now it is ruined. Do you see?"

Tom and Lily nodded. They felt sorry and ashamed. They realized they had been wrong and foolish. They hugged each other and said they were sorry.

"I'm sorry, Tom, I should not have taken your circle," Lily said.

"I'm sorry, Lily, I should have shared my circle with you," Tom said.

They gave the pieces of the circle to their mom and asked her to fix it. Mom smiled and said she would try. She told them to go and play with their other toys and be kind and gentle to each other.

Tom and Lily did as their mom said. They learned their lesson and never fought over the circle again. They became better friends and had more fun with their toys. They understood that sharing is caring and that being nice is better than being mean.

"What game?" Ben and Lily asked.

One day, a boy and a girl went to the forest with their dad. They wanted to see the animals and the plants. Dad had a spear to protect them from danger. He told the boy and the girl to stay close to him and to trust him.

They saw many things in the forest. They saw green trees and red flowers. They saw brown bears and gray rabbits. They saw yellow birds and blue butterflies. They were happy and curious.

But then, they saw something else. It was big and orange. It had sharp teeth and a long tail. It was a tiger. The tiger saw them too. It growled and ran towards them.

The boy and the girl were scared. They screamed and hugged each other. Dad lifted his spear and faced the tiger. He said, "Don't worry, my children. I will keep you safe. Trust me."

He threw his spear at the tiger. The spear hit the tiger in the chest. The tiger roared and fell to the ground. It did not move anymore.

Dad ran to the boy and the girl. He hugged them and kissed them. He said, "You are brave, my children. I am proud of you. You trusted me and I protected you. I love you."

The boy and the girl smiled and said, "We love you too, dad. You are strong and kind. You saved us from the tiger. Thank you."

They left the forest and went back home. They were happy and grateful. They trusted their dad and he trusted them. They were a family.

Lila and Tom were twins who liked to play in the garden. One day, they found a big sack behind the shed. They opened it and saw many candles of different colors and shapes.

"Wow, look at these!" Lila said. "They are so pretty and shiny. Can we take some?"

"I don't know," Tom said. "Maybe they belong to someone. Maybe they are for a special day."

Lila did not listen. She grabbed a red candle and a blue candle and put them in her pocket. Tom took a green candle and a yellow candle and did the same.

They ran back to the house and went to their room. They closed the door and lit the candles with a match. They put them on the table and watched them glow.

"They are so nice," Lila said. "They make our room look like a fairy tale."

"Yes, they do," Tom said. "But I feel bad. We should not have taken them. What if someone misses them?"

Just then, they heard a knock on the door. It was their grandma, who lived with them. She opened the door and saw the candles.

"Children, what are you doing?" she asked. "Where did you get these candles?"

Lila and Tom looked at each other. They felt ashamed. They told their grandma the truth. They said they found the candles in a sack in the garden and took them without asking.

Their grandma was not angry. She was sad. She said, "These candles are very special. They are from my old country. I brought them with me when I came here. They are for a festival that I celebrate every year. It is a festival of light and hope. I was going to share them with you and teach you about it. But now, some of them are gone."

Lila and Tom felt very sorry. They hugged their grandma and said they were sorry. They said they did not know. They said they would give the candles back.

Their grandma smiled and said, "It's okay, my dears. I forgive you. You made a mistake, but you learned from it. That is how you become wise. Come, let's go to the garden and put the candles back in the sack. Then, we can light them together and celebrate the festival. I will tell you all about it."

Lila and Tom nodded and followed their grandma. They put the candles back in the sack and thanked her for being so kind. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to respect other people's things and to be curious about other cultures. They also learned that their grandma was very wise and loved them very much.

Lila and Tom were friends who liked to play with shapes. They had a big box of shapes that they could make into different things. One day, they decided to make a castle with the shapes. They used the squares and triangles to make the walls and towers, and the circles and stars to make the windows and flags.

"Look at our castle!" Lila said. "It is so big and pretty!"

"Yes, it is!" Tom said. "But we need a king and a queen to live in it. Let's pretend we are the king and queen!"

"OK!" Lila said. "You can be the king and I can be the queen. And we can have a crown and a scepter made of shapes too!"

They looked for shapes that could be a crown and a scepter. They found a yellow star and a red heart. They put the star on Tom's head and the heart on Lila's hand.

"Now we are the king and queen of the castle!" Tom said. "We can do whatever we want!"

They played in the castle for a while, pretending to have a feast, a dance, and a parade. They had a lot of fun.

But then, they heard a loud noise outside. It was a big dog that had escaped from its owner. The dog saw the castle and ran towards it. It wanted to play with the shapes too.

"Look out!" Lila said. "There is a big dog coming! It might break our castle!"

"Let's hide!" Tom said. "Maybe it will go away!"

They ran inside the castle and hid behind the walls. They hoped the dog would not see them.

But the dog saw the castle and thought it was a toy. It jumped on it and knocked it down. The shapes flew everywhere. The dog barked and wagged its tail. It thought it was a fun game.

Lila and Tom were scared and sad. They saw their castle destroyed and their shapes scattered. They cried and hugged each other.

"Go away, dog!" Lila shouted. "You are bad! You ruined our castle!"

The dog heard Lila and looked at her. It tilted its head and whimpered. It did not understand why she was angry. It just wanted to play.

Then, the dog's owner came and saw what had happened. He was sorry and angry too. He grabbed the dog by its collar and scolded it.

"Bad dog! Bad dog!" he said. "You should not play with other people's things! You should know better!"

He apologized to Lila and Tom and helped them pick up their shapes. He said he would buy them a new box of shapes.

Lila and Tom were still sad, but they accepted his apology. They thanked him and said goodbye.

They learned a lesson that day. They learned that not everyone likes to play the same way. They learned that they should be careful with their things and respect other people's things. They learned that they should be brave and stand up for themselves, but also be kind and forgive others. They learned that playing with shapes can be fun, but also dangerous.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they found a big bottle with a skull on it. Lily wanted to own the bottle and keep it in her room. She was bossy and said to Ben, "This is mine. You can't have it. It is very pretty and shiny."

Ben was curious and said, "What is in the bottle? Can we open it and see?" He reached for the bottle, but Lily pulled it away. She said, "No, you can't. It is poison. It will make you sick or die. Only I can touch it. It is mine."

Ben was scared and said, "Poison? Why do you want poison? That is bad. You should not own poison. You should throw it away or give it to a grown-up. It is not pretty or shiny. It is dangerous and ugly."

Lily was stubborn and said, "No, I like it. It is mine. You are silly and dumb. Go away and leave me alone." She hugged the bottle and ran away from Ben.

Ben was sad and angry. He did not want to be friends with Lily anymore. He thought she was mean and selfish. He went to find another friend who was nice and shared. He hoped Lily would not get hurt by the poison. He wished she would listen and be sorry.

Lily had a bad fall from her bike. She hurt her arm and it was very sore. Mom took her to the doctor to see if it was broken. The doctor was nice and gentle. He said he needed to take an x-ray of her arm. He explained that an x-ray was a special picture that showed the bones inside.

Lily was scared of the x-ray machine. It was big and noisy and made a strange beep. She did not want to go near it. She clung to Mom and cried. Mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. The x-ray will not hurt you. It will help the doctor fix your arm. You are a brave girl. Can you accept to try it?"

Lily looked at Mom and nodded. She wiped her tears and took a deep breath. She followed the doctor to the x-ray room. He gave her a delicate bracelet with a number on it. He said it was to keep her safe from the x-ray. He asked her to lie down on a table and hold her arm still. He covered her with a heavy blanket and went behind a glass window. He said, "Ready, Lily? I'm going to take the x-ray now. Smile for the camera!"

Lily heard the beep and saw a flash of light. She smiled and said, "Cheese!" The x-ray was over. The doctor came back and showed her the picture of her arm. He pointed to a small crack in her bone. He said, "You have a fracture, Lily. That means your bone is a little broken. But don't worry, it will heal soon. You just need a cast to protect it."

Lily felt proud of herself. She had accepted to do the x-ray and it was not so bad. She thanked the doctor and asked him to make her cast pink. He smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. Pink is a lovely color. You are a very brave and strong girl." He wrapped her arm in a soft and pink cast. He gave her a sticker and a lollipop. He said, "You did a great job, Lily. Now you can go home and rest. Take good care of your arm and it will get better soon."

Lily hugged Mom and said, "Thank you, Mom. Thank you, doctor. I'm sorry I was scared. The x-ray was not scary. It was interesting. It showed me my bones. They are amazing. I like my pink cast. It makes me feel special. Can I show it to my friends?"

Mom smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. You can show it to your friends. They will be happy for you. They will see how brave and strong you are. I'm very proud of you, Lily. You are my amazing girl." She kissed her arm and said, "Let's go home, Lily. We can read a story and have some ice cream. How does that sound?"

Lily grinned and said, "That sounds wonderful, Mom. I love you, Mom. I love stories and ice cream. And I love my bones. They are delicate but strong. Just like me." She held Mom's hand and walked to the car. She felt happy and hopeful. She knew her arm would heal soon. She knew she could accept anything. She knew she was amazing.

One day, a boy named Leo found an ancient spear in the forest. It was long and sharp and shiny. He was very happy and proud of his spear. He wanted to show it to his friends.

He ran to his friend Mia's house and knocked on the door. "Mia, Mia, come and see what I found!" he shouted.

Mia opened the door and saw Leo holding the spear. She was curious and scared. "What is that, Leo?" she asked.

"It's a spear, Mia. It's very old and cool. I found it in the forest. Do you want to play with it?" Leo said.

Mia shook her head. "No, Leo, I don't want to play with it. It looks dangerous. You could hurt yourself or someone else with it. You should put it back where you found it." she said.

Leo was angry. He thought Mia was silly and boring. He wanted to have fun with his spear. He said, "Fine, Mia, you don't have to play with me. I'll find someone else who likes my spear. Goodbye!" He turned around and ran away.

He went to his friend Ben's house and knocked on the door. "Ben, Ben, come and see what I found!" he shouted.

Ben opened the door and saw Leo holding the spear. He was amazed and excited. "Wow, Leo, that's a spear! It's awesome! Where did you get it?" he asked.

"I found it in the forest, Ben. It's very old and cool. Do you want to play with it?" Leo said.

Ben nodded. "Yes, Leo, I want to play with it. It looks fun. Let's go to the park and pretend we are hunters." he said.

Leo smiled. He thought Ben was smart and fun. He said, "OK, Ben, let's go. But don't tell anyone about the spear. It's our secret." He followed Ben to the park.

They ran around the park, waving the spear and making noises. They pretended they were hunting animals and enemies. They had a lot of fun with the spear.

But they did not see the little girl who was playing with her ball near them. She did not know they were pretending. She was scared of the spear. She thought they were going to hurt her.

She screamed and ran to her mom. Her mom saw the spear and was angry. She called the police. The police came and took the spear away. They scolded Leo and Ben for playing with a dangerous thing. They called their parents and told them what happened.

Leo and Ben were very sorry. They realized they made a big mistake. They learned that the spear was not a toy. They learned that they should not play with things that can hurt others. They learned that they should listen to their friends who care about them.

They apologized to the little girl and her mom. They apologized to Mia and their parents. They promised to never play with the spear again. They invited Mia to play with them in the park. They played with their ball and had fun. They were happy and safe.

"Come back, Lily! It's just a worm. It can't hurt you," Tim said. He followed Lily with the worm in his hand. He wanted to make her laugh.

But Lily did not laugh. She cried and hid behind a tree. She did not want to see the worm. She did not like Tim's joke.

Tim felt guilty. He saw that he made Lily sad. He threw the worm back in the dirt. He said sorry to Lily.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to scare you. I was just playing. Do you forgive me?" Tim asked.

Lily peeked from behind the tree. She saw that Tim was sorry. She wiped her tears and nodded.

"I forgive you, Tim. But don't do that again. I don't like worms. They are icky," Lily said.

Tim hugged Lily and said he was sorry again. They went back to playing in the garden. They found some flowers and butterflies. They were happy again.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes the ball would go too far and they had to look for it in the bushes or behind the trees.

One day, they saw a big pond in the park. It had water and ducks and frogs. Tom and Lily wanted to play with the ball near the pond. They thought it would be fun to see the ball splash in the water.

But their mom said, "No, don't go near the pond. The water is cold and deep. You could fall in and get hurt. And the ball could vanish in the water and you would never see it again."

Tom and Lily did not listen to their mom. They were ignorant and did not care about what she said. They waited until she was busy talking to another mom and then they ran to the pond with their ball.

They kicked the ball to each other near the pond. They laughed and shouted and had fun. But then, Tom kicked the ball too hard and it flew over the pond. It landed in the middle of the water and started to sink.

"Oh no!" Tom cried. "The ball is gone!"

Lily ran to the edge of the pond and looked for the ball. But she could not see it. It had vanished in the water. She felt sad and angry.

"Tom, you are so silly!" she said. "You kicked the ball too hard and now we have no ball. Mom was right. We should not have played near the pond."

Tom felt sad and sorry. He wished he had listened to his mom. He did not know what to do.

"Let's go and tell mom what happened," he said. "Maybe she can help us get the ball back."

But Lily shook her head. She was afraid of what mom would say. She did not want to tell her the truth.

"No, let's not tell mom," she said. "Let's pretend we lost the ball somewhere else. Maybe she will buy us a new one."

Tom and Lily walked away from the pond. They did not see the duck that had swum to the ball and grabbed it with its beak. The duck was happy. It had found a new toy. It quacked and swam away with the ball.

Lily went to her bed and fell asleep. She dreamed of sleeping in a big castle, with a huge bed, a fluffy blanket and a giant teddy bear. She dreamed of sleeping all day and all night, without anyone bothering her.

But when she woke up, she was not happy. She was lonely and bored. She missed her mom and dad. She missed the park. She missed the swings, the slides, the flowers and the ducks. She missed the picnic. She missed the delicious sandwiches, cookies and juice. She realized that sleeping was not the only thing she liked. She realized that she liked to have fun, to play, to explore and to share.

She ran to the window and looked outside. She saw her mom and dad coming back from the park. They were smiling and laughing. They had a basket full of goodies. They looked happy and full.

Lily wanted to join them. She wanted to hug them and tell them she was sorry. She wanted to ask them if they could go to the park again. She wanted to try the delicious sandwiches, cookies and juice.

But it was too late. Her mom and dad did not see her. They did not hear her. They walked past her house and went to the next door. They knocked on the door and greeted their neighbors. They said they had a wonderful time at the park. They said they had a surprise for them. They said they had a new daughter. They said her name was Lily.

Lily was shocked and sad. She realized that her mom and dad had left her. They had given her away. They had replaced her with another Lily. They did not love her anymore. They did not want her anymore.

She cried and cried. She wished she had gone to the park. She wished she had not slept so much. She wished she had not been so selfish. She wished she could change the result.

But she could not. She had made a big mistake. She had lost her family. She had lost her happiness. She had lost everything.

The end.

The big duck saw that Sara was in trouble. He did not like the dog. He flapped his wings and quacked loudly. He swam to the shore and chased the dog away. He was brave and strong. He protected Sara from the dog.

Sara was happy and relieved. She thanked the big duck and gave him the rest of the bread. He ate it and wagged his tail. He was jolly and friendly again. Sara and the big duck became friends. They played and laughed at the pond. Sara was not scared of dogs anymore. She was brave and strong too.

Lily and Tom are playing in the park. They like to run and jump and slide. They see a big hole in the ground. Lily wants to look inside. Tom says no.

"That is a trap. A bad man made it. He wants to catch us and take us away. We have to stay away from it," Tom says.

But Lily is curious. She thinks Tom is scared. She runs to the hole and peeks inside. She sees something shiny. She wants to touch it.

"Come back, Lily! It is not safe!" Tom shouts.

Lily does not listen. She reaches for the shiny thing. But it is a trick. The shiny thing is a button. When Lily presses it, a net falls on her. She is trapped.

"Help! Help!" Lily cries.

Tom hears her. He is very brave. He runs to the hole and sees the net. He looks for a way to free Lily. He sees a pair of scissors on the ground. He picks them up and cuts the net.

"Lily, you are free! Come out!" Tom says.

Lily crawls out of the hole. She is scared and sorry. She hugs Tom and says thank you.

"I am sorry, Tom. You were right. It was a trap. A bad man made it. I should have listened to you," Lily says.

Tom hugs her back and says it is okay.

"Let's go back to the slide. It is more fun and safe," Tom says.

Lily agrees. They run back to the slide and play. They are happy and careful. They do not go near the trap again.

Lily and Ben are birds who live in a nest on a big tree. They like to sing and fly and play with their friends. One day, they see a shiny thing on the ground. It is a ring with a bright stone.

"Wow, look at that!" Lily says. "It is so pretty!"

"Let's go get it!" Ben says. "We can take it to our nest!"

They fly down to the ground and pick up the ring with their beaks. They are very happy and excited. They fly back to their nest and put the ring on a branch.

"Isn't it beautiful?" Lily says. "It makes our nest sparkle!"

"Yes, it does!" Ben says. "We are so lucky!"

But then, they hear a loud voice. It is a man who is looking for his ring. He is very angry and sad. He lost his ring when he was walking with his wife. The ring is very important to him. It is a gift from his wife.

"Hey, you birds!" the man shouts. "Give me back my ring! That is mine!"

Lily and Ben are scared. They do not want to lose their shiny thing. But they also do not want to make the man sad. They do not know what to do.

"Please, please, please!" the man begs. "That ring means a lot to me and my wife. We love each other very much. That ring is a sign of our love. Please, give it back!"

Lily and Ben look at each other. They see that the man is serious and honest. They feel sorry for him. They decide to do the right thing.

"OK, OK, OK!" Lily says. "We will give you back your ring. We are sorry. We did not know it was yours. We just liked it a lot."

"Thank you, thank you, thank you!" the man says. "You are very kind and generous. I am sorry I yelled at you. You can keep this as a reward." He throws a shiny coin to the nest.

Lily and Ben catch the coin with their beaks. They are happy and proud. They have done a good deed. They have also got a new shiny thing for their nest.

They fly to the man and give him back his ring. The man smiles and thanks them again. He puts the ring on his finger and hugs his wife. They walk away, holding hands.

Lily and Ben fly back to their nest. They look at their coin and their ring. They decide to spend the coin on some seeds and berries. They share them with their friends. They also sing a song to celebrate their new shiny thing and their new friends.

The end.

Lily wanted to dress up as a fairy for the party. She had a long pink dress, a shiny crown and a wand that made sparks. She was very happy.

But when she went to the living room, she saw her brother Tom. Tom was dressed as a pirate. He had a black hat, a hook and a sword. He was not happy.

"Fairies are silly," Tom said. "Pirates are cool. You can't come to the party with me. You will make me look bad."

Lily felt sad. She liked her fairy dress. She did not want to make Tom look bad. She wanted to have fun at the party.

"Please, Tom," Lily said. "Let me come with you. I like your pirate costume. You can be the captain and I can be the fairy helper. We can play together."

Tom thought for a moment. He liked being the captain. He did not want to be alone at the party. He saw that Lily's wand made sparks. He liked sparks.

"Okay, Lily," Tom said. "You can come with me. But you have to do what I say. And don't make too many sparks. They might scare the other kids."

Lily nodded. She was glad that Tom let her come. She did not mind doing what he said. She just wanted to be his sister.

They held hands and went to the party. They played with the other kids. They had cake and juice. They had a lot of fun.

Lily and Tom learned that they could be different and still get along. They were happy.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big, white cloud in the sky. It looked like a fluffy pillow.

"Let's jump on the cloud!" Lily said. "It must be soft and fun!"

"But how can we reach it?" Ben asked. "It is too high for us."

Lily had an idea. She ran to the shed and got a big, red balloon. She blew it up and tied it to her wrist. Then she gave another balloon to Ben.

"Now we can fly to the cloud!" she said. "Hold on tight!"

They jumped and jumped, and the balloons lifted them up in the air. They felt the wind on their faces and the sun on their hair. They laughed and shouted with joy.

They got closer and closer to the cloud. But when they touched it, they were surprised. It was not soft and fluffy. It was wet and cold. It made them sneeze and shiver.

"Uh-oh, this is not fun at all!" Lily said. "The cloud is not a pillow. It is made of water!"

"Let's go back down!" Ben said. "I want to play on the ground!"

They let go of their balloons and fell down. But they did not get hurt. They landed on a big, soft pile of hay. They were safe and warm.

They looked at each other and smiled. They learned something new that day. They learned that clouds are not for jumping. They learned that some things are better to look at than to touch.

They hugged each other and said, "We are happy to be twins. We have each other to play with and to learn with. We don't need to fly to the cloud. We have everything we need right here."

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play with toys, draw pictures and read books. One day, Lily found a new pen in her backpack. It was shiny and had many colors. Lily wanted to try it, but Ben was nosy. He wanted to see the pen too.

"Can I have your pen?" Ben asked.

"No, it is mine. I want to draw with it," Lily said.

"Please, let me see it. Just for a moment," Ben begged.

Lily did not want to share. She hid the pen behind her back. Ben tried to grab it, but Lily ran away. She ran to the corner of the room, where there was a big box. She opened the box and went inside. She thought she was safe.

But Ben followed her. He was curious. He wanted to know what was in the box. He opened the box and saw Lily. She was holding the pen. She looked angry.

"Go away, Ben. This is my secret place. You are not allowed here," Lily said.

Ben did not listen. He reached for the pen. Lily tried to stop him, but it was too late. Ben pulled the pen and revealed a surprise. The pen was not a normal pen. It was a magic pen. It could make things appear and disappear. When Ben pulled the pen, he made the box disappear. Lily and Ben were exposed. Everyone in the room saw them. They saw the pen too.

Lily and Ben felt ashamed. They had been selfish and rude. They had not shared the pen or respected each other's privacy. They had made a mess. They said sorry to each other and to their teacher. They learned a lesson. They learned to be kind and generous. They learned to be careful with magic. They decided to share the pen and use it for good. They drew beautiful pictures and made their friends happy. They became better friends.

Sara liked to act. She liked to pretend she was a sailor on a big boat. She had a hat, a coat and a toy wheel. She said, "I am the captain of this ship. I can go anywhere I want. I am independent."

Tommy was her brother. He liked to act too. He liked to pretend he was a pirate. He had a hat, a sword and a toy parrot. He said, "I am the captain of this ship. I can take anything I want. I am independent."

One day, Sara and Tommy both wanted to play with the same boat. They both said, "This is my ship. You go away." They both pulled the boat. They both got angry.

"Stop it!" said Mommy. She came to see what was wrong. She said, "You are both acting silly. You can share the boat. You can be sailors and pirates together. You can be independent and kind."

Sara and Tommy looked at each other. They felt sorry. They said, "Sorry, Mommy. Sorry, brother. Sorry, sister." They hugged and smiled. They decided to play together. They said, "We are the captains of this ship. We can go anywhere we want. We are independent and kind."

Lily loved her cat, Snowy. She liked to cuddle with him and play with him. But one day, Snowy got sick. He did not eat or drink. He only slept and made sad noises. Lily was very worried.

She told her mom, "Mom, Snowy is sick. He needs help."

Mom nodded and said, "You are right, Lily. We need to take him to the veterinarian. The veterinarian is a person who helps animals feel better."

Lily and Mom put Snowy in a basket and drove to the veterinarian's office. There, they met a nice lady who wore a white coat. She smiled and said, "Hello, I am the veterinarian. What is your cat's name?"

Lily said, "His name is Snowy. He is sick. Can you make him better?"

The veterinarian said, "I will try, Lily. First, I need to check him. I will use this spray to make him sleepy. Then, I will look at his ears, his eyes, his mouth, and his tummy. Don't worry, it won't hurt him."

Lily did not like the spray. She thought it was scary. She held Snowy's basket and said, "No, don't spray him. He doesn't like it. He is scared."

The veterinarian said, "I know, Lily. But it is for his own good. The spray will make him calm and relaxed. He won't feel any pain. And when he wakes up, he will feel much better. Trust me, Lily. I am here to help him."

Lily looked at Snowy. He looked very sick. She wanted him to feel better. She nodded and said, "OK, spray him. But please be gentle. And please wake him up soon. I miss him."

The veterinarian said, "I will, Lily. I will be gentle and fast. And I will wake him up as soon as I can. You are a very brave and caring girl, Lily. Snowy is lucky to have you."

She sprayed Snowy with a little bottle. Snowy closed his eyes and fell asleep. The veterinarian took him to another room. Lily and Mom waited in the waiting room. They read some books and played some games. Lily hoped Snowy would be OK.

After a while, the veterinarian came back with Snowy. He was awake and alert. He looked much better. He meowed and licked Lily's face. Lily hugged him and said, "Snowy, you are back. I am so happy. Are you feeling better?"

The veterinarian said, "Yes, he is feeling much better. He had an infection in his ear. I gave him some medicine and cleaned his ear. He will be fine. But you need to give him some more medicine at home for a few days. And you need to keep him warm and cozy."

Lily said, "Thank you, veterinarian. You are very nice. You helped Snowy. I will give him his medicine and keep him warm and cozy. I love him very much."

The veterinarian said, "You are very welcome, Lily. You are a good friend to Snowy. He loves you very much too. Take good care of him. And come back if you need anything."

Lily and Mom thanked the veterinarian and left the office. They drove back home. Lily cuddled with Snowy in the car. He purred and snuggled with her. Lily was very happy. She had her best friend back. And he was feeling better.

He opened the door and walked in. He saw a big cage. Inside the cage, there was a real bear. It was not like the picture. It was not wearing a hat or a bow tie. It was big and brown and furry. It had sharp teeth and claws. It roared at Tom.

Tom and Lily were very scared. They hugged each other and closed their eyes. They hoped someone would come and save them.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with many red and yellow fruits. They wanted to pick some fruits and eat them.

"Look, Lily, those fruits look like candy!" Tom said.

"Let's get some, Tom!" Lily said.

They ran to the tree and tried to reach the fruits. But they were too high for them. They jumped and stretched, but they could not touch them.

"Maybe we need a stick," Tom said.

He looked around and found a long stick. He gave it to Lily and said, "You hold this end, and I hold the other end. We can use it to knock down the fruits."

Lily nodded and held the stick with Tom. They swung the stick at the tree, hoping to hit the fruits. But they missed and hit a big bee nest instead.

Suddenly, many angry bees came out of the nest. They buzzed and flew around Tom and Lily. They stung them on their arms and legs. Tom and Lily screamed and dropped the stick. They ran away from the tree as fast as they could.

"Ow, ow, ow, the bees hurt us!" Tom cried.

"Help, help, help, the bees chase us!" Lily cried.

They ran to their mom, who was sitting on a bench. She saw them and got up. She hugged them and said, "What happened, my sweeties? Why are you crying?"

"Mom, mom, mom, we wanted some candy fruits, but we got bees instead!" Tom said.

"We hit their home with a stick, and they got mad at us!" Lily said.

Mom looked at their red and swollen skin. She felt sorry for them and said, "Oh, you poor things. You should not hit the bee nest. The bees live there and make honey. They do not like it when you bother them. They will sting you to protect themselves."

"We did not know, mom. We were confused. We thought the fruits were candy," Tom said.

"We are sorry, mom. We will not do it again," Lily said.

Mom smiled and said, "It's okay, my loves. You made a mistake, but you learned something. Next time, you can ask me before you pick fruits from a tree. I will tell you which ones are safe and which ones are not. Now, let's go home and put some ice on your stings. And maybe I have some real candy for you in the kitchen."

Tom and Lily nodded and said, "Thank you, mom. We love you."

They hugged mom and walked home with her. They surrendered the stick and the fruits to the bees. They hoped the bees would forgive them and be happy.

The moral of the story is: Listen to your parents and go to bed on time. Eating too much honey is not good for you. Sleeping is good for you.

"Hello, dolphin!" Jill and Ben said. They tried to copy the sounds.

One day, they found a door in the basement that they had never seen before. It was locked, but they saw a key on a shelf. They took the key and opened the door. Inside, they saw a lot of old boxes, books, and clothes. They decided to look for treasures and secrets.

They opened a box and found a shiny necklace with a big red stone. Lila put it on and said, "Look, Ben, I'm a princess!" Ben opened another box and found a lighter with a picture of a dragon. He said, "Look, Lila, I'm a dragon!" He flicked the lighter and made a small fire.

They played with the necklace and the lighter for a while, pretending to be a princess and a dragon. They didn't notice that the fire was getting bigger and bigger, and that it was catching on the books and clothes. They didn't hear the smoke alarm or their mom and dad shouting.

They only realized something was wrong when they saw a fireman arrive at the door. He was wearing a helmet, a coat, and a mask. He said, "Come with me, kids, it's not safe here!" He took them by the hand and led them out of the basement. He said, "You're lucky I got here in time. You could have been hurt by the fire. What were you doing in there?"

Lila and Ben looked at each other and felt ashamed. They knew they had been naughty and careless. They said, "We're sorry, fireman. We were playing with a necklace and a lighter. We didn't mean to start a fire."

The fireman said, "Well, I'm glad you're okay, but you should never play with fire. It's very dangerous and can destroy things and hurt people. And you should never go into places you're not supposed to. You could get lost or trapped. You should always listen to your mom and dad and follow the rules."

Mom and dad said, "We love you too, Lila and Ben. We're happy you're safe. But you have to be more careful and responsible. You can't play with fire or go into the basement. You could have lost everything we have, and more importantly, you could have lost each other."

Lila and Ben said, "We know, mom and dad. We learned our lesson. We don't need fire or treasures to have fun. We have each other, and that's the best thing we have." The moral of the story is: Don't hide in a trash can. It's dirty and dangerous and it can scare your friends. Hide in a safe and clean place and be kind to your friends. And don't play in the park in the evening. Play in the day when it's bright and warm.

Tom is a fisherman. He likes to catch fish in the lake. He has a regular boat, a regular net and a regular hat. He goes to the lake every day.

One day, he sees a big fish in the water. It is shiny and red. Tom wants to catch it. He throws his net at the fish. But the fish is too fast. It swims away.

Tom tries again and again. But the fish is too smart. It dodges the net every time. Tom gets sad. He wants the fish very much.

He sees a little girl on the shore. She has a small rod and a small bucket. She is fishing too. She sees Tom and his net. She smiles at him.

She asks him, "Do you need help, fisherman?" Tom nods. He says, "Yes, please. I want to catch that big fish. But it is too hard."

The girl says, "I can help you. I have a secret. Do you want to know?" Tom says, "Yes, please. Tell me your secret."

The girl says, "You have to be nice to the fish. You have to talk to them. You have to say, 'Hello, fish. You are beautiful. Can I be your friend?' Then they will come to you."

Tom thinks this is silly. He says, "That is not how you fish. You have to use a net or a hook. You have to be quick and strong."

The girl says, "No, you have to be kind and gentle. Try it. You will see."

Tom is curious. He decides to try it. He puts down his net. He picks up his rod. He says to the water, "Hello, fish. You are beautiful. Can I be your friend?"

He waits. He does not see the big fish. He thinks the girl is wrong. He is about to give up.

But then, he feels a tug on his line. He looks. He sees the big fish. It is smiling at him. It says, "Hello, fisherman. You are nice. I want to be your friend."

Tom is amazed. He says, "Hello, fish. You are amazing. I want to be your friend too."

He reels in the fish. He holds it in his hands. He is happy. He says, "Thank you, fish. Thank you, girl. You taught me a new way to fish."

The girl is happy too. She says, "You are welcome, fisherman. You learned a good lesson. Friends are better than food."

Tom agrees. He says, "You are right, girl. Friends are better than food. I will not eat this fish. I will let it go. I will come back to visit it. And you. Can we be friends?"

The girl says, "Yes, we can be friends. I like you, fisherman. You are kind and smart."

When she woke up, Lily felt very light and full of energy. She was so happy that she took a nap because now she could play with her friends for a long time without getting tired. She ran to the park and joined her friends.

But soon, a conflict arose when Lily's friends wanted to play a game she didn't like. Lily didn't know what to do, so she asked her mom for help. Her mom said, "Just tell your friends that you don't want to play that game and suggest a different one." Lily did what her mom said and her friends were happy to play a different game. They all had fun and Lily was glad she took a nap. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to walk on the path in the forest with her mommy. One day, they went on a walk and found a bitter fruit on the ground. 

Lily's mommy said, "Let's pause and rest for a bit." 

Lily asked, "What's that, mommy?" 

"It means we stop walking and take a break," mommy replied. 

Lily picked up the bitter fruit and showed it to her mommy. "Can we eat it?" she asked.

"Yeah, please, mister, don't be mean. We have waited a long time for this. We have joked a lot, too," Anna said.

"OK, OK, I will let you in. But only if you can make me laugh. You say you have joked a lot. So tell me a joke. A good one. If I laugh, you can go in. If I don't, you have to go back," he said.

Tim and Anna looked at each other. They thought hard. They wanted to make the man laugh. They wanted to go to the zoo. They remembered some of the jokes they had heard and told before. They picked one they liked.

"OK, mister, we have a joke for you. Are you ready?" Tim said.

"Yes, I am ready. Let's hear it," the man said.

"OK, here it goes. Why did the chicken cross the road?" Tim asked.

"I don't know. Why did the chicken cross the road?" the man said.

"To get to the other side!" Anna said.

Tim and Anna waited. They hoped the man would laugh. They thought it was a funny joke. They smiled and looked at him.

The man at the gate stared at them. He did not laugh. He did not smile. He did not say anything. He just shook his head.

"That's not a joke. That's an old and silly riddle. That's not funny at all. You can't go in. You have to go back. Your tickets are spoiled and your joke is spoiled, too," he said.

He gave them back their tickets and turned away. He did not care about them. He did not care about the zoo. He did not care about anything.

They looked at their mom. She was also sad and angry. She did not like the man at the gate. She did not like how he treated them. She did not like how he spoiled their day.

She hugged them and said, "Don't worry, my loves. We will find another way to go to the zoo. We will not let this man ruin our day. We will not let him spoil our jokes. We will joke more and laugh more and be happy more. Come on, let's go."

She took their hands and led them away from the gate. She looked for another entrance. She looked for another man. She looked for another chance.

She found one. She found a nice and friendly man who smiled and welcomed them. He looked at their tickets and said, "Wow, these are beautiful tickets. They have pictures of animals on them. You must love animals. You can go in and see them. Have a wonderful day."

He let them in and wished them well. He did not spoil their tickets. He did not spoil their jokes. He did not spoil their day.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toys. They had a castle, a king, a queen, and some knights. They liked to make up stories about them.

"Let's pretend the king is sick and the queen needs to find a cure," Lily said.

"OK, but the cure is very difficult to get. It is in a far away land with many dangers," Ben said.

They moved the toys around the castle and the map. They made the queen ask the knights to help her. They made the knights pass mountains, rivers, and forests. They made some knights fall or get hurt by animals.

"Look, the queen and one knight are almost there. They can see the cure. It is a magic flower," Lily said.

"Yes, but there is a big problem. There is a dragon guarding the flower. It is very angry and breathes fire," Ben said.

They made the dragon roar and chase the queen and the knight. They made the queen and the knight run and hide. They tried to think of a way to get the flower.

"I know, the knight can distract the dragon and the queen can grab the flower," Lily said.

"Good idea, let's do that," Ben said.

They made the knight come out of his hiding place and shout at the dragon. They made the dragon turn and follow the knight. They made the queen sneak behind the dragon and reach for the flower.

But then something bad happened. The dragon saw the queen and swung its tail. It hit the queen and made her fly away. She dropped the flower and it fell into a river. The queen did not get up. She was very hurt.

The knight saw what happened and ran to the queen. He tried to help her, but it was too late. The queen was gone. The knight was very sad. He cried and cried.

The king in the castle waited for the queen. He did not know what happened. He was very sick and lonely. He wished the queen would come back. But she never did. The king died too.

Ben and Lily stopped playing. They looked at their toys. They felt very sad. They did not like this story. They wished they had a different ending.

Tom and Lily were playing in the sandbox. They liked to make things with the sand and the toys. They made a castle, a cake, a car and a treasure. The treasure was a shiny stone that Lily found in the sand. She put it in a small box and buried it under the castle.

"Look, Tom, this is our treasure. It is very pretty and sparkly. We can pretend we are pirates and find it again," Lily said.

Tom nodded. He liked the treasure too. He wanted to hold it and look at it. He waited until Lily was busy making a cake and dug up the treasure. He took it out of the box and put it in his pocket.

Lily finished her cake and looked for the treasure. She could not find it. She dug and dug, but the box was gone. She felt upset. She thought someone had taken her treasure.

"Tom, where is our treasure? Did you see it?" she asked.

Tom felt guilty. He knew he had taken the treasure, but he did not want to tell Lily. He lied and said, "No, I did not see it. Maybe someone else took it. Maybe a bird or a dog or a big kid."

Lily did not believe him. She saw a bulge in his pocket. She knew he had the treasure. She felt angry. She said, "Tom, you are lying. You have the treasure. Give it back to me. It is mine. I found it."

Tom did not want to give it back. He liked the treasure too much. He said, "No, it is mine. I took it. It is my treasure. Go away."

Lily and Tom started to fight. They pulled and pushed and shouted. They did not play nicely. They did not share. They made a big mess in the sandbox. They made their teacher sad. "Please, Sam, let me wear the wig. It will be fun to act like a mean boss and tell you what to do," Tom said.

"No, Tom, I don't want to play that game. The wig is not yours, and it might belong to someone who needs it. And being mean is not fun, it is rude," Sam said.

But Tom did not listen to Sam. He put on the wig and started to act like a mean boss. He ordered Sam to do silly things, like jump on one leg, or bark like a dog, or clean his shoes. Sam did not like it at all. He felt sad and angry.

"Stop it, Tom, you are not a nice friend. You are a mean boss. I don't want to play with you anymore," Sam said.

But Tom did not stop. He laughed and said, "You have to do what I say, or I will fire you. You are a bad worker. You are a silly boy."

Then, something bad happened. The wig fell off Tom's head and landed on the floor. Sam saw that the wig had a tag on it. It said, "Property of Mr. Lee, the principal of the school. Do not touch."

Sam gasped. He knew that Mr. Lee was a very nice and bald man who worked at their school. He also knew that Mr. Lee would be very angry if he saw that Tom had taken his wig and acted like a mean boss.

"Tom, you are in big trouble. This is Mr. Lee's wig. He will be very mad at you. You should not have taken it. You should not have acted like a mean boss. You should have listened to me," Sam said.

But it was too late. Mr. Lee came into the room and saw Tom with his wig. He was very mad. He scolded Tom and took his wig back. He also told Tom's parents what he had done. Tom's parents were very disappointed. They took away his gear and made him say sorry to Sam and Mr. Lee. Tom felt very sorry and ashamed. He wished he had not acted like a mean boss. He wished he had been a nice friend.

The moral of the story is: Do not take things that are not yours. Do not act like a mean boss. Be a nice friend. Listen to good advice.

"See, Lily, your car is fixed. It's not broken anymore. You can play with it again." Max said, as he gave the car back to Lily.

Lily smiled and hugged Max. She was happy that he helped her. She looked at her car and saw that it was still red, but it had some white tape on it.

"Thank you, Max. You are very nice. My car is fixed, but it looks different. It has white stripes on it. It looks like a zebra!" Lily said, as she laughed.

One day, they find a big rock that is shiny and smooth. Tom says, "This is a good rock. I want to keep it." Sue says, "No, this is my rock. I saw it first." They both pull the rock and try to take it away from each other.

A man sees them and comes over. He says, "Hello, children. What are you doing with that rock?" Tom and Sue say, "This is our rock. We found it in the field." The man says, "Do you know what kind of rock this is?" Tom and Sue shake their heads. The man says, "This is a quartz rock. It is very hard and can make sparks if you hit it with another rock. It is also very pretty and can be used to make jewelry or decorations."

Tom and Sue are amazed. They say, "Wow, this is a very special rock. We did not know that." The man says, "Yes, it is. But you know what is more special than a rock? A friend. A friend can help you, share with you, and have fun with you. A rock can only sit there and look nice. If you fight over a rock, you might lose a friend. And that would be very sad."

Tom and Sue think about what the man says. They look at each other and say, "You are right. A friend is more special than a rock. We are sorry for fighting. We can share the rock and play with it together." The man smiles and says, "That is very smart of you. I am glad you are friends again. Here, I have a gift for you. It is a small knife made of quartz. You can use it to cut things or make marks on other rocks. But be careful, it is very sharp. And remember, always be kind and generous to your friends."

Tom and Sue thank the man and take the knife. They hug each other and say, "We are happy to have each other and this rock. We will always be friends and share our things." They run back to the field and play with the rock and the knife. They make sparks, cut grass, and draw pictures on the rocks. They have a lot of fun and learn a lot of things. They are smart and happy children.

"Wow!" Max said. "And this is a map!" He held up a paper with many lines and shapes. "We can go on an adventure!"

They pretended to follow the map, and walked around the room. They bumped into the sofa, the lamp, and the bookshelf. They made loud noises and laughed.

"Shh!" Lily said. "We have to be quiet. Dad is sleeping upstairs."

"Sorry!" Max said. "But this is fun!"

They reached the window, and saw a big tree outside. They saw a bird on a branch, and a squirrel on the trunk.

"Look, there is the treasure!" Lily said. "It is in the tree!"

She threw the wallet out of the window, hoping it would land on the tree. But it missed, and fell on the ground.

"Oh no!" Max said. "We destroyed the wallet!"

They ran to the window, and saw the wallet lying on the grass. It was dirty and torn, and some of the cards and papers were scattered.

They heard Dad coming downstairs. He looked angry.

"Who took my wallet?" He asked. "And why is it on the ground?"

Lily and Max felt scared. They knew they did something bad.

"We are sorry, Dad!" Lily said. "We were playing with the wallet. We did not mean to destroy it."

"We wanted to find the treasure!" Max said. "But we made a mistake."

Dad sighed. He picked up the wallet, and looked at it. It was ruined.

He was very sad, but he saw that Lily and Max were sorry. He decided to be polite.

"I understand that you were curious, and wanted to have fun." He said. "But you should not play with things that are not yours. The wallet is important to me. It has my money, and my ID, and my photos. You could have lost them, or damaged them."

He showed them the cards and papers, and explained what they were. He told them that they were not toys, but tools.

He also told them that they should always ask before they touch something, and that they should be careful and respectful.

He hugged them, and said that he loved them.

Lily and Max felt sorry, and learned a lesson. They said that they loved Dad, and that they would not play with the wallet again.

They asked Dad if they could help him fix the wallet, or buy him a new one.

Dad smiled, and said that they could help him clean it, and that he would keep it as a reminder.

He also said that he would buy them a new toy, as a reward for being polite and honest.

They thanked Dad, and went to clean the wallet.

They were happy, and played with their new toy later.

But she was not clever. She was naughty. She did not know that the magazine belonged to a nice lady who was feeding the ducks. The lady saw Lily take her magazine and was very sad. She called out, "Hey, little girl, that's my magazine! Please give it back!"

Lily heard the lady and felt scared. She knew she did something wrong. She stopped running and turned around. She saw the lady walking towards her. She felt sorry for the lady. She said, "I'm sorry, lady. I like your magazine. But I should not take it. It is yours. Here you go."

The lady took the magazine and smiled. She said, "Thank you, little girl. I'm glad you like my magazine. But you should not steal. Stealing is bad. If you want something, you should ask or save or trade. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She said, "I understand, lady. I'm sorry. I will not steal again. Can we be friends?"

The lady said, "Of course we can be friends. What is your name?"

Lily said, "My name is Lily. What is yours?"

The lady said, "My name is Anna. Do you want to feed the ducks with me?"

Lily said, "Yes, please. That sounds fun."

Anna said, "Come on, then. Let's go. And you can look at my magazine with me, if you like."

Lily said, "Thank you, Anna. You are very nice. I'm glad I met you."

Anna said, "You're welcome, Lily. I'm glad I met you, too."

Sara smiled and nodded. She was happy that Tom apologized and accepted her bike. She was not fearful of him anymore. She said to Tom, "It's okay. I forgive you. We can play together. Do you want to ride my bike?"

Tom smiled and nodded. He was glad that Sara forgave him and shared her bike. He was not afraid of pink anymore. He said to Sara, "Yes, I want to ride your bike. Thank you. You are a good friend."

He wants to find a better crayon, so he looks in his dad's desk again. He sees a shiny thing that looks like a crayon, but it is not. It is a knife and it is very sharp. He does not know what it is, but he wants to try it. He picks it up and tries to draw on the paper, but it does not work. It cuts the paper and it hurts his hand. He drops the knife and cries.

His mom hears him and comes to see what is wrong. She sees the knife and the paper and the blood and she is scared. She hugs Ben and says he is brave and she loves him. She takes him to the doctor, who is nice and patient. He cleans Ben's hand and puts a band-aid on it. He tells Ben not to play with sharp things, because they are dangerous. He gives Ben a sticker and a lollipop and says he is a good boy.

Ben says he is sorry and he will not play with sharp things again. He says he likes crayons better, because they are soft and colorful and they make pretty pictures. He says he loves his mom and the doctor and he wants to go home. He learns a lesson and he is happy.

Lila had a pet fish. She liked to watch him swim in his bowl. He was red and blue and he had a big tail. His name was Sparky.

One night, Lila woke up and saw something strange. Her fish bowl was glowing. She got out of bed and went to see. Sparky was glowing too. He was bright and shiny. He looked happy.

Lila smiled and said, "Hello, Sparky. Why are you glowing?" She touched the bowl and felt it was warm. She thought maybe Sparky was warm too.

Sparky swam to the top of the bowl and made a little sound. He said, "Hello, Lila. I am glowing because I am special. I come from a deep place where it is dark and cold. But sometimes, I can glow and make light. I want to show you how much I love you."

Lila hugged the bowl and said, "I love you too, Sparky. You are special and beautiful. Thank you for glowing for me." She kissed the bowl and put it back on her nightstand. She went back to bed and fell asleep. Sparky kept glowing until the sun came up. He was happy to have Lila as his friend.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a big truck that she liked to drive around. Ben had a small car that he liked to zoom with. They were having fun until Lily saw Ben's car.

"Hey, that's my car!" Lily shouted. "You took it from my room!"

"No, it's mine!" Ben said. "Dad gave it to me for my birthday!"

They both grabbed the car and pulled hard. The car broke in half with a loud snap.

"Look what you did!" Lily cried. "You broke my car! It was expensive!"

"It was not your car!" Ben yelled. "It was mine! And you broke it! You suffer!"

They both started to cry and scream. Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong.

"What's going on here?" Mom asked. "Why are you fighting?"

They both pointed at each other and told their stories. Mom looked at the broken car and sighed.

"Listen, both of you," Mom said. "This car was not yours or Ben's. It was a gift from your uncle. He sent it to both of you to share. He wanted you to be happy and play together. But you were selfish and greedy and broke it. Now you can't play with it at all. How do you think your uncle would feel if he saw this?"

Lily and Ben felt ashamed and sorry. They realized they had been wrong and hurt their uncle's feelings.

"We're sorry, Mom," they said. "We're sorry, uncle."

Mom hugged them and said, "It's okay. I'm glad you understand. But you have to learn to share and be kind. And you have to take care of your toys. They are not just things. They are gifts from people who love you."

Lily and Ben nodded and said, "We will, Mom. We will."

They looked at their truck and their car and decided to play with them together. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They learned their lesson and had fun. Mom smiled and watched them. She was proud of them.

Lila was very happy. She had a new bathrobe. It was soft and pink and had a hood with ears. She liked to wear it after her bath and pretend she was a bunny.

One day, she wanted to show her bathrobe to her friend Sam. She put it on and ran to his house. She knocked on the door and waited.

"Be careful!" Sam said. "Don't drop it!"

But Lila did not hear him. She was too busy playing with the lamp. She lifted it up and down and made it flash. She did not see that the cord was tangled.

Ben and Jen are twins who like to play with their toy cars. They have a big box of cars in different colors and sizes. They like to make races and crashes and noises with their cars.

One day, they find a new car in the box. It is shiny and red and has a button on the top. Ben and Jen wonder what the button does. They decide to try it out.

They put the car on the floor and push the button. The car makes a loud beep and starts to move. But it does not go forward. It goes backward. It is a reverse car!

"Wow, look at that!" Ben says. "The car can go reverse!"

"That is so cool!" Jen says. "Let's see where it goes!"

They follow the car as it goes backward around the room. It goes under the table, behind the sofa, and into the kitchen. It bumps into the trash can and knocks it over. It spills some beans on the floor.

"Oh no, the car made a mess!" Ben says. "We have to stop it!"

They run after the car and try to catch it. But the car is too fast and too smart. It dodges them and goes backward out of the door. It goes down the stairs and into the street.

"Stop, car, stop!" Jen shouts. "You are in trouble!"

But the car does not stop. It goes reverse across the street and into the park. It zooms past the swings, the slide, and the sandbox. It heads toward the pond.

"Look out, car, look out!" Ben warns. "There is water!"

But the car does not look out. It goes reverse into the pond and splashes into the water. It sinks to the bottom and stops.

Ben and Jen run to the edge of the pond and look at the car. They are sad and angry. They want their car back.

"Bad car, bad car!" they say. "You are naughty and wet!"

They see a man with a fishing rod near the pond. He sees them and smiles.

"Hello, kids," he says. "Do you need some help?"

"Yes, please," Ben and Jen say. "Our car is in the pond. Can you get it for us?"

The man nods and casts his line into the water. He waits for a while and then pulls it up. He has caught the car!

"Here you go, kids," he says. "Your car is safe and sound."

He gives them the car and they take it. They are glad and thankful.

"Thank you, mister," they say. "You are nice and kind!"

They dry the car with their shirts and push the button. The car makes a loud beep and starts to move. But it does not go backward. It goes forward. It is a normal car!

"Wow, look at that!" Ben says. "The car can go forward!"

"That is so cool!" Jen says. "Let's play with it!"

They hug the car and run back to their house. They play with their car and their other cars. They have fun and forget about the mess.

The end.

Lily was a shy girl who liked to play with blocks. She liked to build tall structures with different colors and shapes. She was very careful not to knock them down or let anyone touch them. She was proud of her structures and wanted to show them to her mom and dad.

One day, Lily was playing with her blocks in her room when she heard a knock on the door. It was her cousin Max, who came to visit. Max was a loud boy who liked to run and jump and make noise. He saw Lily's structures and wanted to play with them too.

"Can I play with your blocks?" he asked.

Lily did not want to share her blocks. She liked to play by herself and did not like Max's noise. She was afraid he would break her structures or make them fall.

"No, you can't play with my blocks. They are mine. Go away!" she said.

Max did not listen to Lily. He did not mind her words. He ran into her room and grabbed some of her blocks. He threw them in the air and laughed. He knocked down some of her structures and made a mess.

Lily was very angry and sad. She cried and shouted at Max. She tried to get her blocks back, but he was bigger and stronger. He pushed her away and kept playing with her blocks.

Lily ran to her mom and dad and told them what Max did. They came to her room and saw the mess. They scolded Max and made him apologize to Lily. They helped Lily pick up her blocks and fix her structures. They hugged her and told her they were sorry.

Lily felt better and thanked her mom and dad. She forgave Max and decided to give him another chance. She asked him if he wanted to play with her blocks, but only if he was nice and careful. Max agreed and said he was sorry. He learned to mind Lily's words and respect her structures. They played together and had fun. Lily was not so shy anymore and made a new friend.

Lily and Ben were twins who lived in a big house with their wealthy parents. They had many toys and clothes, but they were not happy. They wanted to play with other children, but their parents were always busy or away. They only had a nanny who was very strict and did not let them have fun.

One day, they saw a group of children playing in the park across the street. They looked so happy and free, running and laughing and sharing. Lily and Ben wanted to join them, but they knew their nanny would not let them. They had an idea. They waited until the nanny was in the kitchen, and then they put on their coats and hats and sneaked out of the house.

They ran across the street and approached the children. They said hello and asked if they could play with them. The children were surprised, but they were friendly and welcomed them. They asked Lily and Ben their names and where they lived. Lily and Ben lied and said they lived in a small apartment nearby. They did not want the children to know they were wealthy, because they thought they would not like them.

They played for a long time, and had a lot of fun. They played tag and hide and seek and hopscotch and swings. They shared their snacks and stories and jokes. Lily and Ben felt happy and free, too. They made new friends and forgot about their big house and their strict nanny.

But then they heard a loud voice calling their names. It was their nanny, who had noticed they were gone and had followed them to the park. She was angry and scared, and she grabbed them by their waists and dragged them back to the house. She scolded them and told them they were in big trouble. She said they were not allowed to play with those children, because they were not like them. She said they were dirty and poor and rude, and they would teach them bad things.

Lily and Ben did not understand. They did not think their new friends were dirty or poor or rude. They thought they were nice and fun and kind. They did not think being wealthy made them better than anyone else. They wanted to play with them again, and they did not want to lose them.

They looked at each other and whispered, "We will find a way to see them again. We will not let the nanny stop us. We will be friends with them, no matter what." They smiled and nodded, and hoped their nanny did not hear them. They knew they had a secret to keep, and a plan to make.

One day, Anna went to the library with her mom. She saw a new novel on the shelf. It had a blue cover and a dragon on it. Anna loved dragons. She wanted to read the novel very much. She took it from the shelf and showed it to her mom.

"Can I keep this novel, mom?" Anna asked.

"Sure, honey. But you have to borrow it first. You need a library card for that. Do you have one?" her mom said.

Anna shook her head. She did not have a library card. She felt sad. She did not want to give back the novel.

"Then let's get you one. Come with me to the desk. We'll fill out a form and get you a card. It's easy and fast," her mom said.

Anna followed her mom to the desk. There was a lady behind the desk. She had a big smile and a name tag that said "Miss Lily". She looked nice, but Anna felt shy. She hid behind her mom and held the novel tight.

"Hello, there. What's your name?" Miss Lily asked.

Anna did not answer. She looked at the floor.

"This is Anna. She wants to borrow this novel. But she doesn't have a library card yet. Can you help us?" her mom said.

"Of course. I'm happy to help. Anna, this novel looks very interesting. Do you like dragons?" Miss Lily said.

Anna nodded. She liked dragons a lot. She peeked at Miss Lily. She saw that Miss Lily had a pin on her shirt. It was a dragon pin. It was shiny and green.

"I like dragons, too. See, I have a dragon pin. Do you want to see it?" Miss Lily said.

Anna nodded again. She wanted to see the pin. She stepped out from behind her mom and went closer to Miss Lily. She touched the pin gently. It felt smooth and cool.

"It's beautiful. Where did you get it?" Anna asked.

"I got it from a friend. He gave it to me as a gift. He likes dragons, too. He writes novels about dragons. Maybe you've read some of his novels. His name is Ben," Miss Lily said.

Anna gasped. She looked at the novel in her hand. She saw the name on the cover. It was Ben. He was the author of the novel. He was Miss Lily's friend.

"Wow. You know Ben? He wrote this novel? He's amazing. I want to read all his novels. Can I keep this one?" Anna asked.

"You can borrow it, Anna. You can keep it for two weeks. Then you have to bring it back. But you can borrow another one. Ben has written many novels. They are all in the library. You can read them all. But first, you need a library card. Do you want one?" Miss Lily asked.

"Yes, please. I want a library card. I want to read all the novels. Thank you, Miss Lily. You're very nice. And so is Ben. And so are dragons," Anna said.

Miss Lily smiled. She gave Anna a form and a pen. She helped Anna fill out the form. She took a picture of Anna and printed a card. She gave the card to Anna.

"Here you go, Anna. This is your library card. You can use it to borrow any book you want. Just remember to bring them back on time. And enjoy the novel. I hope you like it," Miss Lily said.

Anna hugged the novel and the card. She was very happy. She thanked Miss Lily and her mom. She ran to the door. She wanted to go home and read the novel. She wanted to meet the dragon and the other characters. She wanted to go on an adventure with them.

She did not feel shy anymore. She felt excited and curious. She loved novels. Novels were the best.

Anna does not answer. She is too busy reading.

Her mom comes upstairs. She sees Anna on her bed with the book. She smiles.

"Anna, you are a good reader. I am proud of you. But you need to eat something. You must be hungry," her mom says.

Anna looks up. She sees her mom. She feels a little guilty.

"Sorry, mom. I did not hear you. I was reading this book. It is very good. Can I finish it later?" Anna says.

Her mom nods.

"Of course, honey. You can finish it later. But you need to ask me first before you borrow a book from my bookshelf. That is my book. I was going to read it too," her mom says.

Anna gasps.

"Oh, I did not know. I thought it was mine. I am sorry, mom. I did not mean to take your book. Can I borrow it, please?" Anna says.

Her mom smiles.

"Sure, you can borrow it. But you have to promise to take good care of it and return it when you are done. And you have to tell me what you think of the story. Deal?" her mom says.

Anna nods.

"Deal. Thank you, mom. You are the best. Can we read it together?" Anna says.

Her mom hugs her.

"I would love that. But first, let's go downstairs and have some yummy lunch. Then we can read it together. Come on, let's go," her mom says.

Anna puts the book on her pillow. She follows her mom downstairs. She is happy. She loves books. And she loves her mom.

The elderly man smiled and said, "I'm just enjoying the sunshine. What about you, little one?"

"I'm playing!" Jack exclaimed. "Do you want to play with me?"

The elderly man chuckled and said, "I'm a bit too old for that, but I appreciate the offer. Say, have you ever heard the saying 'sticks and stones may break my bones, but words will never hurt me'?"

Jack shook his head. "No, what does that mean?"

"It means that sometimes people say mean things to us, but we shouldn't let it hurt us. We should be strong and not let their words shoot us down."

Jack thought about this for a moment and then smiled. "I get it now! Thank you for telling me that."

The elderly man nodded. "Remember, it's important to be kind to others and not say mean things. You never know how your words might affect someone."

From then on, Jack made sure to always be kind to others and not let mean words shoot him down.

So, they bought the box and Timmy made a big fort out of it. He was so happy and cheerful playing in his new fort. Then, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy was sad because he didn't have any toys to play with. Timmy saw that Billy was sad and said, "Don't be sad, I have an idea! Let's play in my new fort together!" Billy was so happy and cheerful too.

The moral of the story is that sharing is caring. When we share our things with others, we can make them happy too.

One sunny day, Timmy went to the park with his mom. He saw a big tree and wanted to climb it. "Mommy, can I climb the tree?" Timmy asked. "Yes, but be careful," his mom replied.

Timmy started to climb the tree. He climbed higher and higher until he reached the top. He felt like a superhero with his red cap on his head. "Look, Mommy! I'm on top of the world!" Timmy shouted.

His mom smiled and said, "You did a great job, Timmy. You're so dependable." Timmy felt proud of himself and couldn't wait to climb more trees in the future.

Lily's mommy came into the room and said, "Lily, we need to test the window to make sure it's safe. Can you help me?" Lily didn't know what "test" meant, but she nodded her head and followed her mommy.

They went outside and Lily's mommy pushed on the window. It didn't move! "Great job, Lily! The window is safe," her mommy said. Lily smiled and felt proud that she helped.

Later that day, Lily heard a loud noise outside. She looked out the window and saw that the pink bird was stuck in a tree. "Mommy, the pink bird needs help!" she said. They ran outside and Lily's mommy climbed the tree to save the bird.

Lily was happy that the window was safe and that she helped save the pink bird. She knew that she was a good helper.

But when it was time for dinner, Lily's mom took out the soup from the refrigerator and tasted it. She realized that she had put too much spice in it and it was too spicy for Lily to eat. Lily was disappointed and sad.

Her mom explained to her that sometimes we get excited about something, but it doesn't always turn out the way we want it to. We have to be patient and wait for the right time. Next time, her mom promised to make a less spicy soup for Lily to enjoy.

As they were playing, Lily's mommy noticed a fragile branch hanging over their heads. "Be careful, Lily," she warned. "That branch might fall if we touch it."

Lily didn't listen and reached up to grab the branch. Suddenly, she heard a loud crack and the branch started to twist. "Mommy, help!" she cried.

Mommy quickly grabbed Lily and pulled her away just as the branch fell. "I told you to be careful," she said. "You never know what might happen."

From that day on, Lily always listened to her mommy's warnings and never touched anything that looked fragile or could twist.

"There, all done," Anna said, smiling. "The lion has a new lung. He will be much better now. He will wake up soon and thank us."
