Lily was a little girl who liked to explore. She saw many things in her yard, like flowers, bugs, and birds. One day, she saw a big, black cat with green eyes. The cat looked at her and ran away. Lily wanted to see where the cat went, so she followed it.

The cat ran across the street, into the woods, and under a fence. Lily did not stop. She wanted to catch the cat and pet it. She did not see the cars, the thorns, or the sign that said "Keep Out". She only saw the cat.

"Meow!" The cat said, as it jumped over a pile of trash. Lily tried to jump too, but she tripped and fell. She scraped her knee and got dirt on her dress. She started to cry.

"Hey, what are you doing here?" A voice said. Lily looked up and saw a boy. He was older than her and wore a hat and a jacket. He had a stick in his hand. He looked angry.

"I-I was following the cat," Lily said, pointing at the black cat. The cat hissed and ran away.

"Well, you shouldn't be here. This is my place. And you made a mess. You're in trouble, little girl," the boy said. He raised his stick and moved closer to Lily.

Lily was scared. She did not know the boy or his place. She wished she had stayed in her yard. She wished she had listened to her mom, who always told her not to follow unknown things.

"Stop! Leave her alone!" Another voice said. Lily saw another boy. He was younger than the first boy and wore a red shirt and jeans. He had a dog with him. The dog barked at the first boy.

"Who are you?" The first boy said, lowering his stick.

"I'm Sam. I live in the house next to the woods. And this is my dog, Spot. Who are you?" The second boy said.

"I'm Tom. I live in the house behind the fence. And this is my place. And she," he pointed at Lily, "is a trespasser."

"No, she's not. She's just a little girl who got lost. She didn't mean to cause any trouble. She was following the cat. Can't you see she's hurt and scared?" Sam said.

Tom looked at Lily. He saw her tears, her scrape, and her dirt. He felt a little sorry for her.

"Fine. But she has to go. And she can't come back. And neither can you or your dog," Tom said.

"OK. Come on, Lily. Let's go. Spot will protect us," Sam said. He helped Lily stand up and gave her his hand. Lily took it and smiled. She was glad Sam was there. He was kind and brave.

They walked back to the street, where Lily's mom was waiting. She had heard Lily's cry and came looking for her. She hugged Lily and thanked Sam. She was angry at Tom, but she did not say anything. She took Lily home and cleaned her wound and dress. She also gave her a hug and a cookie.

Lily learned a lesson that day. She learned that following unknown things can lead to trouble. She learned that some people are mean and some are nice. She learned that she should always listen to her mom and stay safe. She also learned that she had a new friend, Sam, who liked to explore too. But they agreed to only explore in their yards, where they knew the things and the people. And they always asked their moms first.

They heard footsteps outside. It was their dad. He heard their cries and came to the barn. He opened the door and saw them and the horse.

"What are you doing here?" he asked. "This is not a safe place to play. This horse is not friendly. He could hurt you."

He took them by the hand and led them out of the barn. He hugged them and said, "I'm glad you are OK. But you should never go inside the barn without me. It is dangerous. Do you understand?"

"Yes, dad, we understand," said Lily and Tom. "We are sorry. We won't do it again."

They learned their lesson. They never opened the barn door again. They played with the other animals that were nice and gentle. They had fun on the farm.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise from the kitchen. They jumped off the armchair and ran to see what it was. They saw a big rat running away with a piece of bread. They screamed and chased the rat, but they could not catch it. They forgot about the armchair.

Lena and Tom were friends. They liked to play with toys and books. One day, they found a big book with many pictures. It was a story book.

"Let's read the story book!" Lena said. "It looks lively and fun!"

"OK!" Tom said. "But we have to be careful. The book is old and torn. We don't want to break it."

They opened the book and saw many stories. There were stories about animals, fairies, pirates, and more. They picked a story about a princess and a dragon. They started to read.

The princess was brave and smart. She wanted to save her kingdom from the dragon. The dragon was big and mean. He wanted to burn everything with his fire. The princess had a plan. She spread honey on a big rock. She hid behind the rock and waited for the dragon.

The dragon smelled the honey. He flew to the rock and licked it. The honey was sticky and sweet. The dragon liked it. He licked more and more. He did not see the princess.

The princess jumped out from behind the rock. She had a sword. She ran to the dragon and stabbed him in the heart. The dragon roared and fell. The princess had killed the dragon. She saved her kingdom. She was happy.

Lena and Tom clapped and cheered. They liked the story. They liked the princess. They wanted to read more stories.

They turned the page. But they turned it too hard. The page ripped. The book ripped. The stories ripped.

Lena and Tom gasped. They were scared. They had broken the book. They had ruined the stories.

They heard a voice. It was Lena's mom. She was angry.

"What have you done?" she yelled. "You have destroyed the book! It was a special book! It was my grandma's book! It was very old and precious! How could you be so careless and naughty?"

Lena and Tom cried. They were sorry. They did not mean to break the book. They did not know it was special. They just wanted to read the stories.

But it was too late. The book was gone. The stories were gone. Lena's mom was mad. She took the book and threw it in the trash. She sent Lena and Tom to their rooms. She did not let them play together anymore.

Lena and Tom were sad. They lost the book. They lost the stories. They lost their friend. It was a bad ending.

Lily was playing with her dolls in her room. She liked to dress them up and make them talk. She had a big dollhouse with many rooms. She pretended that the dolls lived there and had fun.

She heard her mom call her name. "Lily, it's time for dinner. Come to the kitchen, please." Lily put her dolls down and ran to the door. She was hungry and wanted to eat.

But on the way, she saw something that made her stop. It was the bathroom. The door was open and she could see inside. It was very dirty. There was water on the floor, soap on the sink, and towels on the toilet. Lily felt curious. She wanted to see what was in the bathroom.

She walked in and looked around. She saw a big bottle of shampoo on the shelf. It was pink and shiny. Lily liked pink. She reached for the bottle and tried to open it. But it was hard to open. She twisted and pulled and shook the bottle. She felt frustrated.

Suddenly, the bottle popped open and shampoo squirted out. It went all over Lily's face, hair, and clothes. It also went on the walls, the mirror, and the shower curtain. Lily felt shocked. She dropped the bottle and screamed. "Mommy, help!"

Her mom heard her scream and ran to the bathroom. She saw Lily covered in shampoo and the mess in the bathroom. She felt angry and worried. She grabbed a towel and wiped Lily's face. "Lily, what did you do? You made a big mess. You shouldn't touch things that are not yours. You could have hurt yourself. You are very dirty. You need a bath right now."

Lily felt sorry and scared. She didn't mean to make a mess. She just wanted to see the shampoo. She looked at her mom and said, "I'm sorry, mommy. I was curious. I won't do it again. Please don't be mad at me."

Her mom sighed and hugged Lily. She felt love and forgiveness. She said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm not mad at you. I'm glad you're not hurt. But you need to be careful and listen to me. Now let's clean up this mess and get you a bath. Then we can have dinner."

Lily nodded and smiled. She felt happy and relieved. She said, "Okay, mommy. Thank you. I love you."

They cleaned up the bathroom and gave Lily a bath. Then they went to the kitchen and had dinner. Lily felt full and sleepy. She said goodnight to her mom and went to her room. She picked up her dolls and put them in the dollhouse. She said, "Goodnight, dolls. I hope you had a good day. I had a very dirty day. But it's okay. Mommy loves me. And I love mommy."

She got into her bed and closed her eyes. She felt cozy and warm. She fell asleep and dreamed of pink shampoo.

Tom and Lily were playing with paper. They liked to fold the paper and make different shapes. Tom made a hat and put it on his head. Lily made a boat and put it in a bowl of water.

"Look, I have a hat!" Tom said. "I am a king!"

"Look, I have a boat!" Lily said. "I am a sailor!"

They were having fun with their paper shapes. But they were also hungry. They wanted some cheese for a snack.

They went to the kitchen and saw their mom. She was busy making dinner. She had a lot of pots and pans on the stove.

"Mom, can we have some cheese?" Tom asked.

"Mom, can we have some cheese?" Lily asked.

Mom smiled and said, "Of course, you can have some cheese. But you have to wait a minute. I have to finish cooking."

Tom and Lily waited for a minute. They looked at the cheese on the counter. It looked yummy. They wanted to eat it now.

"Mom, can we have some cheese now?" Tom asked.

"Mom, can we have some cheese now?" Lily asked.

Mom said, "Not yet, my loves. I have to cut the cheese first. It is too big for you to eat."

Tom and Lily waited for another minute. They looked at the cheese again. It looked even yummier. They wanted to eat it very much.

"Mom, can we have some cheese now?" Tom asked.

"Mom, can we have some cheese now?" Lily asked.

Mom said, "Yes, you can have some cheese now. Here you go. Be careful, it is a little bit hot."

Mom gave Tom and Lily each a slice of cheese. They took a bite and said, "Mmm, this is good cheese. Thank you, mom."

They ate their cheese and felt happy. They gave mom a hug and a kiss. Then they went back to their paper shapes. They folded some more paper and made some more fun things. They had a good day.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, it is very cold. Lily has a long coat. Ben has a short coat.

"Ben, are you cold?" Lily asks.

"Yes, I am cold. My coat is too short," Ben says.

Lily feels sorry for Ben. She has an idea. She takes off her long coat and wraps it around Ben.

"Here, you can share my coat. Now we are both warm," Lily says.

Ben smiles. He likes Lily. He gives her a kiss on the cheek.

"Thank you, Lily. You are very nice. I like you," Ben says.

Lily blushes. She likes Ben too. She gives him a kiss back.

"You are welcome, Ben. I like you too," Lily says.

They hug and giggle. They are happy. They play in the park with the long coat. They are the best friends.

Tom and Mia are friends who like to look at the stars. They have a big book with pictures of planets and stars. They want to learn more about them.

One night, they go outside with a flashlight and the book. They find a spot on the grass and open the book. They point at the pictures and question each other.

"What is this planet?" Tom asks, pointing at a red one.

"That is Mars. It is very far and very cold. No one lives there," Mia answers.

"What is this planet?" Mia asks, pointing at a blue one.

"That is Earth. It is our home. It is very cool and has many animals and plants," Tom answers.

They keep questioning and answering until they see a bright light in the sky. It is a shooting star. They get excited and make a wish.

"I wish we could go to Mars and see if it is really cold," Tom wishes.

"I wish we could go to Earth and see if it is really cool," Mia wishes.

They close their eyes and wait for their wishes to come true. But something goes wrong. The shooting star is not a star. It is a big rock that is falling from the sky. It is very fast and very hot. It hits the ground near them and makes a loud boom. It makes a big hole and a big fire. Tom and Mia are scared and hurt. They cry and scream for help. But no one hears them. No one comes. They are alone and in pain. Their wishes do not come true. They are on the wrong planet. The end.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big event in the park. There are many people, balloons, and games. Lily and Tom want to join the event.

They run to the event and see a lady with a microphone. She is speaking to the people. She says, "Welcome to the clean-up event! We are here to make the park clean and beautiful. Who wants to help us?"

Lily and Tom raise their hands. They want to help. The lady gives them gloves and bags. She says, "Thank you, Lily and Tom. You are very kind. You can pick up the trash and put it in the bags. Then, you can get a prize."

Lily and Tom are happy. They start to pick up the trash. They see cans, bottles, wrappers, and papers. They put them in the bags. They work hard and fast. They fill up many bags.

When they are done, they go back to the lady. She smiles and says, "Wow, Lily and Tom, you did a great job! You made the park clean and beautiful. You are very good helpers. Here is your prize. You can choose a balloon or a sticker."

Lily and Tom are very happy. They choose a balloon and a sticker. They say, "Thank you, lady. We had fun. We like to help. We like to make the park clean and beautiful."

The lady says, "You are welcome, Lily and Tom. You are very smart and nice. You learned a good lesson today. The lesson is: helping others is fun and rewarding. Do you know what rewarding means?"

Lily and Tom nod. They say, "Yes, we know. Rewarding means we get something good for doing something good. Like a balloon or a sticker. Or a smile or a hug."

The lady says, "That's right, Lily and Tom. You are very wise. I hope you always remember this lesson. And I hope you always keep the park clean and beautiful. Thank you for joining the clean-up event. Have a nice day."

Lily and Tom say, "Thank you, lady. Have a nice day, too." They wave goodbye and go home. They are proud of themselves. They learned a good lesson. They helped others. They made the park clean and beautiful. They had fun. They got a prize. They are happy. The end.

Anna was fearful of the dark. She did not like to sleep in her bed alone. She wanted to bring her teddy bear with her, but she left it in the living room. She was too scared to go and get it.

She heard a noise outside her door. She thought it was a monster. She hid under her blanket and cried. She wished her mom or dad would come and help her.

She heard the door open. She saw a shadow on the wall. She screamed. But it was not a monster. It was her dad. He came to check on her.

"Anna, what's wrong?" he asked. He turned on the light and saw her tears.

"I'm scared, daddy. I want my teddy bear. But I left it in the living room. Can you bring it to me?" she sobbed.

"Of course, sweetie. I'll be right back. Don't be afraid. I'm here." he said. He kissed her forehead and went to get her teddy bear.

He came back with the teddy bear and gave it to her. She hugged it and smiled. She felt better.

"Thank you, daddy. I love you." she said.

"I love you too, Anna. Now, try to sleep. I'll be in the next room. If you need me, just call me." he said. He tucked her in and turned off the light.

He left the door ajar. He heard her whisper to her teddy bear.

"Good night, teddy. You're my best friend. You make me brave." she said.

She closed her eyes and fell asleep. She was not fearful anymore.

One day, they go to the park with Mom. They see a big pond with ducks and fish. Mia wants to feed the ducks. She has some bread in her bag. Ben wants to catch the fish. He has a net in his hand.

They run to the pond. Mia throws some bread to the ducks. The ducks come closer and quack. Mia is happy. Ben tries to catch the fish with his net. The fish swim away and splash. Ben is frustrated.

"Stop throwing bread!" Ben says to Mia. "You scare the fish!"

"No, you stop catching fish!" Mia says to Ben. "You hurt the fish!"

They start to argue. They yell and push each other. Mom hears them and comes to the pond. She is angry.

"What are you doing?" Mom says to Mia and Ben. "You are not nice to each other or to nature!"

Mia and Ben feel sorry. They say sorry to Mom and to each other. They say sorry to the ducks and the fish. They hug and make up.

They decide to share the bread and the net. They feed the ducks and watch the fish. They enjoy nature and have fun. They do not scream or fight anymore. Mom is proud of them.

Mom heard them and ran to them. She picked them up and carried them away from the dog. She was not happy. She looked at their boots and saw that they were ugly and wet and muddy.

"Let's go, Tom!" Sara said. "It will be fun!"

The duck quacked loudly and flapped its wings. It surprised Sara and Tom. They turned around and saw the duck. They were scared. The duck looked mean.

"Go away, duck!" Sara said. "This is our puddle!"

"No, it is mine!" the duck said. "You are noisy and rude!"

"Look, Lily, I have an ant!" Tim said.

Lily looked at the ant and smiled. She liked ants. They were small and fast and had many legs.

"Can I hold it?" Lily asked.

The ant did not answer. It did not like being held. It wanted to go back to its home. It was grumpy.

The ant bit Lily's finger. Lily yelped and dropped the ant.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily cried. "The ant bit me! It hurt!"

Tim ran to Lily and hugged her. He felt sorry for her.

"I'm sorry, Lily," Tim said. "The ant was grumpy. It did not want to play with us. Maybe it was hungry or scared."

Lily sniffed and rubbed her finger. She was sad and angry.

"Bad ant," Lily said. "It was mean. I don't like ants anymore."

Tim shook his head and smiled.

Tom and Lily are twins. They like to play outside in the garden. They are very intelligent. They know many things about animals, plants and stars.

One day, they see dark clouds in the sky. They hear a loud noise. It is thunder. They see a bright flash. It is lightning.

"Wow, look at that!" Tom says. "What is lightning?"

Lily thinks for a moment. She remembers what their mom told them. "Lightning is a big spark of electricity. It comes from the clouds when they are angry."

"Why are the clouds angry?" Tom asks.

Peter frowned. He wanted to stroke the goat but it kept running away whenever he approached.

"Come over here and watch," said Mum. She pointed at something in the distance.

Peter gasped as he saw a brightly-coloured rainbow spinning in the sky. It moved around, glowing and glistening in the air.

"Wow!" Peter shouted, jumping up and down. "What is it?"

Mum chuckled. "It's a display for us," she said. "The goat is shy, so it's giving us a show."

Peter smiled and clapped his hands. He never knew that such a shy animal could be so special.

Tom heard Mom and smiled. He ran to her and hugged her. He said, "Thank you, Mom! I won the race! I'm proud of me too!"

Lily heard Mom and looked at her. She saw Mom's smile and heard her words. She felt a little better. She walked to Mom and hugged her too. She said, "Thank you, Mom. I lost the race. But I tried my best. I'm proud of me too."

Lily and Tom were playing in the yard. They saw a big pile of leaves and ran to jump on it. They had fun throwing leaves in the air and hiding under them.

But then Lily smelled something bad. She lifted a leaf and saw a brown and green apple. It was soft and had holes in it. It was rotting.

"Yuck!" Lily said. "This apple is rot. It makes my nose hurt."

Tom came to see. He poked the apple with a stick. He saw a worm crawling out of it. He was not scared. He was curious.

"Look, Lily, a worm!" Tom said. "It likes the rot apple. Maybe it is its home."

Lily did not like the worm. She thought it was gross. She threw the leaf back on the apple and ran away.

Tom followed her. He saw a shiny thing in the grass. He picked it up. It was a metal ring. It was iron.

"Wow, Lily, look what I found!" Tom said. "It is iron. It is hard and cold. Maybe it is a treasure."

Lily came to see. She liked the iron ring. She put it on her finger. It was too big for her. It slid down to her wrist.

"It is a bracelet!" Lily said. "It is pretty. Can I keep it?"

Tom nodded. He was nice. He let Lily have the iron ring.

They played with the ring for a while. They pretended it was a magic ring that could do anything. They made wishes and told stories.

But then Lily felt funny. She felt dizzy. Her head was spinning. She felt sick.

"Lily, are you okay?" Tom asked. He saw that Lily was pale and sweaty. He was worried.

Lily shook her head. She felt worse. She took off the iron ring and threw it away.

"I don't like the iron ring," Lily said. "It makes me dizzy. It is bad."

Tom hugged Lily. He was sorry. He did not know the iron ring was bad. He thought it was a treasure.

"Let's go inside," Tom said. "Maybe Mom can help you. Maybe you need some water and a hug."

Lily nodded. She wanted to go inside. She wanted to feel better.

They left the yard. They left the rot apple and the iron ring behind. They did not want to play with them anymore. They learned that some things are not good to play with.

He rides close to Lily and grabs her purse. He pulls it out of the basket. Lily is scared and angry.

Then, Anna takes a doll with long hair and says, "This is me. I have long hair and a pink dress." Ben takes a doll with short hair and says, "This is me. I have short hair and a blue shirt." They put the dolls on top of the blocks.

But then, they disagree. Anna says, "Your mom is too small. She should be bigger than your dad." Ben says, "Your dad is too big. He should be smaller than your mom." They start to argue and pull the blocks and dolls.

"Stop it!" says Anna. "You are ruining our image!" "No, you stop it!" says Ben. "You are making it wrong!" They get angry and sad. They do not want to play with each other anymore.

But then, they remember. They are friends. They are loyal to each other. They do not want to hurt each other. They say sorry and hug. They say, "We can make our image different. We can make it how we like. We can share our blocks and dolls. We can have fun together." They smile and play again. They are happy.

Tom loves trains. He has many trains in his room. He plays with them every day. He makes them go fast and slow, and he makes them stop and go.

One day, Tom finds a train that does not work. He tries to make it go, but it does not move. He tries to make it sound, but it does not beep. He is sad. He wants to fix his train.

He asks his mom for help. "Mom, can you fix my train?" he says. "It is broken. It does not go or beep."

Mom looks at the train. She sees that the battery is out. She says, "I can fix your train, Tom. We need a new battery. Do you know where the batteries are?"

Tom thinks. He remembers that he saw some batteries in the kitchen. He says, "Yes, Mom. The batteries are in the kitchen. In the drawer. Can we get one?"

Mom says, "Yes, Tom. Let's go to the kitchen. You can help me find a battery."

Tom and Mom go to the kitchen. Tom is alert. He looks in the drawer. He sees many batteries. He picks one that is the same size as the one in his train. He says, "Mom, I found a battery. Is this the right one?"

Mom says, "Yes, Tom. That is the right one. Good job. Now, let's go back to your room and fix your train."

Tom and Mom go back to Tom's room. Mom puts the new battery in the train. She turns it on. The train moves and beeps. Tom is happy. He says, "Thank you, Mom. You fixed my train. Now I can play with it again."

Mom says, "You're welcome, Tom. I'm glad you love your train. Have fun playing with it. But remember to be careful with the batteries. They can be dangerous if you swallow them or put them in your mouth."

Tom says, "I know, Mom. I will be careful. I will not put them in my mouth. I will only put them in my train."

Tom hugs Mom. He says, "I love you, Mom. You are the best."

Mom hugs Tom. She says, "I love you too, Tom. You are the best too."

One day, they see a big boy in the park. He has a black football with yellow stripes. He name it Stripe. He says, "My football is better than yours. It is bigger and faster. You have a baby football. Give it to me."

Tom and Sam are scared. They do not want to give their football to the big boy. They say, "No, this is our football. We like it. It is not a baby football. It is Star. Go away."

The big boy is angry. He tries to take their football. He kicks it hard. It flies away. It lands in a bush. The bush has thorns. The thorns make holes in the football. The air comes out. The football is flat.

Tom and Sam are sad. They run to the bush. They see their football. It is not red and white anymore. It is brown and green. It is not round and bouncy anymore. It is flat and soft. It is not Star anymore. It is nothing.

The big boy laughs. He says, "Ha ha, your football is broken. It is a bad football. My football is still good. It is Stripe. I win."

Tom and Sam are angry. They do not like the big boy. He is mean and rude. He is not a friend. He is a bully. They say, "You are a bad boy. You are not nice. You are bitter. You do not win. You lose. We do not want to play with you. Go away."

They pick up their football. They hug it. They say, "We still love you, Star. You are our football. You are not nothing. You are something. You are our friend."

Anna liked to draw pictures with her crayons. She had many colors, but her favorite was red. She used red for flowers, apples, hearts, and anything else she liked. One day, she wanted to draw a picture for her grandma, who lived far away. She asked her mom for an envelope to put the picture in.

"Mom, can I have an envelope, please?" she said.

"Sure, honey, here you go," her mom said, and gave her a big white envelope. "What are you going to draw?"

"I'm going to draw a big red heart for grandma, and write 'I love you' on it," Anna said.

"That's very sweet of you, Anna. Grandma will be very happy to get your picture," her mom said.

Anna took the envelope and her crayons and went to her room. She drew a big red heart on a piece of paper, and wrote 'I love you' with her best letters. She was very proud of her picture. She put it in the envelope and sealed it. She wrote 'Grandma' on the front, and asked her mom for a stamp.

"Mom, can I have a stamp, please?" she said.

"Sure, honey, here you go," her mom said, and gave her a small sticker with a picture of a bird on it. "This is a stamp. You stick it on the envelope, and then we can mail it to grandma."

"Thank you, mom," Anna said, and stuck the stamp on the envelope. She was very excited to mail her picture to grandma.

She ran to the door, where her dad was waiting for her. He was going to take her to the park.

"Hi, Anna, are you ready to go?" he said.

"Yes, dad, but first I want to mail this to grandma," she said, and showed him the envelope.

"That's very nice of you, Anna. Let's go to the mailbox, then," he said.

They walked to the mailbox, which was a big blue box on the street. Anna saw a boy there, who was holding a weird envelope. It was purple and had stars and glitter on it. He looked sad.

"Hi, what's your name?" Anna said to the boy.

"I'm Ben," he said.

"What's that?" Anna said, pointing to his envelope.

"It's a letter for my friend, Lily. She moved away, and I miss her. But I don't have a stamp, and I can't mail it," he said.

Anna felt sorry for him. She remembered how she felt when her grandma moved away, and how happy she was to get her letters. She had an idea.

"Ben, do you want to lend my stamp?" she said.

"Really? You would do that for me?" he said.

"Yes, I have another one at home. You can have this one. Then you can mail your letter to Lily," she said.

"Thank you, Anna, you are very kind. Here, you can have this sticker. It's a star. Lily gave it to me. I want you to have it," he said, and gave her a shiny sticker.

"Thank you, Ben, it's very pretty. I like stars," she said.

They smiled at each other, and swapped their envelopes. They put them in the mailbox, and heard them drop inside.

"Bye, Ben, I hope Lily likes your letter," Anna said.

"Bye, Anna, I hope grandma likes your picture," Ben said.

They waved goodbye, and went their ways. Anna ran to her dad, who hugged her.

"Who was that, Anna?" he said.

"That was Ben. He was my new friend. I lent him my stamp, and he gave me a sticker. He was very nice," she said.

"That was very nice of you, Anna. You made his day. And I'm sure grandma will love your picture, even without the stamp. You are a very good girl," he said.

They went to the park, and had a lot of fun. Anna played on the swings, the slide, and the sandbox. She put her sticker on her shirt, and showed it to everyone. She was very happy. She knew that grandma and Lily would be happy, too, when they got their letters. She thought that lending and sharing were good things to do. She hoped to see Ben again, and maybe lend him something else. She liked making new friends.

Lily liked olives. She liked the green ones and the black ones. She liked them on pizza and in salad. She liked them mild and salty.

One day, Lily went to the market with her mom. She saw a big jar of olives. She wanted to try them. She asked her mom, "Can I have some olives, please?"

Her mom said, "Sure, honey. But these are spicy olives. They are not mild. They might be too hot for you."

Lily said, "I don't mind. I like all olives. Please, please, please."

Her mom said, "Okay, but only one. And have some water ready."

Lily took an olive from the jar. She put it in her mouth. She bit it. She felt a fire in her tongue. She spit it out. She cried, "Ow, ow, ow! This olive is bad! It hurts!"

Her mom gave her some water. She hugged her. She said, "I'm sorry, sweetie. You were brave to try it. But not all olives are the same. Some are mild and some are spicy. Next time, we will find some mild olives for you."

Lily nodded. She drank some water. She said, "I still like olives. But only mild ones. Spicy ones are not for me."

But then, something happened. The hose made a big splash. It sprayed water on the truck. It sprayed water on the man. It sprayed water on Ben and Lily. They were wet. They were shocked. They dropped the hose.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park with their mom. They liked to run, swing, slide and climb. They were very happy and obedient. They listened to their mom when she said to stay close and not go too far.

But then, a big, bad mosquito came and buzzed around them. It wanted to bite them and make them itch. Anna and Ben were scared and tried to swat it away. But the mosquito was fast and sneaky. It landed on Ben's nose and bit him hard. Ben cried out loud and rubbed his nose.

"Ow, ow, ow! Mom, mom, mom! The mosquito bit me!" he shouted.

Mom heard him and ran to him. She hugged him and checked his nose. She saw a small red bump and kissed it gently.

"Shh, shh, shh. It's okay, Ben. It's just a mosquito bite. It will go away soon. You are very brave," she said.

Anna saw her brother crying and felt sorry for him. She also felt a little embarrassed. She thought the mosquito was silly and mean. She wanted to make Ben feel better. She had an idea.

She ran to the slide and climbed up. She looked at the mosquito, who was still flying around. She stuck out her tongue and made a funny face.

"Hey, mosquito! You are not nice! You are not smart! You are not cool! You are just a bug! A tiny, ugly, annoying bug! Go away and leave us alone!" she yelled.

The mosquito heard her and got angry. It flew towards her and tried to bite her too. But Anna was ready. She slid down the slide and dodged the mosquito. She laughed and ran to her mom and brother.

"Ha, ha, ha! I tricked you, mosquito! You are too slow and dumb! You can't catch me!" she said.

Ben saw his sister and smiled. He stopped crying and wiped his tears. He was proud of her. She was funny and smart. She helped him forget his pain.

"Thank you, Anna. You are the best sister ever. You scared the mosquito away. You made me laugh," he said.

Anna hugged him and said, "You're welcome, Ben. You are the best brother ever. You are brave and strong. You don't let the mosquito win."

Mom smiled and said, "You are both wonderful. You are kind and loving. You stick together and help each other. I'm so proud of you."

They hugged and kissed each other. They were happy and obedient. They played some more and had fun. They forgot about the mosquito. The mosquito was embarrassed. It flew away and never came back.

They ran to the bench and lifted the lid. Inside, they found a bag of rice. Sam was happy. He liked rice. He wanted to eat some.

"Yum, yum, this is our treasure!" he said, grabbing the bag.

But Lila was not happy. She did not like rice. She wanted something else.

"No, no, this is not treasure!" she said, pulling the bag. "This is normal food. I want gold and jewels!"

They started to tug the bag, each one trying to take it. They did not see a man coming to the bench. He was the owner of the rice. He was angry.

"Hey, you little pirates, what are you doing with my rice?" he shouted. "Give it back to me!"

Lila and Sam were scared. They dropped the bag and ran away.

"Sorry, sorry, we did not know!" they said.

The man picked up his rice and shook his head.

"Next time, ask before you take something that is not yours!" he said.

Lila and Sam learned their lesson. They decided to play something else. They did not want to be pirates anymore. They wanted to be normal kids.

Lily loved to perform. She liked to sing and dance and act in front of her family and friends. She always wore her best fashion when she performed. She had a pink dress, a blue hat, and a shiny necklace. She felt like a star.

One day, Lily wanted to perform a new show for her mom and dad. She had a big idea. She wanted to tell a story about a princess and a dragon. She needed some help. She asked her brother Tom to play the dragon. Tom was lazy. He did not like to perform. He liked to play with his cars and trucks.

"Please, Tom, please," Lily begged. "It will be fun. You just have to roar and chase me. I will be the princess and you will be the dragon. Mom and dad will love it."

Tom sighed. He did not want to make Lily sad. He agreed to play the dragon. But he did not try very hard. He put on a green shirt and a cardboard tail. He did not roar. He did not chase. He just walked slowly behind Lily.

Lily was not happy. She wanted her show to be exciting. She wanted her brother to be scary. She wanted her mom and dad to clap and cheer. She decided to change her story. She had a new idea.

She ran to her room and got her toy sword. She came back and said, "Now the story is different. I am not a princess. I am a knight. And you are not a dragon. You are a monster. And I will fight you and save the day."

Tom was surprised. He did not like this idea. He did not want to fight. He wanted to stop. But Lily did not listen. She ran at him with her sword. She shouted, "Take that, monster! You are no match for me!"

Tom tried to dodge. He tried to run. He tried to say, "Stop, Lily, stop!" But it was too late. Lily swung her sword and hit him on the head. Tom fell down and cried. Lily dropped her sword and gasped. She did not mean to hurt him. She ran to him and hugged him. She said, "I'm sorry, Tom, I'm sorry. Are you okay?"

Mom and dad heard the noise and came to see what happened. They saw Lily and Tom on the floor. They saw the green shirt and the cardboard tail. They saw the pink dress and the blue hat. They saw the toy sword and the shiny necklace. They understood what happened. They were not angry. They were not amused. They were worried.

They picked up Tom and checked his head. They said, "Oh, Tom, oh, Lily. What were you doing? Why were you fighting? You could have hurt each other. You have to be careful. You have to be kind. You have to play nice."

Lily and Tom felt bad. They said, "We're sorry, mom, we're sorry, dad. We were trying to perform. We were trying to have fun. We did not mean to fight. We did not mean to hurt. We love each other. We will play nice."

Mom and dad hugged them and kissed them. They said, "We love you, too. We're glad you're okay. We're proud of you for performing. But next time, please choose a different story. And please ask us first. We want to see your show. We want to clap and cheer. But we also want you to be safe and happy."

Lily and Tom nodded. They said, "Okay, mom, okay, dad. We will do that. We will choose a different story. We will ask you first. We will be safe and happy. And we will still perform. Because we love to perform."

The end.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toy cars on the floor. They liked to make them zoom and crash and beep. Ben had a red car and Lily had a blue car. They pretended they were racing on a big road.

"Zoom, zoom, zoom!" Ben said, making his car go fast. "I will win the race!"

"No, I will win!" Lily said, making her car go faster. "You are too slow!"

They both laughed and zoomed their cars around the floor. They did not see that their mom was walking in the room with a tray of cookies. She was going to give them a snack, but she was not looking at the floor.

"Oh no!" Mom said, as she tripped over Ben's car and dropped the tray. The cookies flew in the air and landed on the floor and on the couch and on the table. Mom fell down and hurt her knee.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Mom said, rubbing her knee. "That hurt a lot!"

Ben and Lily stopped playing and blinked. They saw the mess they made and felt bad. They ran to their mom and hugged her.

"Sorry, Mom!" Ben said. "We were careless. We did not see you."

"Sorry, Mom!" Lily said. "We were careless. We did not hear you."

Mom smiled and hugged them back. She was not angry, but she was sad.

"It's okay, my loves," Mom said. "But you have to be careful when you play. You have to look and listen and be aware of others. You could have hurt yourselves or me or the toys."

Ben and Lily nodded. They understood. They helped Mom get up and clean the mess. They threw away the broken cookies and saved the good ones. They put away their cars and said they were sorry again.

Mom kissed them and gave them each a cookie. She said she loved them and they said they loved her. They decided to play a quieter game, like puzzles or books. They did not want to be careless again. They wanted to be careful and kind.

One day, they decided to play that their country was very delicate. They said that everything was made of glass and flowers and feathers. They had to be very careful not to break anything. They wore shiny crowns and necklaces and dresses.

"I believe you, Lily," Ben said. "We have to be very brave and smart. We have to make rules and laws for our country. And we have to hide our box from the others."

They wrote some rules on a piece of paper and stuck it on the box. They said things like "No loud noises", "No touching the glass", and "No entering without permission". They thought they were very clever.

But they did not see that Tom, the bully, was watching them. He did not like Lily and Ben. He thought they were silly and boring. He wanted to ruin their game. He waited until they went inside the box. Then he ran over and kicked the box hard.

The box collapsed with a loud crash. Lily and Ben screamed. They were covered in broken glass and feathers and flowers. They were hurt and scared. They cried and hugged each other.

Tom laughed and ran away. He did not care that he had broken their box and their country. He did not care that he had hurt their feelings and their bodies. He did not believe in their game. He only believed in being mean.

Lily liked to study books. She liked to look at the pictures and the letters. She wanted to learn new things. But her brother Ben did not like to study. He liked to play with his toys and make noise.

One day, Lily found a penny on the floor. It was shiny and round. She was happy. She wanted to put it in her piggy bank. She picked it up and ran to her room.

But Ben saw her. He wanted the penny too. He ran after her and shouted, "Give me that penny! It's mine!"

Lily said, "No, it's not! I found it! It's mine!"

They reached Lily's room and started to tug on the penny. They both pulled hard. The penny flew out of their hands and rolled under the bed.

They both crawled under the bed to get it. But it was dark and dusty. They could not see the penny. They only saw spiders and dust bunnies.

They both screamed and ran out of the bed. They were scared and dirty. They did not want the penny anymore.

Mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw them crying and hugging each other. She was troubled. She asked them, "What happened? Why are you so upset?"

They told her about the penny and the bed. Mom smiled and hugged them. She said, "It's okay. The penny is not important. What is important is that you love each other and share. Do you understand?"

They nodded and said, "Yes, Mom. We're sorry. We love you."

Mom said, "I love you too. Now, why don't you go and study together? I have some books and puzzles for you. Maybe you can learn something new."

They smiled and said, "Okay, Mom. Thank you."

They went to the living room and studied together. They looked at the pictures and the letters. They learned new things. They were happy. They did not think about the penny anymore.

"Hello, swan. Do you like the bread?" Lily said.

The swan nodded and looked at them with its black eyes. It seemed friendly.

"Can I touch it?" Ben said. He reached out his arm to the swan.

"Wait, Ben, don't!" Lily said.

"Ow, ow, ow! The swan bit me! It hurts!" Ben said.

Lily ran to him and hugged him. She looked at his arm and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. The swan was not nice. It did not like you to touch it. Let me see your arm. Does it bleed?"

Ben shook his head and said, "No, it does not bleed. But it stings. Why did the swan bite me? I gave it bread."

Lily said, "I don't know, Ben. Maybe the swan was scared or angry. Maybe it wanted more bread. Maybe it did not want us to be near it. Swans are not like dogs or cats. They are wild animals. They do not like people to touch them. They can taste with their beaks and they can hurt with them too."

Ben said, "I see. I will not touch the swan again. I will not feed it either. I do not like the swan. It is not pretty. It is mean."

Lily said, "I agree. The swan is mean. But it is still graceful. It can swim and fly and make sounds. It is not its fault that it does not like us. It is just different. We should leave it alone and play somewhere else."

Ben said, "OK. Let's go to the slide. The slide is fun. It does not bite."

Lily said, "Yes, let's go to the slide. The slide is fun. It does not bite. And it does not taste your arm either."

"I'm Tim, and this is Lily. We are playing with the ball. Who are you?" Tim says.

"I'm Ben. I live here. This is my home. Do you want to play with me?" Ben says.

Tim and Lily look at each other. They feel sorry for Ben. He has no house, no toys, no friends.

"Sure, we want to play with you. Can we share the ball?" Lily says.

"Of course, you can. I have nothing to share, but I have a lot of fun. Come in, come in!" Ben says.

He moves aside and makes room for Tim and Lily. They crawl into the shelter. They play with the ball, and tell stories, and sing songs. They forget about the time. They make a new friend.

Lila and Tom were twins who liked to play in the jungle. They had a big tree house where they slept and kept their toys. Every morning, they would rise with the sun and go out to explore.

One day, they found a big red fruit that looked very juicy and sweet. They picked it and took it back to their tree house. They cut it in half and each took a bite. But the fruit was not sweet at all. It was bitter and made their mouths hurt. They spat it out and threw it away.

They heard a loud roar from behind the trees. It was a lion who smelled the fruit and wanted to eat it. The lion was angry that someone had taken his fruit and left it on the ground. He ran towards the tree house, ready to attack.

Lila and Tom were scared and climbed up the ladder to their tree house. They locked the door and hoped the lion would go away. They hugged each other and wished they had never found the bitter fruit. They learned a lesson: not everything that looks good is good.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play with paper and make things. One day, they found a big book with pictures of animals and flowers. They wanted to make some of them with paper.

They took some paper and looked at the book. Lily saw a picture of a butterfly. She liked the colors and the wings. She tried to fold the paper like the book showed. She made a butterfly. She was happy.

Ben saw a picture of a ring. He liked the shape and the shine. He tried to fold the paper like the book showed. He made a ring. He was proud.

They showed each other what they made. Lily said, "Your ring is nice. What is it for?" Ben said, "It is for marriage. When you love someone, you give them a ring and say you want to be with them forever." Lily said, "Oh, I see. Do you love someone?" Ben said, "Yes, I love you. You are my best friend. Do you want to marry me?" Lily said, "Yes, I do. You are my best friend too. Let's marry."

They put the ring on Lily's finger and hugged. They were happy. They did not know what marriage really meant. They just knew they liked each other and wanted to be together.

But then, their moms came to pick them up. They had to say goodbye. They did not want to leave. They cried. They gave each other their paper things. Lily said, "Keep my butterfly. It will remind you of me." Ben said, "Keep my ring. It will remind you of me." They hugged again and left.

They did not see each other for a long time. They moved to different places. They grew up. They forgot about their paper things. They forgot about their marriage.

Many years later, they met again. They were at a park. They did not recognize each other. They were both pale and sad. They had problems and worries. They had no friends.

They sat on a bench and talked. They found out they had the same names and the same birthday. They felt something familiar. They looked at each other and smiled. They felt happy.

They reached into their pockets and found their paper things. They were old and torn, but they still had their colors and shapes. They remembered their childhood. They remembered their marriage.

They looked at each other and said, "I love you. You are my best friend. Do you want to marry me?" They said, "Yes, I do. You are my best friend too. Let's marry."

They put the ring on Lily's finger and hugged. They were happy. They knew what marriage really meant. They knew they liked each other and wanted to be together.

Lily liked to help her mom in the kitchen. She wanted to be a good cook like her mom. One day, her mom asked her to get a pan from the cupboard. Lily was happy to do it. She opened the cupboard and saw a big shiny pan. She reached for it, but it was too high for her.

"Mom, I can't get the pan. It's too high," Lily said.

"Wait a minute, honey. I'll help you," her mom said.

But Lily did not want to wait. She saw a chair near the cupboard. She thought she could use it to get the pan. She moved the chair to the cupboard and climbed on it. She stretched her arm and grabbed the pan. But the pan was heavy and slippery. It slipped from her hand and fell on the floor. It made a loud noise and scared Lily. She lost her balance and fell off the chair. She hurt her knee and started to cry.

Her mom heard the noise and ran to the kitchen. She saw Lily on the floor and the pan next to her. She was worried and angry.

"Lily, what did you do? Why did you not wait for me? You could have hurt yourself badly. That was very dangerous," her mom said.

She picked up Lily and hugged her. She checked her knee and saw it was not bleeding. She kissed it and said, "It's okay, honey. You'll be fine. But you have to listen to me. You can't do things by yourself that are too hard or too risky. You have to ask for help or wait for me. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to help you. I wanted to get the pan. But it was too heavy and I fell. I won't do it again. I'll listen to you."

Her mom smiled and said, "I know you wanted to help me, and I appreciate it. But you have to be careful and safe. I love you, Lily. Now, let's return the pan to the cupboard and make some cookies together. How does that sound?"

Lily smiled and said, "I love you too, mom. That sounds yummy. Can I stir the dough?"

Her mom said, "Of course you can. But only with a spoon, not with a pan."

They laughed and went to the counter. They made some delicious cookies and had a good time. Lily learned her lesson and never tried to get the pan by herself again. She always asked for help or waited for her mom. She was a good helper and a good cook.

Once upon a time, there was a black cat named Sugar. Sugar loved to play and run in the big yard. She liked to hear the birds sing and chase them around.

One day, Sugar heard a loud noise. It was a big dog barking. Sugar was scared, but she wanted to see the dog. She walked slowly and saw the dog behind a fence. The dog was big and black, just like Sugar.

Sugar and the dog became friends. They played together every day, and they were very happy. Sugar liked to hear her new friend's bark, and they had lots of fun. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a class of little kids. They loved to play together and learn new things. One day, their teacher brought a big basket of fruits to share with the class. There were sweet apples and sour lemons.

A little boy named Timmy saw the sour lemons and wanted to try one. He asked his friend, Sally, if she would like to try it too. Sally was scared because she had never tried a sour lemon before. Timmy told her not to worry and they both took a bite. Their faces puckered up as they tasted the sour lemon. They laughed and shared the sour lemon with their friends.

The teacher saw them sharing and was very happy. She told the class that it was important to share and try new things together. The class learned that sharing can make new experiences more fun. From that day on, the kids in the class always shared their toys and snacks with each other. They also learned to yield to their friends when they wanted to play with something.

The moral of the story is that sharing and yielding to others can make everyone happy and help us learn and grow together.

Tim and Sue are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see big clouds in the sky. They hear loud noises. They feel rain on their faces.

"Look, Tim, a storm is coming!" Sue says.

"Let's go home, Sue. Storms are scary!" Tim says.

They run to their bikes. They part ways at the corner. Tim lives on the left. Sue lives on the right.

"Be careful, Sue!" Tim shouts.

"You too, Tim!" Sue shouts back.

They pedal fast. They reach their homes. They are wet and cold. But they are safe and happy. They wave to each other from their windows. They hope the storm will go away soon. They want to play outside again.

Ben and Mia liked to play with their kayak in the lake. They had a big kayak that was red and yellow. It was dependable and did not break. They took turns to paddle and steer the kayak. They had fun and saw many fish and birds.

One day, they wanted to go to the other side of the lake, where there was a big tree with a swing. They asked their mom if they could go. She said yes, but they had to be back before nap time. Ben and Mia agreed and got into their kayak. They paddled hard and fast. They wanted to get to the swing soon.

But when they got to the other side, they saw another boy on the swing. He was bigger than them and had a mean face. He said, "This is my swing. Go away. You can't play here." Ben and Mia felt sad and scared. They did not want to fight. They asked him nicely, "Can we have a turn, please? We came from far away in our kayak. We will share with you."

The boy laughed and said, "No, you can't. This is my tree and my swing. Your kayak is ugly and small. You are silly and weak. Go back to where you came from." He swung higher and higher and kicked his legs at them. Ben and Mia felt angry and hurt. They did not like the boy. They wanted to play on the swing.

They looked at each other and had an idea. They waited until the boy swung back and then they pushed their kayak under him. He swung forward and hit the kayak with his feet. He lost his balance and fell into the water. He splashed and screamed. He was wet and cold. Ben and Mia laughed and said, "That's what you get for being mean and rude. Now we can play on the swing. Our kayak is dependable and strong. We are smart and brave." They got out of their kayak and climbed on the swing. They swung high and low and had fun.

They played until they heard their mom calling them. They remembered it was nap time. They got back into their kayak and paddled to their mom. She hugged them and said, "You look happy and tired. Did you have fun on the swing?" Ben and Mia nodded and said, "Yes, we did. But we also met a bad boy who tried to stop us. We taught him a lesson with our kayak. He was wet and sorry." Their mom smiled and said, "You did well to stand up for yourselves. But don't be too rough. Sometimes you have to share and be kind." Ben and Mia agreed and said, "We know, mom. We are kind and share with each other. But not with mean boys." They got out of their kayak and followed their mom to their house. They had a good nap and dreamed of their kayak and their swing.

Anna and Ben are playing in the kitchen. They like to pretend they are chefs and make yummy food. They have a big oven that can bake cakes and pies. Anna wants to make a cake for Mommy, who is in the living room.

"Ben, can you help me make a cake?" Anna asks. "We need flour, eggs, milk, and sugar."

"OK, Anna, I will help you," Ben says. "But we have to be careful with the oven. It is very hot and can hurt us."

Anna and Ben find the ingredients and mix them in a big bowl. They pour the batter into a cake pan and put it in the oven. They set the timer for 20 minutes and wait.

"Anna, I'm bored. Can we play something else?" Ben says.

"No, Ben, we have to watch the cake. We don't want it to burn," Anna says.

"But I want to play with my cars. They are in the bedroom. Can we go there?" Ben says.

"Fine, Ben, but only for a little while. We have to come back soon," Anna says.

Anna and Ben go to the bedroom and play with the cars. They have fun making noises and racing. They forget about the cake and the oven.

The timer beeps in the kitchen, but they don't hear it. The cake starts to smell bad and smoke. Mommy smells the smoke and gets worried. She runs to the kitchen and sees the cake burning in the oven. She turns off the oven and takes out the cake. It is black and hard.

"Anna! Ben! What have you done?" Mommy yells.

Anna and Ben hear Mommy and get scared. They run to the kitchen and see the cake. They feel sorry and sad.

"Mommy, we are sorry. We wanted to make you a cake, but we forgot," Anna says.

"Mommy, we are sorry. We didn't mean to make a mess," Ben says.

Mommy is angry, but she loves Anna and Ben. She hugs them and says, "I appreciate your thought, but you should never play with the oven. It is dangerous and can cause a fire. You could have been hurt. Next time, ask me before you use the oven, OK?"

"OK, Mommy, we will," Anna and Ben say.

Mommy throws away the cake and cleans the oven. She makes a new cake with Anna and Ben. They help her measure, stir, and decorate. The new cake is delicious and pretty. They eat it together and say, "Happy Mother's Day!"

Lily and Tom were playing dress-up in their room. They had many clothes and hats and shoes to try on. Lily liked to act like a princess, and Tom liked to act like a spy.

Lily put on a pink dress and a crown. She looked in the mirror and smiled. She felt very pretty and important. She said to Tom, "I am the princess of this castle. You have to do what I say."

Tom put on a black coat and a hat. He also found a tie in the closet. He did not know how to wear a tie, but he tried to wrap it around his neck. He looked in the mirror and frowned. He felt very silly and uncomfortable. He said to Lily, "I am a spy on a secret mission. I have to find the bad guys and stop them."

Lily and Tom started to play. Lily pretended to give orders to Tom, and Tom pretended to sneak around the room. They had fun making noises and faces and stories.

But then, Tom tripped on his tie and fell on the floor. He hurt his knee and started to cry. Lily ran to him and saw that his tie was torn. She felt sorry for him and hugged him. She said to Tom, "I'm sorry, Tom. Are you okay? Your tie is very delicate. You have to be careful with it."

Tom stopped crying and looked at his tie. He saw that it was ripped and dirty. He felt sad and angry. He said to Lily, "I don't like this tie. It's too hard to wear. It's not good for a spy. I want a different tie."

Lily thought for a moment. She had an idea. She took off her crown and gave it to Tom. She said to Tom, "Here, Tom. You can have my crown. It's very shiny and cool. It's good for a spy. You can wear it instead of a tie."

Tom looked at the crown. He saw that it was sparkly and bright. He felt happy and curious. He said to Lily, "Thank you, Lily. Your crown is very nice. It's good for a spy. I can wear it instead of a tie."

Lily and Tom smiled at each other. They swapped their clothes and hats and shoes. They continued to play dress-up. They acted like a spy and a princess. They had fun.

Tom and Lily were playing with their blocks in the living room. They liked to build towers and houses and cars with the blocks. They had many colors and shapes of blocks to choose from.

"Look, Lily, I made a big tower!" Tom said, showing his sister his creation. "It is taller than you!"

Lily smiled and said, "That is a nice tower, Tom. But I made a house. It has a door and a window and a roof. Do you want to see?"

Tom nodded and walked over to Lily's house. He liked her house too. He wanted to touch the door and the window and the roof.

But as he reached out his arm, he bumped into the tower. The tower wobbled and then fell down. The blocks scattered all over the floor. Some of them hit Tom and Lily and made them cry.

Mom heard the noise and came to the living room. She saw the mess and the tears and felt worried. She hugged Tom and Lily and said, "Are you okay, my loves? Did you hurt yourselves?"

Tom and Lily sniffed and said, "We are okay, Mom. But our blocks are broken. We worked hard to make them."

Mom said, "I know, my loves. But blocks are not broken. They are just scattered. You can pick them up and make them again. And maybe you can help each other and share your ideas. How does that sound?"

Tom and Lily nodded and said, "Okay, Mom. We are sorry for the noise."

Mom said, "It's okay, my loves. I'm glad you are okay. Now, let's clean up and then you can play some more. And maybe you can show me your tower and your house later. I would love to see them."

Tom and Lily smiled and said, "Okay, Mom. We love you."

Mom said, "I love you too, my loves. Now, let's get to work."

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they find a kite in the park. It is big and red and has a long tail.

"Wow, look at this kite!" Tim says. "Can we fly it?"

"Sure, let's try!" Sam says. "But we need to tie it to something first."

They look around and see a tree. They run to the tree and tie the kite to a branch. Then they pull the kite and let it go. The kite flies high in the sky. It looks like a bird.

"Yay, it works!" Tim says. "It is so pretty!"

Sam nods. He is happy too. But then he sees something else. He sees a cloud. It is big and gray and has a loud sound. It is a storm cloud.

"Oh no, look at that cloud!" Sam says. "It is coming this way!"

Tim looks up and sees the cloud too. He is scared. He does not like storms. They make him feel pale and cold.

"Let's go home!" Tim says. "We need to get the kite first!"

They run to the tree and try to untie the kite. But the knot is too tight. They pull and pull, but they cannot undo it.

"Help, help!" Tim says. "We can't get the kite!"

Sam has an idea. He sees a rock. He picks it up and throws it at the branch. The branch breaks and the kite falls down. They catch the kite and run away.

"Thank you, Sam!" Tim says. "You are smart and brave!"

Sam smiles. He is glad he helped his friend. They hold the kite and run home. They are safe and happy. They still like the kite, but they do not like the storm.

Lily and Ben were bored. They wanted to play a trick on Mom. They had a plan. They found some tape in the drawer. They taped the door to the kitchen. They hid behind the couch and waited.

Mom came home from the store. She had a big bag of food. She tried to open the door to the kitchen, but it was stuck. She pushed and pulled, but the tape was too strong. She said, "What is going on? Who did this?"

Lily and Ben giggled. They thought it was funny. But then they saw Mom's face. She was not happy. She was angry. She looked around and saw them behind the couch. She said, "Lily and Ben, did you do this? This is not nice. This is naughty. You made a mess and wasted the tape. You could have hurt me or the door. You need to say sorry and help me clean up."

Lily and Ben felt bad. They did not mean to make Mom angry. They did not think about the mess or the hurt. They felt guilty. They said, "Sorry, Mom. We were just playing. We won't do it again." They got up and helped Mom take off the tape and put it in the trash. They hugged Mom and said, "We love you, Mom."

Mom smiled and hugged them back. She said, "I love you too, Lily and Ben. I know you were just playing, but you need to be careful and respectful. Next time, ask me before you use the tape. And don't tape the door. That's not a good trick. How about we make some cookies instead?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They liked cookies. They followed Mom to the kitchen and helped her make some yummy cookies. They ate some and shared some with Mom. They felt happy and sorry at the same time. They learned their lesson. They did not tape the door again.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a stream with many fish and frogs. They wanted to catch them and put them in a bucket.

"Look, Tom, a big fish!" Lily said. She kneeled by the stream and reached her hand into the water. She grabbed the fish and pulled it out. It was slippery and shiny.

"Wow, Lily, you are good at catching fish!" Tom said. He kneeled next to her and tried to catch a frog. He missed and splashed water on his face. He laughed and wiped his eyes.

They put the fish and the frog in the bucket and looked for more. They had fun and forgot about the time.

But then they heard a voice. It was Mom. She was looking for them and she sounded angry.

"Lily! Tom! Where are you? It's time to go home!" Mom shouted.

Lily and Tom felt guilty. They knew they should have listened to Mom and not gone too far. They picked up the bucket and ran to Mom.

"Mom, we are sorry. We were playing by the stream and we caught some fish and frogs. Can we keep them?" Lily asked.

Mom looked at the bucket and shook her head. She was not happy.

"No, you can't keep them. They belong to the stream. You have to let them go. And you have to say sorry to the fish and the frogs for taking them away from their home." Mom said.

Lily and Tom nodded. They felt bad for the fish and the frogs. They went back to the stream and kneeled again. They poured the water and the animals back into the stream.

"Sorry, fish. Sorry, frog. We hope you are okay. We won't catch you again." Lily and Tom said.

They waved goodbye to the fish and the frogs and followed Mom to the car. They learned their lesson and promised to be more careful next time.

Tim and Mia were playing with their toy boats in the bath. They pretended that the bath was a big sea and the edge was a port. They made noises like waves and horns and engines.

"Look at my boat, it's faster and stronger than yours!" Tim said. He pushed his boat towards Mia's and bumped it hard.

"Hey, stop that! You're being mean!" Mia said. She tried to move her boat away, but Tim followed her and bumped it again.

"Ha ha, I'm going to destroy your boat and take over the port!" Tim said. He bumped Mia's boat so hard that it flipped over and sank.

Mia started to cry. She was sad and angry that Tim ruined her boat and her game. She grabbed Tim's boat and threw it out of the bath.

"Hey, what did you do that for?" Tim said. He was shocked and scared that Mia threw his boat. He heard a loud crash and saw that his boat hit the mirror and broke it.

Mom came running into the bathroom. She saw the broken mirror, the wet floor, and the crying children. She was very upset and angry.

"What happened here? Who broke the mirror?" Mom said.

Tim felt embarrassed and ashamed. He knew he was wrong to be mean to Mia and to break the mirror. He pointed at Mia and said, "She did it!"

Mia felt hurt and betrayed. She knew Tim was lying and trying to blame her. She pointed at Tim and said, "He did it!"

Mom looked at both of them and sighed. She knew they were both in trouble. She said, "You both did it. You both need to say sorry to each other and to me. And you both need to help me clean up this mess. And no more playing with boats in the bath!"

Ben and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. Ben had a big truck that made loud noises. Lily had a soft doll that she hugged and kissed. Ben liked to pretend that his truck had power and could move anything. Lily liked to pretend that her doll was her baby and could talk to her.

"Vroom, vroom, vroom!" Ben said, as he drove his truck around the floor. He saw Lily's doll lying on the couch. He wanted to play with it too. He drove his truck towards the doll and tried to push it off the couch.

"Hey, stop it!" Lily said, as she ran to the couch and grabbed her doll. She held it tight in her arms. "This is my doll, not your truck!"

"But I want to play with it!" Ben said, as he reached for the doll. He pulled on its leg, but Lily did not let go.

"No, you can't!" Lily said, as she pulled back. "You will break it or chew it!"

"I will not!" Ben said, as he pulled harder. "I just want to see it!"

They both pulled and pulled, until the doll's leg came off. They both gasped and looked at the doll. Lily started to cry. Ben felt sorry.

"I'm sorry, Lily," Ben said, as he gave her the doll's leg. "I didn't mean to hurt your doll."

Lily sniffed and took the leg. She looked at Ben and saw that he was sad too.

"It's okay, Ben," Lily said, as she wiped her tears. "Maybe we can fix it."

They hugged and said they were sorry. Then they went to find their mom and asked her to help them fix the doll. Mom smiled and said she would. She was glad that they learned to share and be kind.

Sara and Ben were playing with blocks in their room. They liked to create towers and castles and bridges with the blocks. They were having a jolly time, laughing and sharing.

But then, a loud noise made them jump. It was thunder, from the big storm outside. Sara was scared of thunder. She dropped her blocks and ran to the bed. She hid under the blanket and cried.

Ben felt sorry for his sister. He wanted to help her. He picked up some blocks and walked to the bed. He said, "Sara, don't be scared. Thunder is just a sound. It can't hurt you. Look, I made you something."

He lifted the blanket and showed her his creation. It was a block house, with a roof and a door and a window. He put it on the bed next to her. He said, "This is your house. It is strong and safe. You can hide in it when you hear thunder. And I will be with you. We can play in your house together."

Sara smiled and wiped her tears. She liked the block house. She hugged her brother and said, "Thank you, Ben. You are very kind. I am not scared anymore. You are the best brother ever."

They put the blanket over the block house and crawled inside. They pretended they were in a cozy cottage in the woods. They played with their blocks and told stories. They did not mind the thunder anymore. They were happy and jolly.

Lily liked to draw with her crayons. She had many colors and made pictures of flowers, animals and people. She was very happy when she drew.

One day, she was drawing in her room when she heard a loud noise. It was her brother, Max, who came in. He saw her crayons and wanted to play with them.

"Give me your crayons!" he said in a harsh voice. He grabbed some of them from her hand and threw them on the floor.

Lily was very sad and angry. She did not like when Max was mean to her. She wanted her crayons back.

"No, they are mine!" she said. "You are bad! Go away!"

She tried to get her crayons, but Max was bigger and stronger. He pushed her away and laughed.

Lily started to cry. She did not know what to do. She wished Max would leave her alone.

She heard another noise. It was her mom, who heard her cry. She came in and saw what Max did.

"Max, what are you doing?" she said in a stern voice. "Why are you hurting your sister and her crayons?"

Max was scared of his mom. He knew he did something wrong. He dropped the crayons and ran away.

Mom hugged Lily and helped her pick up her crayons. She said she was sorry that Max was rude. She said she would talk to him and make him say sorry.

Lily felt better. She thanked her mom and gave her a kiss. She went back to drawing with her crayons. She hoped Max would be nicer to her next time.

Anna liked to study. She liked to look at books and learn new things. She had a cat named Tom. Tom liked to play and sleep. He did not like to study.

One day, Anna wanted to study about stars. She found a big book with pictures of stars. She opened the book on the floor and started to look at it. Tom saw the book and was curious. He walked over to the book and sniffed it. He did not like the smell of the book. He scratched the book with his claws.

"Tom, no!" Anna shouted. "That is my book! You are making it bad!"

Tom did not listen. He scratched the book more and more. He tore some pages with his teeth. He made a big mess.

Anna was very angry and sad. She ran to her mom and told her what Tom did. Her mom was worried. She went to see the book and Tom. She saw the book was ruined. She saw Tom was sick. He had eaten some of the paper and glue from the book. He was coughing and shaking.

"Oh no, Tom!" her mom said. "We have to take you to the vet!"

She picked up Tom and put him in a box. She told Anna to get her coat and shoes. They had to go to the car and drive to the vet.

Anna was scared. She did not want Tom to be sick. She did not want to lose Tom. She wished she had not studied about stars. She wished she had played with Tom instead. She hugged Tom and said sorry. But Tom did not hear her. He was too sick. He closed his eyes and did not open them again.

Lily and Ben were friends. They liked to play with toys and draw pictures. One day, they had a big fight. Lily wanted to play with the black car, but Ben said it was his. He grabbed the car and ran away. Lily was very angry. She shouted at Ben and threw a crayon at him. It hit his eye and made him cry.

"Ow! That hurt! You are mean, Lily!" Ben said.

"I don't care! You are mean, too! You took my car!" Lily said.

They did not talk to each other for a long time. They sat in different corners of the room and made faces. The teacher saw them and was sad. She wanted them to be friends again. She came to them and said:

"Lily and Ben, why are you so quiet? What happened?"

They told her about the fight. The teacher said:

"I see. You both wanted the same toy, and you did not share. That was not nice. But you also hurt each other with your words and your crayon. That was not nice, either. You should say sorry and forgive each other. Then you can play together again. Can you do that?"

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They did not want to say sorry. They did not want to forgive. They were still angry. They shook their heads and said:

"No!"

The teacher sighed. She said:

"Okay. Then you have to stay in your corners until you change your minds. You can't play with any other toys or friends. You have to be quiet and think about what you did."

Lily and Ben did not like that. They wanted to play and have fun. But they were too stubborn to say sorry and forgive. They stayed in their corners and missed all the fun. They were very bored and lonely. They wished they had not fought over the black car. But it was too late. They had lost their friend. The end.

Ben and Tom are friends. They like to play with cars and balls. One day, they go to the park with their moms. They see a big truck with a sign. The sign says "work".

"Look, Ben, a work truck!" Tom says. "Let's go see!"

"No, Tom, we can't. Mom said we have to stay here. Work trucks are not for kids. They are for grown-ups. They can be dangerous," Ben says.

But Tom does not listen. He runs to the work truck. He wants to touch it and see what it does. He does not see the man who is driving the work truck. The man does not see Tom either. He is busy talking on his phone.

"Hey, what are you doing? Get away from there!" the man yells. He sees Tom at the last second. He tries to stop the work truck, but it is too late. The work truck hits Tom. Tom falls to the ground. He does not move. He does not make a sound.

Ben and the moms hear the man yell. They run to the work truck. They see Tom on the ground. They are scared and sad. They cry and scream.

"Tom, Tom, wake up! Please, wake up!" Ben says. He shakes Tom's body. But Tom does not wake up. He is gone.

The man gets out of the work truck. He is confused and sorry. He did not mean to hurt Tom. He did not see him. He says he is sorry. He says he will call for help. But it is too late. Nothing can bring Tom back.

Ben and the moms are very sad. They hug each other. They miss Tom. They wish he had listened to Ben. They wish he had stayed away from the work truck. They wish he was still alive.

One day, Lily and Max went to the park with their mom. They saw many flowers and trees and birds. They liked to play and run and laugh.

They found a big green caterpillar on a leaf. Lily wanted to touch it, but Max said, "No, it is bitter. It can hurt you with its hairs. Mom told us to be careful with caterpillars."

Lily said, "But it is so cute and fuzzy. I want to be its friend. Maybe it is not bitter. Maybe it is sweet."

She reached out her hand to the caterpillar, but it moved away. It did not want to be touched. It wanted to eat the leaf and be alone.

Lily was sad. She said, "Why are you so mean, caterpillar? Don't you like me?"

The caterpillar said, "I am not mean. I am just busy. I need to eat and grow and change. One day, I will be a butterfly. Then I will fly and see the world. But now, I need to soak in the sun and the rain and the wind. Please, leave me alone."

Lily and Max understood. They said, "Okay, caterpillar. We are sorry. We will let you be. We hope you will be a beautiful butterfly."

They waved goodbye to the caterpillar and went to play with their mom. They had fun in the park. They learned something new. They were happy.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. They saw a big house with a red roof. They wondered what was inside.

"Let's go and see!" said Ben.

"No, we can't. That's not our house. We have to ask first." said Lily.

But Ben did not listen. He ran to the house and climbed on the roof. He wanted to look in the windows. Lily followed him. She was scared.

They saw a big cake on the table. It smelled good. They were hungry.

"Let's take some!" said Ben.

"No, we can't. That's not our cake. We have to say please and thank you." said Lily.

But Ben did not listen. He reached for the cake. He did not see the dog. The dog saw him. The dog barked loud. He was angry.

Lily and Ben were scared. They ran away from the roof. They fell and hurt themselves. They cried.

The owner of the house came out. He saw them. He was not happy.

"Who are you? What are you doing on my roof? Why did you try to take my cake?" he asked.

Lily and Ben were sorry. They said sorry.

"We were playing in the park. We saw your house. We were curious. We were hungry." they said.

The owner of the house was kind. He said sorry too.

"I'm sorry for my dog. He was protecting my house. He was hungry too. Do you want some cake?" he asked.

Lily and Ben said yes. They said please and thank you. They ate some cake. They shared with the dog. They became friends.

The owner of the house said:

"Next time, if you want to see my house, you have to ask me first. You have to respect other people's things. You have to be polite and honest. Do you understand?" he asked.

Lily and Ben said yes. They learned their lesson. They said goodbye. They went back to the park. They played some more. They were happy.

Lily loved to sing. She sang every day, in the morning, in the afternoon, and at night. She sang to her dolls, to her dog, and to her mom and dad. She sang happy songs, sad songs, and silly songs. Singing made her feel good.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. But soon they felt tired and yawned.

"Let's nap, Lily," Ben said. "Nap is good."

"OK, Ben," Lily said. "But where do we nap?"

They looked around and saw a big couch with soft pillows and a warm blanket. They thought it looked cozy and comfortable.

"Let's nap on the couch," Ben said. "Couch is nice."

They climbed on the couch and snuggled under the blanket. They closed their eyes and fell asleep.

But they did not know that their dog, Spot, was also napping on the couch. Spot was smelly because he had rolled in the mud and the garbage. He had a cold and he sneezed and snored.

Soon, Ben and Lily woke up and smelled something bad. They opened their eyes and saw Spot next to them. He was licking their faces and wagging his tail.

"Yuck, Spot!" Ben said. "You are smelly!"

"Go away, Spot!" Lily said. "You have a cold!"
