Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with many leaves. They wanted to climb the tree and see the sky.

"Can we climb the tree, Lily?" Ben asked.

"Yes, we can, Ben. But we have to be careful. The tree is very high and the branches are very thin," Lily said.

They found a low branch and tried to pull themselves up. But the branch was too slippery and they fell down.

"Ouch! That hurt!" Ben cried.

"Are you okay, Ben?" Lily asked.

"I think so. But my knee is bleeding," Ben said.

They saw a lady walking by with a dog. The lady was old and had white hair. The dog was small and had brown fur.

"Excuse me, lady. Can you help us?" Lily called.

The lady came over and saw their problem. She smiled and knelt down.

"Hello, children. What happened to you?" she asked.

"We tried to climb the tree, but we fell down. Ben's knee is bleeding," Lily said.

"I see. Well, you are very brave, but you are also very foolish. Climbing trees is not a regular game. It is dangerous and can hurt you. You should play something else, like catch or tag," the lady said.

She took out a tissue and wiped Ben's knee. She put a band-aid on it and gave him a hug.

"Thank you, lady. You are very kind," Ben said.

"You're welcome, Ben. And you, Lily, you are a good friend. You should always look after Ben and yourself. That is wisdom," the lady said.

She stood up and walked away with her dog.

"Bye, lady. Bye, dog," Lily and Ben said.

They waved at the lady and the dog. Then they decided to play catch instead of climbing trees. They learned their lesson and had fun.

Ben and Lily liked to play with their toys in their room. They had many toys: cars, dolls, blocks, books, and more. But they did not like to organize their toys. They left them on the floor, on the bed, on the table, everywhere. Their mom always told them to clean up, but they did not listen.

One night, when they were sleeping, they heard a strange noise. It sounded like someone was moving their toys. They opened their eyes and saw a white shape in the dark. It was a ghost! The ghost was holding their toys and putting them in boxes and shelves. The ghost looked angry and sad.

"Who are you?" Ben asked, feeling scared.

"I am the ghost of toys," the ghost said. "I come to organize the toys that children do not care for. You have so many toys, but you do not play with them nicely. You do not put them away. You make them dirty and broken. That makes me very sad."

"Why do you care?" Lily asked, feeling curious.

"Because I used to be a child like you," the ghost said. "But I had no toys. I had nothing to play with. I always wished for toys, but I never got any. When I died, I became the ghost of toys. I go to the rooms of children who have toys, and I organize them. I hope they will appreciate them more."

Ben and Lily felt sorry for the ghost. They realized they were lucky to have toys, and they should take care of them.

"Can we help you?" Ben asked.

"Yes, you can," the ghost said. "You can help me organize your toys, and then you can play with them. But you have to promise me something."

"What is it?" Lily asked.

"You have to promise me that you will always organize your toys after you play with them. You have to promise me that you will love your toys and treat them well. Can you do that?"

Ben and Lily nodded. They said, "We promise."

The ghost smiled. He said, "Thank you. You are good children. Now, let's organize your toys together. It will be fun."

Ben and Lily got out of bed and joined the ghost. They picked up their toys and put them in the right places. They talked and laughed with the ghost. They learned how to organize their toys. They also learned how to be grateful and kind. They had a difficult but wonderful night with the ghost of toys.

"Hey! Don't push me!" Lily said. She was hurt and angry. She did not like Ben to push her. She pushed him back.

But Max did not like Lily's scarf. He thought it was too bright and silly. He liked to tease her and pull on it. He said it was a snake that would bite her. He made her cry sometimes.

Max did not answer. He looked down and let go of the scarf.

Lily's mom hugged her and checked her scarf. It was a little torn, but still okay.

"Are you okay, sweetie?" she asked.

Lily nodded. She wiped her tears and wrapped her scarf around her neck.

Max's mom scolded him and made him apologize to Lily.

"I'm sorry, Lily," he said in a low voice.

Lily looked at him. She saw that he was sorry. She decided to be nice.

"It's okay, Max," she said. "But don't do it again. This is my favorite scarf."

Max nodded. He did not say anything else.

Their moms smiled and suggested that they play nicely together. They gave them some cookies and juice.

A lecture is when I talk to you for a long time and tell you what you did wrong and why you have to change. You do not want a lecture, do you?"

Lily and Ben did not want a lecture. They knew they had been bad. They felt sorry for grandma and for mom and dad. They said, "We are sorry, grandma. We will behave well. Lily and Ben nodded and smiled. They helped grandma clean up and they had some cookies and milk. They behaved well for the rest of the day. They hoped mom and dad would be proud of them. They learned their lesson and they did not want a lecture again.

Lily and Tom are friends. They live in the same country. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a big ball. It is red and blue and yellow.

"Let's play with the ball!" Lily says.

"OK!" Tom says. "I will throw it to you, and you catch it."

They take turns to throw and catch the ball. They have fun. They laugh and run and jump.

But then, the ball goes too far. It flies over the fence. It lands in the deep pond.

"Oh no!" Lily says. "The ball is gone!"

"Maybe we can get it back," Tom says. "Let's go to the pond."

They run to the fence. They look at the pond. The water is dark and still. They cannot see the ball.

"Where is the ball?" Lily asks.

"I don't know," Tom says. "Maybe it is under the water."

They are sad. They like the ball. They want to play with it again.

"Maybe we can ask someone to help us," Lily says.

"Who can help us?" Tom asks.

They look around. They see a man. He is walking his dog. He is near the pond.

"Excuse me, sir," Lily says. "Can you help us?"

The man stops. He looks at them. He smiles.

"Hello, children," he says. "What do you need?"

"We lost our ball," Tom says. "It is in the pond."

The man nods. He sees the ball. It is floating on the water. It is not very deep.

"I can help you," he says. "Wait here."

He walks to the pond. He takes off his shoes. He rolls up his pants. He steps into the water. He reaches for the ball. He grabs it. He walks back to the shore. He gives the ball to Lily and Tom.

"Here you go," he says. "Be careful next time."

"Thank you, sir," Lily and Tom say. "You are very kind."

They are happy. They have their ball back. They hug the man. They hug the dog. They say goodbye.

They go back to the park. They play with the ball. They are careful not to throw it too far. They have fun. They laugh and run and jump.

"Wow, look at that bird!" Lila said. "It is so pretty and shiny. I admire it a lot. Do you think it can talk?"

"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe it can. Let's try to talk to it."

They walked closer to the tree and called out to the bird. "Hello, bird! What is your name? Where do you come from?"

The bird looked at them and made a loud noise. "Caw, caw, caw!" It said. "I am a crow. I come from far away. I am very wise and clever. You are not. You are silly and small."

Lila and Ben felt hurt by the crow's words. They did not like how it was rude and mean to them. They wanted to go away, but they also wanted to show the crow that they were not silly and small.

"We are not silly and small," Lila said. "We are smart and brave. We can do many things that you can't. We can climb the tree and touch you."

The crow laughed. "Caw, caw, caw! You can't climb the tree. It is too high and slippery. You will fall and hurt yourself. Go away, or I will peck you."

Lila and Ben did not listen to the crow. They wanted to prove it wrong. They started to climb the tree, holding on to the branches and the leaves. They got higher and higher, until they were close to the crow.

"See, we can climb the tree," Ben said. "We are not afraid of you. You are not wise and clever. You are mean and ugly."

The crow got angry. It flapped its wings and pecked at Lila and Ben. It made them lose their balance and fall from the tree. They landed on the ground with a thud. They felt pain in their arms and legs. They cried and called for help.

The crow flew away, cawing and mocking them. "Caw, caw, caw! I told you so. You are silly and small. You should have listened to me. I am wise and clever. You are not."

"I'm sorry, Tim and Lily," she said. "I know you wanted to make me proud, but you have to be careful. Some mushrooms are good, but some mushrooms are bad. You have to ask me before you pick anything in the garden. Do you understand?"

Tim and Lily nodded. They felt sad. They did not want to make Mommy angry.

"We're sorry, Mommy," they said. "We won't do it again."

Mommy hugged them. She smiled.

"It's okay, Tim and Lily," she said. "I love you. You are still my proud kids. How about we have some cake instead?"

Tim and Lily cheered. They forgot about the mushroom. They had some cake with Mommy. It was sweet and yummy. They were happy.

Tom and Lily were fish who lived in a big reef. They liked to swim and play with their friends. One day, they saw a shiny thing on the sand. It was a coin.

"Wow, look at this!" Tom said. "We can buy something with this!"

"Like what?" Lily asked.

"Maybe a new toy, or a pretty shell, or a tasty worm!" Tom said.

They swam to the market, where many fish sold different things. They saw a lot of things they liked, but they were too expensive. They only had one coin.

Then they saw a fish who sold a scarf. It was red and soft and warm.

"Hello, little fish!" the fish said. "Do you like this scarf? It is very good for cold days. You can have it for one coin!"

Tom and Lily looked at the scarf. It was very nice, but they did not need it. They lived in a warm reef, not a cold place.

"Thank you, but no thank you," Lily said. "We do not need a scarf. We are not cold."

But Tom liked the scarf. He thought it would make him look cool and smart.

"Please, Lily, can we buy it?" he begged. "It is only one coin, and we have one coin!"

Lily shook her head. "No, Tom, we do not need it. We should save our coin for something we really need, or share it with someone who needs it more. That is what our mom and dad taught us."

But Tom did not listen. He gave the coin to the fish and took the scarf. He wrapped it around his neck and swam away.

"Look at me, Lily!" he said. "I look so good with this scarf!"

Lily followed him, feeling sad. She did not think the scarf was worth their coin.

They swam back to the reef, where their friends were waiting for them. They saw Tom's scarf and laughed.

"What is that?" they asked. "Why do you have a scarf? Are you cold?"

Tom felt embarrassed. He realized that the scarf was silly and useless. He wished he had listened to Lily and kept their coin.

He took off the scarf and gave it back to Lily. He said he was sorry for being greedy and foolish. He asked her to forgive him.

Lily smiled and hugged him. She said she forgave him. She said they could still use their scarf for something good. They could give it to someone who was cold, or make it into a toy, or trade it for something they needed.

They swam to the market again, looking for someone who needed their scarf. They saw a crab who was shivering on a rock. He had no home and no friends.

"Hello, Mr. Crab," Lily said. "Are you cold?"

The crab nodded. He said he was cold and lonely.

Lily and Tom gave him their scarf. They said they wanted to help him and be his friends.

The crab smiled. He thanked them and wrapped the scarf around his claws. He said he felt warm and happy.

Lily and Tom felt happy too. They learned that it was better to be kind and generous than to be selfish and wasteful. They made a new friend and a good deed.

"Wow, cookies!" Anna and Ben say.

"Really?" Anna and Ben say.

Anna says, "I want to turn into a yellow butterfly!"

Ben says, "I want to turn into a yellow dinosaur!"

They eat the cookies and close their eyes. They feel a strange tingling in their bodies. They open their eyes and see that they have turned into what they said.

Anna has wings and antennae. Ben has scales and teeth. They are both yellow.

They are amazed and happy. They run outside and play with their new shapes. Anna flies and flutters. Ben stomps and growls. They have a lot of fun.

But soon, they feel the tingling again. They look at each other and see that they are changing back. Their wings and scales disappear. Their antennae and teeth shrink. They are no longer yellow.

They are Anna and Ben again.

They hug each other and laugh. They run back to the kitchen and thank Mom for the cookies. They tell her about their adventure.

Mom smiles and hugs them. She says, "I'm glad you had fun. But remember, you are always special, no matter what you turn into. You are my yellow stars."

She ran after the cricket, but it was very fast and clever. It jumped and hid under a big leaf. Lily followed it and peeked under the leaf. She saw the cricket's shiny eyes and long antennae. She smiled and reached out her hand.

"Hello, cricket. Do you want to be my friend?" she asked.

But the cricket did not want to be her friend. It was scared of Lily and her big hand. It made a loud chirp and jumped out of the leaf. It landed on Lily's nose and bit her hard.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily cried. She dropped the leaf and rubbed her nose. It hurt a lot and it started to bleed. She ran back to the house, crying and sniffling.

Mama heard her and came out. She saw Lily's nose and hugged her.

"What happened, my dear?" she asked.

"A cricket bit me, Mama. It was mean and nasty. I just wanted to be its friend," Lily sobbed.

Mama wiped her nose and kissed her cheek.

"I'm sorry, Lily. Some bugs don't like to be touched. They are afraid of us and they defend themselves. You have to be careful and gentle with them. And sometimes, it's better to leave them alone and watch them from afar," Mama said.

Lily nodded and sniffed. She learned her lesson. She decided to be more respectful of the bugs in the garden. She still liked to explore, but she never peeked under a leaf again.

Sara and Ben nod. They say, "Yes, we understand. We are sorry. We do not want to fight. We want to be friends."

Sara's mom says, "That is good. Now, hug and say sorry to each other. Then you can play together again."

Sara and Ben hug and say sorry. They smile and say, "We are friends. We can share and take turns. We can have fun with the cell and the toys."

Sara and Ben say, "Okay, we will. Thank you, mom."

"Your rocket is silly, Max. It is too thin and noisy. My doll is much better. She is so pretty and soft!" Lily said, hugging her doll.

Max felt angry and sad. He wanted Lily to like his rocket. He thought of a way to make her see how cool his rocket was. He ran to the hose and filled his rocket with water. Then he aimed it at Lily and her doll.

"Watch this, Lily! My rocket can squirt water!" Max said, pressing a button on his rocket.

But Max did not know how to control his rocket. The water came out too fast and too much. It sprayed all over Lily and her doll, and also over Max and his rocket. Lily and Max were wet and cold. Lily's doll was wet and dirty. Max's rocket was wet and broken.

Lily and Max started to cry. They felt embarrassed and sorry. They ran to their mom and dad, who were sitting on the porch.

"What happened, kids? Why are you so wet and sad?" Mom asked, wrapping them in towels.

"We were playing with our toys, but we had a fight. Max squirted water at me and my doll, and I said his rocket was silly. Now our toys are ruined and we are sorry," Lily said, sniffling.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I wanted you to like my rocket, but I made a mess. I didn't mean to hurt you and your doll," Max said, sobbing.

Mom and Dad hugged them and kissed them. They said they were not angry, but they were disappointed. They said they should not fight over their toys, but share them and play nicely. They said they should say sorry to each other and make up.

Lily and Max looked at each other. They felt ashamed and sorry. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They said they liked each other and their toys. They said they would play together and have fun.

Mom and Dad smiled and praised them. They said they were proud of them and loved them. They said they would help them clean their toys and dry their clothes. They said they would make them some hot chocolate and cookies.

Lily and Max felt happy and warm. They thanked their mom and dad and followed them inside. They learned their lesson and became better friends. They decided to play with their toys together and have more fun.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the yard. They have a ball, a bike, and a kite. They take turns with the toys.

One day, Sara sees a new toy in the yard. It is a big orange truck. It has wheels, a horn, and a shovel. Sara wants to play with the truck. She runs to the truck and picks it up.

"Look, Ben, a truck!" Sara says. "It is orange and shiny. Can I play with it?"

Ben looks at the truck. He likes trucks too. He feels sad. He wants to play with the truck. He shakes his head.

"No, Sara, that is not your truck. That is Tom's truck. Tom is our neighbor. He left his truck in the yard. You have to give it back."

Sara does not want to give back the truck. She likes the truck. She holds the truck tight.

"But I want to play with it, Ben. It is so fun. Please, let me play with it."

Ben thinks for a moment. He wants to be a good friend. He wants to make Sara happy. He has an idea.

"Okay, Sara, you can play with the truck. But only for a little while. Then we have to give it back to Tom. And we have to share the truck. You can have the shovel, and I can have the horn. Deal?"

Sara smiles. She likes Ben's idea. She nods her head.

"Deal, Ben. Thank you for sharing. You are a good friend."

Sara and Ben play with the truck. They have fun. They make noises with the horn and the shovel. They dig and dump dirt. They laugh and giggle.

"Yeah, sorry, Tom, we didn't mean to take your truck. We just wanted to try it. It is a very cool truck. We had fun with it." Ben says.

Tom looks at Sara and Ben. He sees their faces. They look sincere. He feels happy. He has an idea.

"That's okay, Sara and Ben. I don't mind. You can play with my truck. But only if you let me play with your toys. Can I play with your ball, your bike, and your kite? Deal?"

"Deal, Tom. Thank you for letting us play with your truck. You are a good neighbor."

Sam and Ben were brothers. They lived on a farm with their mom and dad. They had many animals, like cows, pigs, and chickens. They also grew corn in a big field.

One day, a man came to their farm. He wore a suit and a hat. He had a big car. He was rich. He said to their dad, "I want to buy your corn. I will pay you a lot of money."

Their dad was happy. He said, "OK, you can have my corn. But you have to leave some for my family. We need corn to eat and to feed our animals."

The man nodded. He said, "Sure, sure. I will leave some corn for you. Don't worry." He smiled, but he was lying.

The next day, the man came back with a big truck. He and his workers loaded all the corn into the truck. They did not leave any corn for Sam and Ben's family. They took all the corn.

Sam and Ben saw what was happening. They ran to their dad. They said, "Dad, dad, the man is taking all our corn! He is not leaving any for us!"

Their dad was angry. He ran to the man. He said, "Hey, you, stop! You said you would leave some corn for us! You lied to me!"

The man laughed. He said, "Too bad, farmer. I want all your corn. I don't care about you or your family. I am rich, and you are poor. Now, get out of my way, or I will call the police."

He got into his car and drove away. He left Sam and Ben's family with no corn. They had nothing to eat and nothing to feed their animals. They were hungry and sad. The man was mean and greedy. He did not care about anyone but himself. He had a lot of corn, but he had no friends.

The squirrel did not answer. It was scared of the children. It ran away and dropped the nut. The nut fell down and hit Mom on the head.

"Ouch!" Mom said.

Sara and Tom heard Mom's voice. They looked down and saw Mom rubbing her head. They felt sorry and scared.

"Mom, are you okay?" Tom asked.

"Yes, I'm okay. But you are not. You should not climb so high. You could have dropped and hurt yourself. Come down right now." Mom said.

"I know, children. But you have to be careful and listen to me. Climbing trees is not safe for you. You can see the sky and the squirrel from the ground. They are still pretty and cute." Mom said.

Sara and Tom learned their lesson. They did not climb trees anymore. They played on the grass and watched the sky and the squirrel. They were happy and safe. Mom was happy and proud.

The moral of the story is: Listen to your friends who care about you and do not do dangerous things that can hurt you.

"What did we do?" Anna asked.

Anna and Ben felt sorry. They wished they had shared. They wished they had listened. They hugged each other. They said sorry.

"Maybe we can fix the toy," Anna said.

"Maybe we can ask for help," Ben said.

They took the toy to their mom. They told her what happened. They asked her to help them. Mom was not happy. She was disappointed. But she was also kind. She said she would try to fix the toy. She said she hoped they learned their lesson. She said she loved them.

Anna and Ben thanked their mom. They promised to be smart. They promised to share. They promised to listen. They hoped their toy would work again. They hoped they could play with it together. They hoped they could have fun.

One day, when mom and dad were out, Tom and Anna decided to try the switch. They got a chair and a broom and climbed up. Tom held the broom and Anna pushed the buttons. First she pushed the red button. Nothing happened. Then she pushed the green button. Nothing happened. Then she pushed both buttons at the same time.

She also showed them a sign that said "stop", and explained that it meant to stop and look both ways before moving on. She said that if they followed the signs, they would have more fun and avoid accidents.

Ben and Sam liked the picture and put it on the floor. They took their cars and started to drive on the road. John felt his feet pushing off the ground as the comet lifted him higher and higher into the sky. The world below looked so small and he felt dizzy again, but he knew he was having the time of his life.

But Mama had warned them not to touch the peppers. She said they were very hot and would make their mouths hurt. She said they were only for grown-ups who liked spicy food. Lily and Ben remembered Mama's words, but they were curious and hungry.

They decided to take a small bite of the pepper, just to see how it tasted. They pulled the pepper from the plant and broke it in half. They each took a piece and put it in their mouths. As soon as they did, they felt a burning sensation on their tongues. They spit out the pepper and cried out loud. Their mouths were on fire and their eyes were watery. They ran to the house, looking for Mama and some water.

Mama heard their cries and came to see what was wrong. She saw the pepper in their hands and understood what had happened. She felt sorry for them, but also a little angry. She gave them some water and some honey to soothe their mouths. She hugged them and said, "I told you not to touch the peppers. They are not for children. They are too hot and dangerous. Lily and Ben nodded and said they were sorry. They learned their lesson and never touched the peppers again. They realized that Mama was right and that they should trust her. One day, a little boy and his dad went to the zoo. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and birds. The boy liked the animals, but he wanted to see his favorite one: the leopard.

Suddenly, the leopard jumped off the rock and ran to the cage bars. It made a loud roar and showed its sharp teeth. The boy was scared and hid behind his dad. The dad hugged him and said, "Don't worry, the leopard can't hurt you. It's just trying to scare us away. It thinks we are in its territory."

The boy peeked at the leopard, who was still roaring and scratching the bars. He saw that the leopard had a big cut on its ear. He felt sorry for the leopard, and he wondered how it got hurt.

The dad saw the cut too, and he said, "Maybe the leopard had a fight with another leopard, and they split its ear. That's why it's angry and sad. It needs a friend to make it feel better."

The boy nodded, and he said, "Maybe we can be its friends. We can give it some food and a toy, and talk to it nicely. Maybe then it will stop roaring and be happy."

The dad smiled, and he said, "That's a good idea. Let's go and find a zookeeper, and ask if we can do that. Maybe the leopard will like us, and we can come and visit it again."

The boy smiled too, and he said, "Yes, let's do that. I like the leopard, even if it's scary. I want to help it."

They held hands and walked away from the cage, looking for a zookeeper. The leopard watched them go, and it stopped roaring. It felt a little curious, and a little less lonely.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of kindness, patience, sharing, and learning from others. It also shows the consequences of being mean, selfish, and stubborn.

Foreshadowing or setup and payoff: The story foreshadows or sets up the sister's ability to kick the ball by having mom say, "Maybe she will surprise you and kick the ball very well. You never know until you try." The payoff is when the sister does kick the ball very well and impresses her brothers.

Lily said, "Hello, deer! Do you like the food?" The deer looked up and nodded its head. Lily was very happy that the deer liked the food. 

After the deer finished eating, it ran away into the forest. Lily said, "Goodbye, deer! Come back soon!" And the deer looked back and waved its tail. It was a happy day for Lily and her family.

One day, Kayla noticed that her pepper wasn't feeling well. Its leaves were drooping and it had a sad look on its face. Kayla wanted to make the pepper feel better, so she asked it, "What's wrong, pepper?" 

The pepper replied "I'm feeling a bit lonely. I want a friend to keep me company."

Kayla thought for a while, then she smiled. She had an idea! She began to dig in the garden and soon she had made a safe place for a new pepper. 

When she was finished, Kayla looked at her pet pepper and said, "There, now you will have a friend - you can no longer frown!" 

The pepper was so happy! From that day forward, the two peppers were always by each other's side.

So, Pip sang a beautiful song for the mouse. The mouse loved the song and slowly came out from behind the bush. Pip and the mouse became good friends and played together every day.

The moral of the story is that sometimes, we just need to be patient and kind to others, even if they are shy or different from us. And, if we share our talents and gifts with others, we can make new friends and have fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little squirrel named Nutty. Nutty loved to eat nuts, but one day he found a really tough nut that he couldn't crack open. He tried and tried, but it hurt his teeth. 

Nutty was sad because he really wanted to eat the nut. But then he had an idea! He went to his friend, the bird, and asked for help. The bird had a sharp beak and was able to crack open the tough nut for Nutty to eat. 

From that day on, Nutty knew that if he ever found a tough nut again, he could prevent hurting his teeth by asking for help from his friends. And he lived happily ever after, eating lots of yummy nuts!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went outside to play and she saw a lizard on a rock. The lizard was green and had a long tail. Lily smiled and said hello to the lizard. But the lizard didn't say anything back, it just sat there and looked at her.

Lily tried to pick up the lizard, but it was too fast and ran away. Lily was sad and started to frown. She wanted to play with the lizard. But then, she saw a stick on the ground. The stick was flexible, so she picked it up and started to play with it. She pretended that the stick was the lizard and she was very happy.

From that day on, Lily played with the flexible stick and pretended it was a lizard. She never saw the real lizard again, but she was still happy because she had her flexible stick. And whenever she felt sad, she would remember the lizard and how it made her frown, but then she would smile because she had her flexible stick. The end.

Max was surprised but he agreed. And from that day on, Spot and Max became good friends. Spot learned that it's important to stand up for yourself but also to be kind and gentle.

One day, Lily and Ben were playing in their room. They had many toys, but they liked to play with the mirror best. The mirror was big and shiny, and they could see themselves in it.

"Look, Lily, I can make a funny face!" Ben said, and he stuck out his tongue and crossed his eyes. Lily laughed and copied him.

"Look, Ben, I can make a funny nose!" Lily said, and she pinched her nose and made a squeaky sound. Ben giggled and copied her.

They took turns making funny faces and noises, and the mirror showed them how silly they looked. They had so much fun, they did not hear their mom calling them for lunch.

"Come on, kids, it's time to eat!" Mom said, and she opened the door. She saw Lily and Ben in front of the mirror, and smiled. "What are you doing?"

"We are playing with the mirror, Mom!" Lily and Ben said together.

"That's nice, but you have to be careful. The mirror can break, and then you will have no mirror to play with." Mom said.

"We will be careful, Mom. We promise." Lily and Ben said.

Mom nodded and left them to finish their game. But as soon as she was gone, Lily and Ben had a new idea.

"Let's split the mirror, Lily!" Ben said.

"What do you mean, Ben?" Lily asked.

"Let's move the mirror, so we can see half of our faces. Then we will look even funnier!" Ben said.

"OK, let's try it!" Lily said.

They pushed the mirror from one side, and then from the other. They saw half of their faces, and they laughed harder.

"Look, Lily, I have one eye and one ear!" Ben said.

"Look, Ben, I have one mouth and one cheek!" Lily said.

They pushed the mirror more and more, until it was almost falling off the wall. They did not notice the crack that was forming in the middle of the mirror.

"Look, Lily, I have no nose!" Ben said.

"Look, Ben, I have no chin!" Lily said.

They pushed the mirror one last time, and then they heard a loud sound. The mirror split in two, and fell to the floor. The pieces were sharp and shiny, and they cut their feet.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily and Ben cried.

Mom heard the noise and ran to their room. She saw the broken mirror and the blood on the floor. She was very angry and very scared.

"What have you done, Lily and Ben? You broke the mirror, and you hurt yourselves! How could you be so careless?" Mom said.

"We are sorry, Mom. We were playing with the mirror, and we wanted to split it. We did not mean to break it, or to cut ourselves. We were having fun, Mom." Lily and Ben said.

"Fun? That was not fun, that was dangerous. You could have hurt yourselves badly, or even worse. You know the mirror is not a toy, and you should not touch it. You have to be more careful, and listen to me. Now come with me, I have to clean your wounds and put some bandages on them." Mom said.

She took Lily and Ben to the bathroom, and washed their feet. She put some cream and some bandages on them, and gave them a hug.

"I love you, Lily and Ben, but you have to be more responsible. Next time, play with something else, OK?" Mom said.

"OK, Mom. We love you too. We are sorry, Mom." Lily and Ben said.

They learned their lesson, and they never played with the mirror again. They found other toys to have fun with, and they always listened to Mom.

Soon, he hopped into a dry and dusty field, where there was no water and no shade. He felt hot and thirsty, and his tongue was dry. He looked around and saw that he was alone. He did not see the fly anymore. He did not see the pond anymore. He did not see his friends anymore. He felt scared and lonely.

He realized that he had made a big mistake. He had wasted his time and energy chasing something he could not have, and he had lost something he needed and loved. He wished he had been happy with what he had, and not greedy for what he did not.

He hoped he could find his way back to the pond, where he belonged. He hoped he could see his friends again, and play with them. He hoped he could find some water, and drink it. He hoped he could find some flies, and eat them. But he knew it would be difficult.

He learned a valuable lesson that day. He learned that flying is not everything, and that hopping is not nothing. He learned that being fast and smart is not enough, and that being slow and clumsy is not bad. He learned that being happy with what you have is better than being unhappy with what you don't. He learned that hopping is fun, and that flies are tasty. He learned that he was a frog, and that he liked being a frog.

Amy shook her head. She said, "No, I don't want to see them. You should not play with matches and fuel. They can cause a big fire. You should give them to a grown-up. Come on, let's play something else."

Tim felt angry. He said, "No, you are boring. You don't understand me. I don't want to play with you. Go away."

Amy felt sad. She said, "OK, fine. I will go away. But you should be careful. Fire is not a toy. It can be your enemy."

She walked away. Tim did not care. He ran to his home. He took his matches and fuel. He went to his backyard. He poured some fuel on the grass. He lit a match. He threw it on the fuel. He watched the fire grow. He laughed.

He did not see his mom coming out of the house. She smelled the smoke. She saw the fire. She saw Tim. She screamed.

She ran to Tim. She tried to pull him away. But it was too late. The fire was too big. It reached the house. It reached the can of fuel. It exploded.

Tim and his mom were gone. The house was gone. The fire was gone. Only ashes and smoke were left.

The moral of the story is: Do not play with fire. Fire can be your friend, but it can also be your enemy. Fire can take away everything you have and love. Fire can end your life. Be smart and safe. Listen to others who care about you. Make good choices.

As the bird flew away, it saw a group of animals. The animals were having a race. They were trying to see who could run the fastest. The bird watched and judged who was the winner. The winner was a rabbit who was very fast. The other animals seemed a bit sad that they didn't win, but the bird told them they did a good job and it was fun to play together.

"Let's play with this!" Tom said, and picked up the gun.

"No, Tom, that is not a toy. That is a bad thing. It can hurt you and me and others. Put it back!" Sam said, and tried to take the gun from Tom.

But Tom did not listen. He wanted to keep the gun and play with it. He pushed Sam away and ran outside with the gun. He saw a bird on a tree and pointed the gun at it. He pulled the trigger and made a loud bang.

The bird fell down from the tree and did not move. Tom was scared and sad. He did not mean to hurt the bird. He dropped the gun and ran back to Sam.

"Sam, I am sorry. I did a bad thing. I hurt the bird. I should have listened to you. You are a good friend. You are modest and smart. You know what is right and wrong. Can you forgive me?" Tom said, and hugged Sam.

Sam was angry and sad, too. He liked the bird and did not want it to die. But he saw that Tom was sorry and did not know better. He hugged Tom back and said, "It is okay, Tom. I forgive you. Tom nodded and said, "I promise, Sam. Thank you for being my friend. I will do what you say. And I will never play with the gun again. I will only play with toys that are safe and fun."

The moral of the story is: Guns are not toys. They are dangerous and can hurt people and animals. We should listen to our friends who are modest and smart and know what is right and wrong. We should also tell the truth and say sorry when we make a mistake.

One day, she found a book that had a picture of a wire on the cover. She wondered what a wire was and what it could do. She opened the book and started to read. The book told her that a wire was a thin and long piece of metal that could carry electricity. The book also showed her how to make a simple circuit with a wire, a battery and a light bulb.

Lily was very excited and wanted to try it herself. She asked her mom if she could have a wire, a battery and a light bulb. Her mom said yes, but she also told her to be careful and not to touch the wire when it was connected to the battery. Lily said she understood and thanked her mom.

Lily went to her room and followed the instructions in the book. She connected the wire to the battery and the light bulb. She was amazed when the light bulb lit up. She felt very happy and proud. She wanted to show her mom what she had done.

She ran to the living room where her mom was sitting on the couch. She held the wire, the battery and the light bulb in her hands. She said, "Mom, look what I made! I read a book about wires and I made a light!"

Her mom smiled and said, "That's wonderful, Lily! You are very smart and curious. I'm proud of you for reading and learning new things. But be careful, don't touch the wire. It can hurt you if it has electricity."

Lily nodded and said, "I know, mom. I won't touch the wire. I just want to show you how it works."

She put the wire, the battery and the light bulb on the coffee table. She said, "See, mom, when I connect the wire to the battery, the light bulb lights up. And when I disconnect the wire, the light bulb goes off. It's like magic!"

Her mom said, "That's very cool, Lily. But do you know what's more amazing than magic?"

Lily said, "What, mom?"

Her mom said, "Compassion. Compassion is when you care about other people and animals and help them when they are sad or hurt. Compassion is more amazing than magic because it can make the world a better place. Do you know what compassion means, Lily?"

Lily thought for a moment and said, "Is it like when I share my books with my friends? Or when I hug you when you are tired? Or when I feed the birds in the garden?"

Her mom said, "Yes, Lily, those are all examples of compassion. You are very compassionate, Lily. And that makes me even more proud of you than your light. I love you, Lily."

Lily said, "I love you too, mom. And I love to read books. And I love to be compassionate."

They hugged each other and smiled. Lily learned a new word and a new value that day. She learned that reading can teach her many things, but compassion can touch many hearts.

Mia wakes up and looks at the wall. She sees the shadow too. She is not scared. She is smart and she knows what it is. She smiles and says, "Ben, that is not a monster. That is our teddy bear. He is on the shelf and the sun makes his shadow. See, he is helpful. He keeps us company and he makes us laugh."

Ben looks at the shelf and sees the teddy bear. He feels silly and he laughs too. He says, "You are right, Mia. That is our teddy bear. He is helpful and he is funny. He is not a monster. He is our friend."

They hug the teddy bear and they get up. They are happy and they are ready for a new day. They say, "Thank you, teddy bear, for being helpful and making us laugh. We love you."

Lila and Tom are twins. They like to play in the park with their mom. One day, they see a big slide. Lila wants to go on it, but Tom is scared.

"Come on, Tom, it's fun!" Lila says. "You can slide down fast and feel the wind in your hair."

"No, Lila, it's too high. I might fall and hurt myself. I want to stay on the swings. They are safe and cozy." Tom says.

Lila shrugs and runs to the slide. She climbs up the ladder and stretches her arms. She feels brave and happy. She slides down with a whoop and lands on the sand. She does it again and again.

Tom watches her from the swings. He feels a little jealous and a little curious. He wonders what it feels like to slide down. He thinks maybe he can try it once. He gets off the swing and walks to the slide. He looks up and feels his heart beat fast. He climbs up the ladder slowly and carefully. He reaches the top and sits on the edge. He looks down and feels his stomach flip. He wants to go back, but he can't. He is stuck.

"Help, Lila, help!" Tom cries. "I'm scared! I can't slide down!"

Lila hears him and runs to the slide. She sees him and smiles. She has an idea. She climbs up the ladder again and sits behind him. She wraps her arms around him and whispers in his ear.

"Don't worry, Tom, I'm here. You are not alone. We can slide down together. It will be fun. Trust me. You are lucky to have a sister like me." She says.

Tom feels her hug and hears her voice. He feels a little better. He nods and holds her hand. They slide down together and feel the wind in their hair. They land on the sand and laugh. They hug each other and feel proud.

"Wow, Lila, that was amazing! Thank you for helping me. You are the best sister ever." Tom says.

"You're welcome, Tom. You are very brave. I'm glad you tried it. You are the best brother ever." Lila says.

They run to their mom and tell her what they did. She smiles and hugs them. She tells them they are both lucky and safe. They agree and feel happy. They play some more in the park and have a great day.

Lily and Ben were playing with their blocks. They liked to make different shapes with them, like squares, triangles and circles. Lily made a big tower with her blocks, and Ben made a long train.

"Look at my tower, Ben!" Lily said. "It is so tall and strong. It is the best shape ever!"

Ben looked at Lily's tower and felt envious. He wanted to have a tower like that too. He thought his train was boring and small. He decided to do something naughty. He pushed his train towards Lily's tower and crashed into it. The blocks fell down and made a loud noise.

"Ben, why did you do that?" Lily cried. "You broke my tower! That was not nice!"

Ben felt a little sorry, but he also felt happy. He thought he had made a better shape with the blocks. He smiled and said, "My train is better than your tower. It can move and make sounds. Your tower can only stand there and yawn."

Lily was very angry and sad. She did not want to play with Ben anymore. She picked up her blocks and moved to another corner of the room. She started to make a new shape with them, but she did not have fun.

Their mom came in and saw what had happened. She was not happy either. She asked them what was wrong and why they were not playing together. Lily and Ben told her their stories.

Mom shook her head and said, "Lily and Ben, you are both wrong. There is no best shape. All shapes are good and different. You should not be envious of each other's shapes. You should be proud of your own shapes and share them with each other. You should also be kind and respectful to each other's shapes. You should not break them or hurt them. That is not how you play with blocks. That is how you lose friends."

Lily and Ben felt ashamed and realized their mom was right. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They decided to play with their blocks together again. They made new shapes and mixed them up. They had fun and learned to appreciate each other's shapes. They also learned to be good friends.

Tom and Mia were having lunch with Mom. They had yummy soup and bread. Mom gave them each a spoon and a fork. Tom liked to use his fork to poke the bread. Mia liked to use her spoon to scoop the soup.

"Tom, please use your spoon for the soup," Mom said. "The fork is for the salad."

"But I like the fork," Tom said. "It is fun and shiny."

Mia looked at her fork. It was clean and silver. She wanted to try it too. She put her spoon down and picked up her fork. She dipped it in the soup and lifted it to her mouth.

"Oops!" Mia said. The soup dripped from the fork and spilled on her shirt. She felt wet and sticky. She did not like it.

"Mia, what are you doing?" Mom asked. "The fork is not good for the soup. It makes a mess. Use your spoon, please."

Mia nodded. She put the fork down and picked up the spoon. She wiped her shirt with a napkin. She felt better.

"Sorry, Mom," Mia said. "I wanted to try the fork like Tom."

"That's okay, Mia," Mom said. "But the fork is for the salad. The spoon is for the soup. They have different jobs. Do you understand?"

"Yes, Mom," Mia and Tom said. They used their spoons for the soup and their forks for the salad. They ate their lunch and enjoyed it. They returned their spoons and forks to the sink. Mom was happy. She praised them for being good and clean.

"How do we ask the tree, Mom?" Lily asked.

"You have to touch the trunk gently and say hello. Then you have to listen to the tree. It will tell you if it is happy or sad, if it is tired or strong, if it wants to play or rest. The tree has a voice, but it is very soft and slow. You have to be quiet and patient to hear it." Mom said.

Lily and Tom nodded and ran to the tree. They touched the trunk gently and said hello. They listened to the tree. They heard a faint rustle of the leaves and a low hum of the wood. They felt a warm and friendly feeling in their hearts.

Moral: Happiness is not in having more things, but in having fun and sharing with others.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tree with many fruits. They are peaches. They are round and soft and sweet.

Lily and Ben want to pick some peaches. They ask their moms if they can. Their moms say yes, but be careful. Lily and Ben climb the tree. They are very happy. They pick some peaches and put them in a basket.

They see a lady on a bench. She is reading a book. She looks busy. Lily and Ben want to share their peaches with her. They go to the bench. They say hello. They offer her a peach. They say, this is for you. We picked it from the tree.

The lady smiles. She says thank you. She takes the peach. She says, you are very kind. She bites the peach. She says, it is very juicy and yummy. She says, do you want some of my book? She shows them the book. It has many pictures and words.

Lily and Ben say yes. They sit on the bench with the lady. They look at the book. They learn new things. They have fun. They are very happy. They make a new friend.

Ben likes to match his pants with his shirt. He has many pants and shirts in different colors. He can make red and red, blue and blue, or green and green. He thinks matching is fun and easy.

One day, Ben goes to the park with his mom. He sees a boy with a big bike and a shiny watch. The boy wears pants and a shirt that do not match. His pants are yellow and his shirt is purple. Ben thinks the boy looks funny and silly.

Ben runs to the boy and says, "Your pants and shirt do not match. You should wear the same color. Matching is good." The boy looks at Ben and says, "I do not care about matching. I wear what I want. I am rich. I have a big bike and a shiny watch. You are poor. You have a small bike and no watch. Rich is better than matching."

Ben feels sad and angry. He does not like the boy. He likes his small bike and his matching clothes. He thinks rich is not better than matching. He says, "I do not want to be your friend. You are mean and rude. Matching is better than rich. Matching is fun and easy. Rich is boring and hard."

Ben runs back to his mom and tells her what happened. His mom hugs him and says, "I am proud of you, Ben. You are smart and kind. You do not need to be rich to be happy. You have what you need. You have a bike, a watch, and many pants and shirts that match. You also have me, and I love you very much." Ben smiles and says, "I love you too, mom. You are the best. Can we go home and match some more?" His mom says, "Yes, we can. Let's go home and match some more." They leave the park and go home, happy and matching.

Anna loves to perform. She likes to sing and dance and make people happy. She has a big show today at her school. She is very excited.

She puts on her pretty dress and her shiny shoes. She brushes her hair and puts on a bow. She looks in the mirror and smiles. She is ready to perform.

She goes to the school with her mom and dad. They give her a hug and a kiss. They tell her they are proud of her. They help her find her seat in the big hall. She sits with her friends and waits for her turn.

She hears her name on the loud speaker. She gets up and walks to the stage. She sees many people in the hall. She sees her mom and dad. They wave at her and smile. She feels happy and brave.

She sings her song and dances her dance. She performs very well. She hears people clap and cheer. She bows and says thank you. She goes back to her seat. She feels proud and happy. She did a great job.

She hugs her friends and her teacher. They tell her she was amazing. She waits for the show to end. She sees other kids perform. They are all good and fun. She claps and cheers for them.

The show is over. She gets her coat and her bag. She meets her mom and dad. They hug her and kiss her. They tell her they loved her performance. They tell her she is a star. They take her hand and walk to the car. They buckle her up and make her safe. They drive home and talk about the show. She feels happy and loved. She had a great day.

Tim and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big house with a fence. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's go there," Tim said.

"No, we can't," Lily said. "Mom said to stay in the park. And that house looks scary. Maybe a witch lives there."

Tim did not listen. He was brave and curious. He climbed over the fence and ran to the house. He knocked on the door.

"Who is it?" a voice said. It was old and mean.

"It's me, Tim," Tim said.

The door opened. A woman with a long nose and a black hat stood there. She was a witch. She smiled and said, "Hello, Tim. Do you want to come in? I have some candy for you."

Tim liked candy. He forgot about Lily and the park. He said, "Yes, please."

The witch grabbed him and pulled him inside. She locked the door. She said, "You are not here for candy. You are here for my dinner. You are fit and tasty. I will cook you in my pot."

Tim was scared. He cried and shouted, "Help! Help! Lily, help me!"

Lily heard him. She was worried. She ran to the fence and saw the witch's house. She saw the door was locked. She looked for a way to get in. She saw a window. It was small, but she was fit and thin. She climbed over the fence and ran to the window. She pushed it open and crawled inside.

She saw Tim in a cage. She saw the witch with a big pot. She said, "Let Tim go! He is my friend. You are a bad witch!"

The witch laughed and said, "No, I won't. He is my dinner. And you are too. You are fit and sweet. I will cook you both in my pot."

Lily was brave and smart. She saw a broom. She picked it up and swung it at the witch. She hit her on the head. The witch fell down and dropped the key. Lily ran to the cage and unlocked it. She freed Tim and said, "Come on, let's go!"

Tim and Lily ran to the window and crawled out. They ran to the fence and climbed over. They ran to the park and hugged each other. They were safe and happy. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We will never go to the witch's house again. We will always stay in the park."

Tom and Anna were twins who liked to play in their big house. They had many toys and books and games, and they felt very happy. They had a lot of luxury, which means they had more things than they needed.

One day, their mom told them to share their toys with their cousins, who were coming to visit. Tom and Anna did not like this idea. They wanted to keep their toys for themselves. They thought their cousins were noisy and messy and rude. They decided to hide their toys in their rooms, and spread them all over the floor and the bed.

When their cousins arrived, they ran to Tom and Anna's rooms, hoping to find some fun things to play with. But they were very disappointed. They saw only a mess of toys that Tom and Anna did not want to share. They felt angry and sad. They told their mom and dad what Tom and Anna did.

Their mom and dad were not happy either. They scolded Tom and Anna for being selfish and unkind. They told them to clean up their rooms and apologize to their cousins. They also took away some of their toys and gave them to their cousins as a gift.

Tom and Anna felt very sorry for what they did. They realized they had been mean and foolish. They learned that sharing is better than hoarding, and that playing with others is more fun than playing alone. They hugged their cousins and said they were sorry. They also invited them to play with their toys together. Their cousins forgave them and smiled. They all had a playful time, and became good friends.

Lila is a princess who likes to number her toys. She has a lot of toys, but her favorite is a big bear. She puts a sticker with a one on the bear's nose. Then she numbers her dolls, her blocks, her books, and her cars.

One day, a bad man comes to the castle. He wants to take Lila's toys. He sneaks into her room when she is not there. He sees the bear with the one on its nose. He thinks it is a special toy. He grabs it and runs away.

But the bear is alert. It sees the bad man and makes a loud roar. Lila hears the roar and runs to her room. She sees the bad man with her bear. She is very angry. She shouts, "Stop! That is my bear! Give it back!"

The bad man is scared of Lila and the bear. He drops the bear and runs out of the castle. Lila hugs her bear and thanks it for being alert. She says, "You are my number one toy. I love you, bear." The bear smiles and roars again. Lila and the bear are happy.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toy trains on the floor. They liked to make them go fast and make noises. Lily had a red train and Ben had a blue train. They pretended that their trains were going to different places.

"Look, my train is going to the zoo!" Lily said. She pointed to a picture of a lion on the wall. "Roar!"

"My train is going to the mountain!" Ben said. He pointed to a pillow that he put on the floor. "Choo-choo!"

They played for a while, until they heard a loud whistle from outside. They ran to the window and saw a large train passing by. It was black and shiny, and it had steam coming out of its chimney. They were amazed by the sight.

"Wow, look at that train!" Lily said. "It's so big and strong!"

"It's so cool and fast!" Ben said. "It makes a lot of steam!"

They watched the train until it disappeared in the distance. Then they looked at each other and smiled.

"Let's play with our trains again!" Lily said.

"OK, but let's share them!" Ben said. "We can take turns to play with the red and the blue train!"

They agreed and went back to their toys. They learned that trains are fun, but sharing is even more fun.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw some older kids near the park. The older kids had sticks that made smoke. They put the sticks in their mouths and blew out the smoke. Lily and Tom thought the smoke looked cool and wanted to try it.

They went to the older kids and asked them if they could have some sticks. The older kids laughed and said no. They said the sticks were not for little kids. They said the sticks were called cigarettes and they made them feel good. They said Lily and Tom were too young and silly to understand.

Lily and Tom felt sad and angry. They wanted to feel good too. They thought the older kids were mean and rude. They decided to sneak away and find some cigarettes somewhere else. They looked around and saw a trash can near the street. They saw some cigarettes that were not burned all the way. They grabbed them and ran to a hidden spot behind a tree.

They put the cigarettes in their mouths and tried to light them with a match. They did not know how to do it right. They coughed and choked on the smoke. They felt sick and dizzy. They did not feel good at all. They felt scared and sorry.

A man who was walking by saw the smoke and the kids. He ran to them and took away the cigarettes and the match. He was very angry and worried. He shouted at them and asked them what they were doing. He said they were very naughty and stupid. He said they could have hurt themselves or started a fire. He said he would tell their parents and they would be in big trouble.

Lily and Tom cried and begged him not to tell. They said they were sorry and they would never do it again. They said they only wanted to try something new. They said they did not know it was so bad. The man did not listen. He did not permit them to go. He took them by the hand and dragged them to their homes. He told their parents everything. Their parents were very angry and sad. They scolded them and punished them. They said they were very disappointed and ashamed. They said they could not trust them anymore.

Lily and Tom felt very bad. They wished they had never seen the smoke. They wished they had never been so curious and lazy. They wished they had listened to the older kids and stayed away. They wished they had played something else. They learned a hard lesson that day. They never touched cigarettes again.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play with toys. They had many toys, but they always wanted more. One day, they saw a big box in the living room. They thought it was a new toy for them, so they ran to open it.

But when they opened the box, they were disappointed. It was not a toy, but a wire. A long, thin, metal wire that their dad needed for his work. It looked boring and useless to them. They sighed and threw the wire on the floor.

Then they went to look for other toys to play with. But they could not find any. They had played with all their toys so many times that they were bored of them. They sighed again and sat on the couch.

Their mom saw them and asked them what was wrong. They told her that they had no toys to play with and that the wire in the box was boring. Their mom smiled and said, "Why don't you use your imagination? The wire can be anything you want it to be. You can bend it, twist it, shape it, and make it into something fun. You just have to be creative and try."

Tom and Lily looked at each other and decided to give it a try. They picked up the wire and started to play with it. They made it into a snake, a necklace, a crown, a bracelet, a ring, a car, a plane, a star, and many other things. They had so much fun that they forgot about their other toys. They laughed and smiled and thanked their mom for the idea.

Their mom hugged them and said, "You're welcome, my loves. I'm glad you learned that you don't need many toys to have fun. You just need your imagination and your creativity. And sometimes, the most boring things can be the most fun things, if you look at them differently."

Ben and Sam are brothers. They like to play with their toy jeep. It is red and big and has four wheels. They pretend it is a real jeep and they go on adventures.

One day, they see a shiny car in the street. It is a limo. It is very long and black and has a driver. They think it belongs to someone rich. They want to see who is inside.

"Let's follow the limo with our jeep!" Ben says. "Maybe we can catch a glimpse of the rich person!"

"OK!" Sam agrees. They hop on their jeep and start to pedal. They follow the limo at a safe distance. They are very curious and excited.

The limo stops at a big house with a gate. The driver gets out and opens the door. Ben and Sam pedal faster to catch up. They see a man in a suit and a woman in a dress get out of the limo. They are holding hands and smiling.

"Wow, they look so happy and rich!" Ben says.

"Maybe they are movie stars!" Sam says.

They are about to get closer when they hear a loud bark. A big dog runs out of the house and towards them. It has sharp teeth and a mean face. It does not like strangers.

"Uh-oh, it's a guard dog!" Ben says. "We have to get away!"

They turn their jeep around and pedal as fast as they can. The dog chases them and tries to catch them. It is very scary.

"Help!" Ben and Sam scream.

They pedal and pedal until they reach their home. They jump off their jeep and run inside. They slam the door behind them. They are safe.

"That was a close call!" Ben says.

"Too close!" Sam says.

They hug each other and breathe hard. They are glad they have each other. They decide to play with their jeep inside from now on. They do not want to follow any more limos. They are happy with what they have.

Lily liked to play with her red bracelet. It was shiny and pretty and made a nice sound when she moved her arm. She got it from her grandma for her birthday and she loved it very much.

One day, she was playing with her bracelet in the garden when her big brother Tom came over. He saw the bracelet and wanted to have it.

"Give me that bracelet, Lily. It's mine now," he said, reaching for her arm.

"No, Tom. It's mine. Grandma gave it to me. Go away," Lily said, pulling her arm away.

Tom was angry and tried to grab the bracelet again. He was bigger and stronger than Lily and he thought he could take anything he wanted.

"Stop it, Tom. You're hurting me. Leave me alone," Lily cried, trying to run away.

But Tom was faster and he caught her. He snatched the bracelet from her wrist and ran away, laughing.

Lily was very sad and hurt. She ran to her mom and told her what happened.

Mom was not happy with Tom. She called him and scolded him.

"Tom, how could you do that to your sister? That was very mean and selfish of you. You should be ashamed of yourself. Give the bracelet back to Lily right now and apologize to her," she said.

Tom felt bad and realized he was wrong. He gave the bracelet back to Lily and said he was sorry.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong. I shouldn't have taken your bracelet. It's yours and it's very nice. Can you forgive me?" he said.

Lily was still upset, but she saw that Tom was sorry. She decided to forgive him and hugged him.

"Thank you, Tom. I forgive you. You're my brother and I love you. But don't take my things again, okay?" she said.

Tom nodded and hugged her back.

"Okay, Lily. I love you too. And I'm sorry. Can we play together now?" he said.

Lily smiled and nodded.

"Okay, Tom. We can play together. But let me wear my bracelet, okay?" she said.

Tom agreed and they went to play together in the garden. They both learned a lesson and became closer as siblings.

Tim and Lily liked to play in the garden. They had a big bucket and a small shovel. They used the shovel to fill the bucket with mud. They made mud pies and mud castles. They had a lot of fun.

One day, they saw a shiny car parked in front of their house. It was their aunt's car. She came to visit them. She had a big smile and a big bag. She said, "Hello, Tim and Lily! I have a surprise for you in the bag. Do you want to see?"

Tim and Lily ran to the car. They wanted to see the surprise. They left the bucket and the shovel in the garden. They did not see the cat.

The cat was curious. It saw the bucket and the shovel. It jumped into the bucket. It played with the mud. It made a big mess. It got mud all over its fur and the bucket.

Tim and Lily opened the bag. They saw two beautiful dolls. They had long hair and pretty dresses. They were expensive dolls. Tim and Lily were very happy. They thanked their aunt. They said, "We love the dolls! They are so nice!"

They wanted to show the dolls to their mom. They ran to the house. They did not see the cat.

She gasped. She said, "Oh, no! My car! My seat! My cat! What happened?"

Their aunt sighed. She said, "It's okay, Tim and Lily. I know you did not do it on purpose. But you should be more careful. Mud is fun, but it can also be dirty. And my car is expensive, and my cat is precious. You should respect them."

Tim and Lily nodded. They said, "We understand, aunt. We will respect them. We will help you clean them."

Sam and Lily liked to play in the park. They had a big ball that they could roll on the grass. One day, they saw a trail in the dirt. It looked like a snake had made it.

"Let's follow the trail!" Sam said. He picked up the ball and ran after it. Lily followed him. They wanted to see the snake.

The trail went into the bushes. Sam and Lily pushed the leaves aside and looked inside. They saw a long, shiny snake. It had black and yellow stripes. It looked at them with small, black eyes.

"Wow, it's so pretty!" Lily said. She reached out her hand to touch it.

"Stop, Lily!" Sam shouted. "It might bite you!"

The snake hissed and coiled up. It was angry. Sam and Lily got scared. They dropped the ball and ran away. The snake slithered after them.

"Help, help!" Sam and Lily cried. They ran back to the grass. They saw their mom and dad sitting on a bench. They ran to them and hugged them.

"What's wrong, kids?" Mom asked.

"We saw a snake! It chased us!" Lily said.

"Where is it?" Dad asked.

They pointed to the bushes. Dad got up and walked over. He looked inside. He saw the ball, but no snake.

"It's gone, kids. It was probably more scared of you than you were of it. But you should be careful. Some snakes can be dangerous. Don't touch them or follow them. Stay on the grass where it's safe," Dad said.

"Did you hear that, Lily? The caterpillar said 'rawr'!" Tom said.

The vendor said, "I don't know anything about that box, but I do have something that might help you open it." He gave Lily a small key. When she used the key to open the box, she found a beautiful necklace inside. She was so happy and thanked the vendor for his help.

From that day on, Lily loved to search for new things with her special key. She always remembered the kind vendor who helped her find the mysterious necklace.

She was having fun, but she did not notice that the sun was shining on her box of crayons. The crayons started to get soft and sticky. Some of them broke in half. Some of them melted together. Sara did not see what was happening to her crayons.

She finished her picture and was very proud of it. She wanted to show it to her mom. She picked up her box of crayons and was shocked. Her crayons were not crayons anymore. They were a big mess of colors and wax. They had melted in the sun.

Sara was very sad. She cried and ran to her mom. She showed her mom her picture and her box of crayons. Her mom hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Sara. Your picture is very pretty, but your crayons are ruined. Next time, don't leave them in the sun. They will melt."

Sara nodded and wiped her tears. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I didn't know. Can I have new crayons, please?" Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, Sara. You can have new crayons. But first, let's put your picture on the fridge. It's very fancy." Sara smiled and hugged her mom. She learned a new word and a new lesson. She never left her crayons in the sun again.

"Can we see the nest?" Lily asks. She wants to touch the nest.

"No, we can't see the nest. It is too high and too far. And we have to be polite. The nest is the bird's home. We don't want to bother them or scare them," mom says. She holds Lily's hand.

"Okay, mom. We are polite. We just look and listen," Lily says. She nods.

Ben and Lily look and listen to the birds. They see different colors and shapes. They hear different sounds and tunes. They are happy and curious.

"Mom, how do the birds make the nest?" Ben asks. He wonders how the birds can manage.

"They use their beaks and feet. They find sticks and leaves and other things. They weave them together. They make a cozy and safe place for their eggs and babies," mom says. She smiles.

"Wow, the birds are smart and strong. They can manage a lot," Ben says. He is impressed.

"Yes, they are. And they are also beautiful and musical. They can sing and fly. They are a gift from God," mom says. She hugs Ben and Lily.

Ben and Lily hug mom back. They thank God for the birds and the tree and the park. They enjoy the sunny day and the lovely sight and sound. They are polite and grateful.

It also saw that Mia was humble, and did not try to bother it. The leopard respected Mia, and it did not want to hurt her.

The leopard gave Mia a small nod, and Mia smiled. She felt a connection with the leopard, and she was happy. She thanked the leopard for being nice, and she waved goodbye. She hoped to see the leopard again, but she knew it was better to leave it alone. She learned that some animals are best admired from afar, and that being humble is a good way to make friends.

Their moms are not scared. They are amused. They tell Tom and Jen that the dead thing is not a rat or a bear. It is a pine cone. A pine cone is a part of the tree. It has seeds inside. The ants like to eat the seeds. That is why they make a line to the hole.

Tom and Jen are surprised. They did not know that a pine cone can look like a dead animal. They feel silly. They laugh with their moms. They learn something new. They still like to play in the park. But they do not go near the hole anymore.

Lily and Ben did not listen to mom. They wanted to play in the pool. They thought they could fix the leak themselves. They found some glue and tape in the garage. They put glue and tape on the hole. They thought they were clever.

"Help, mom!" Sam shouted. "We can't stop!"

Mom heard them and ran along the river bank. She saw a big waterfall ahead. She screamed and tried to reach them, but it was too late.

The raft went over the edge and fell into the air. Sam and Ben screamed too. They held each other tight. The raft crashed into the water below. It broke into pieces. Sam and Ben sank into the water. They did not come up.

Mom cried and cried. She could not save them. The river took them away. The raft was dead. Sam and Ben were dead. The sun was dry. Mom was alone.

They reach the top of the slide. Lily says, "Ready, set, go!" and they slide down together. Anna feels the wind in her hair and the sun on her face. She laughs and says, "Whee!" Lily laughs too and says, "See, it was fun!" They hug and go on the slide again and again.

Their mom watches them and smiles. She thinks, "Lily is a good sister. She helps Anna overcome her fears. She makes her feel safe and happy. Anna is a lucky sister. She has a funny and kind sister. They love each other very much."

The moral value of the story is that helping others is good and rewarding. The narrative uses foreshadowing or setup and payoff by showing how Lily helps Anna with many things before they go to the park, and how that helps Anna enjoy the slide. The verb "help", the noun "sister" and the adjective "funny" are used in the story.

Lily smiled and thought Jack was very attractive. They talked and laughed together. Jack caught a butterfly for Lily, and she was very happy. They became friends and promised to play again soon.

"No, I'm too tired. Let's just sit here," her daddy replied.

Lily was sad because she wanted to play with her daddy, but then she saw two boys fighting over a ball. She ran over to them and said, "Stop fighting! We can all play together."

And so, Lily and her daddy joined the boys and they had a great time playing together. Her daddy wasn't lazy anymore and Lily was happy because she got to spend time with her daddy and make new friends too.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her friends in the park. One day, Lily and her friends decided to have a race. They ran as fast as they could, and Lily won the race!

After the race, they sat down to rest. Lily's friend, Sarah, showed her a beautiful flute that she had just learned to play. Lily thought it sounded so pretty.

Suddenly, a little bird flew down and landed on Sarah's flute. The bird was harmless and just wanted to listen to the music. Lily and her friends were so happy to have a new friend to play with. They talked to the bird and asked if it wanted to race with them. The bird chirped happily and said yes!

Lily and her friends had so much fun playing with the bird and listening to Sarah's flute. They knew it was a day they would never forget.

Timmy felt very angry and wanted to tell the dog's owner how he felt, but he was too scared. Instead, he decided to draw a big, wide line around his next drawing so that the dog wouldn't step on it. From then on, Timmy made sure to draw wider and bigger so that his drawings would be safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. Jack loved to play outside in the big green field near his house. One day, Jack saw a big goose walking around the field. The goose had a shiny golden egg in its beak.

Jack thought the goose was very lucky to have such a pretty egg. He wanted to have it for himself. So, he followed the goose around the field, trying to catch it. But the goose was too fast for Jack.

Suddenly, Jack saw a big tree with a branch that was springy. He had an idea! He climbed up the tree and waited for the goose to come closer. When the goose was right under the tree, Jack jumped down and scared the goose. The goose dropped the golden egg and Jack caught it.

Jack was so happy to have the golden egg, but he realized he was not lucky like the goose. He had to work hard to catch it. From that day on, Jack learned that hard work can make you lucky too.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and teddy bears. One day, she was playing with her dolls when her mommy came into the room.

"Hi, Lily," said her mommy. "What are you doing?"

"I'm playing with my dolls," replied Lily.

"That's nice," said her mommy. "Can we discuss something for a moment?"

"Sure," said Lily.

"Do you know what a loop is?" asked her mommy.

Lily shook her head.

"A loop is like a circle," explained her mommy. "It goes around and around."

Lily thought about this for a moment. "That sounds fun," she said.

"It can be," said her mommy. "But sometimes, loops can be foolish. They don't go anywhere."

Lily nodded, understanding what her mommy meant. "I don't want to be foolish," she said.

"Good," said her mommy. "You're a smart girl, Lily."

Tommy laughed and said, "Silly Lily, acorns are not for us. They are for squirrels. Let's go and find some squirrels. Maybe they will share their acorns with us."

Tommy and Lily peeked inside the hole. They saw a furry gray animal with a long bushy tail. It was a squirrel. It had a red nose and watery eyes. It looked sick. It sneezed again. "Achoo, achoo, achoo!"

Tommy and Lily felt sorry for the squirrel. They wanted to help it. They said, "Hello, Mr. Squirrel. Are you okay? Why are you sneezing so much?"

The squirrel looked at them and said, "Hello, little ones. I'm not okay. I have a cold. I ate too many acorns. They made me sick. They are not good for me. They are too dry and dusty."

Tommy and Lily said, "Oh, no, Mr. Squirrel. That's not good. You need to drink some water and eat some fresh fruits. They are good for you. They are juicy and sweet."

The squirrel said, "Thank you, little ones. You are very kind and smart. Do you have any water and fruits for me?"

Tommy and Lily said, "Yes, we do. We have a bottle of water and some apples in our backpack. We will share them with you. Come out of the hole and we will give them to you."

The squirrel came out of the hole and followed Tommy and Lily. They gave him some water and some apples. He drank and ate them. He felt better. He stopped sneezing. He smiled and said, "Thank you, little ones. You are brilliant. You saved me. You are my friends."

Tommy and Lily smiled and said, "You're welcome, Mr. Squirrel. You are our friend too. We are happy that you feel better. Can we play with you?"

Tommy and Lily said, "Yay, that sounds fun. Let's play with the acorns."

Tom and Sue were at the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and look for shells. Mom and Dad said they could have a picnic later, but first they had to wait for the tide to go down.

"Why do we have to wait?" Tom asked.

"Because we want to find some oysters," Dad said. "Oysters are yummy and they live in the water. But when the water is too high, we can't see them or reach them. We have to wait until the water is low and then we can dig them out."

"What do oysters look like?" Sue asked.

"Oysters are round and hard and gray," Mom said. "They have a wide mouth that opens and closes. Inside, they have a soft part that we can eat. But we have to be careful, because sometimes they have a sharp thing inside that can hurt us. It's called a pearl."

"A pearl?" Tom and Sue said. They wanted to see a pearl. They wondered if it was shiny and pretty.

They waited and waited for the water to go down. They played with their toys and made a sandcastle. They watched the birds and the boats. They saw some crabs and some fish. But they did not see any oysters.

"Can we have the picnic now?" Tom asked. He was hungry and tired of waiting.

"Not yet," Dad said. "The water is still too high. We have to delay the picnic a little longer. Trust me, it will be worth it."

Tom and Sue sighed. They did not like to delay. They wanted to eat and see the oysters and the pearls.

Finally, the water was low enough. Dad took a bucket and a shovel and walked to the edge of the water. He started to dig in the sand and the rocks. He looked for oysters.

"Come on, kids, help me find some oysters," he said.

Tom and Sue ran to join him. They helped him dig and look. They found some oysters. They were round and hard and gray, just like Mom said. They had a wide mouth that opened and closed.

Dad put the oysters in the bucket. He opened one with a knife. He showed Tom and Sue the soft part inside.

"See, this is what we can eat," he said. "It's delicious. Do you want to try?"

Tom and Sue shook their heads. They did not want to eat the soft part. It looked slimy and gross.

"Maybe later," Mom said. "Let's see if there are any pearls inside."

Dad opened another oyster. He looked inside. He smiled.

"Look, kids, we found a pearl!" he said. He showed them a small, shiny, white thing. It was a pearl. It was beautiful.

Tom and Sue gasped. They wanted to touch the pearl. They wanted to keep it.

"Can we have it, Dad?" they asked.

"Sure, you can have it," Dad said. "It's a lucky find. You can share it or take turns with it. It's yours."

Tom and Sue were happy. They thanked Dad. They hugged the pearl. They forgot about the picnic. They forgot about the delay. They only cared about the pearl. They had found a treasure.

Betty was so happy! She was finally able to play with the hose. She sprayed the water all around in the garden, laughing as she played.

As they were leaving the store, Lily accidentally dropped her favorite toy. She didn't notice and kept walking. When she got home, she realized it was missing and started to cry again. Her mom suggested they go back to the store to look for it. They went back and luckily, someone had found her toy and put it in the lost and found. Lily was so happy to have her toy back and hugged it tight.
