Joe saw a wise old man sitting nearby. The old man smiled and said, "It looks like you need some help. I recommend you go soak your feet in the river to make them feel better." Joe thanked the wise old man for his advice and he decided to do as he recommended.

He walked to the river and dipped his feet in the cool water. Sure enough, the water helped to soothe the itch and made Joe feel better. He thanked the wise old man again and promised himself to never be so foolish next time.

After a few minutes, he heard a splash in the pond. He saw that his coffee had made the pond glow. Everywhere he put it, the coffee made everything shine and sparkle.

The man was so happy with his coffee, he decided to always take it outside and make everything around him glow.

She finally made it to her grandma's house. She told her what she had seen and her grandma agreed that it was too hot for the corn and that she should help it by giving it some water.

Tom and Sue were brother and sister. They lived in a big house with their mom and dad, who were very wealthy. They had many toys and clothes and books, but they were not happy. They always wanted more and more, and they never shared or said thank you.

One night, a fairy came to their room while they were sleeping. She saw how spoiled and selfish they were, and she decided to teach them a lesson. She sprinkled some magic powder on their heads and whispered, "When you wake up, you will see how it feels to have nothing."

The next morning, Tom and Sue opened their eyes and gasped. They were not in their big house anymore. They were in a small hut with a dirt floor and a leaky roof. They had no toys or clothes or books, only rags and sticks and stones. They were hungry and cold and scared.

"Where are we?" Tom cried. "What happened to our things?"

"I don't know," Sue sobbed. "Maybe we are dreaming."

They ran outside and looked around. They saw other children who were also poor and dirty, but they were smiling and playing and helping each other. They saw a boy who had only one shoe, but he gave it to a girl who had none. They saw a girl who had only a slice of bread, but she shared it with a boy who had none. They saw a boy who had only a broken toy, but he fixed it with a girl who had none.

"Hello," the boy with one shoe said to Tom and Sue. "Do you want to play with us?"

Tom and Sue shook their heads. They felt ashamed and sad. They realized how mean and greedy they had been, and how little they had cared for others. They wished they could go back to their big house and their mom and dad, and they promised to be better and kinder.

The fairy, who was watching from a tree, smiled. She waved her wand and said, "You have learned your lesson. Now you can go home, but don't forget what you have seen."

Tom and Sue blinked and found themselves back in their big house, in their cozy beds, with their toys and clothes and books. They hugged each other and thanked the fairy, who they could not see but they could hear.

"Thank you, fairy," they said. "We are sorry for being bad. We will share and say thank you and be happy with what we have."

The fairy nodded and flew away. She hoped that Tom and Sue would keep their promise, and that they would grow up to be good and generous and happy.

Lily was sad. She really wanted to play with the moon. She said, "But mom, the moon looks so fun and pretty. I want to touch it and hug it and laugh with it."

The moral of the story is: You can't always have what you want, but you can appreciate what you have.

Timmy brought the stick and the gold coin back to Tom. He said, "Look, Tom! I found a big stick and a reward for us!" Tom was happy and said, "Thank you, Timmy. I'm sorry I was bossy." From that day on, Tom and Timmy were good friends and shared the gold coin.

The girl thanked the bald king for his help. They became good friends. From that day on, the bald king encouraged everyone who came to the tower to be brave and try new things.

Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big pile of ash near a bench. It was from a fire that happened a long time ago. Sara wanted to poke the ash with a stick. She thought it was fun and curious.

"Look, Ben, what is this?" Sara said, holding the stick.

Ben shook his head. He did not like the ash. He thought it was dirty and scary. He remembered the fire and how it made loud noises and bright lights. He wanted to go away.

"That is ash, Sara. It is from an ancient fire. It is bad. Do not poke it. It can hurt you," Ben said, pulling Sara's hand.

Sara did not listen. She wanted to poke the ash more. She thought Ben was silly and scared. She pulled her hand back and ran to the pile. She poked the ash with the stick. She laughed and smiled.

"See, Ben, it is not bad. It is soft and gray. It does not hurt me. It is fun," Sara said, poking the ash more.

Ben was angry and worried. He did not want Sara to poke the ash. He thought she was naughty and foolish. He ran to the pile and grabbed the stick. He tried to take it from Sara.

"Stop, Sara, stop! Give me the stick. You have to stop poking the ash. It is dangerous. It can make you sick. It can make you dirty. It can make you sad," Ben said, pulling the stick.

Sara and Ben fought over the stick. They pulled and pushed and shouted. They did not see the man who was walking to the bench. He was the owner of the ash. He was an old man who liked to smoke. He had left his ashtray on the bench. He was not happy to see Sara and Ben poking his ash.

"Hey, you kids, what are you doing? That is my ash. Leave it alone. Go away. You are making a mess. You are being rude. You are being bad," the man said, yelling at Sara and Ben.

Sara and Ben stopped fighting. They dropped the stick. They looked at the man. They felt scared and sorry. They did not know the ash was his. They did not mean to make a mess. They did not mean to be rude. They did not mean to be bad.

"We are sorry, sir. We did not know. We were just playing. We will go away. We will not poke your ash again," Sara and Ben said, in a small voice.

The man nodded. He picked up his ashtray. He walked away. He did not say anything more. He did not smile.

Sara and Ben ran to their mom. They told her what happened. She hugged them. She told them to be careful and respectful. She told them to not poke things that are not theirs. She told them to not play with ash. She told them to play with something else.

Sara and Ben nodded. They learned their lesson. They did not poke the ash anymore. They played with something else. They played with their ball. They had fun. They were happy.

"Please, Tom, I want the squash. It is so big and yellow. It will make a good soup," Lily said.

Lily was persistent. She did not listen to Tom. She pulled and pulled on the squash. The vine broke and the squash fell to the ground. Lily was happy. She lifted the squash and ran to the house.

Tom was sad. He liked the squash. He wanted to see it grow bigger and bigger. He followed Lily to the house. He hoped she would change her mind and settle the squash back on the vine.

But Lily did not change her mind. She went to the kitchen and put the squash on the table. She took a knife and tried to cut the squash. But the squash was too hard. His mom laughed and said, "A shrug is when you raise your shoulders like this." She showed him how to shrug. "It means you do not know or do not care about something."

Tom tried to shrug and said, "Like this?"

His mom said, "Yes, like that. But be careful, Tom. Sometimes a shrug can be rude or mean. You should not shrug when someone asks you something important or when someone needs your help or when someone is sad or angry. You should only shrug when it is okay to do so."

Anna liked to play with her toys, especially her bear. She named him Brownie and gave him hugs and kisses every day. She took him everywhere with her, even to the park.

One day, she saw a big dog at the park. The dog was black and white and had a long tail. He looked friendly, but Anna was scared. She held Brownie tight and hid behind a bench.

The dog came closer and sniffed the air. He smelled Brownie and wagged his tail. He wanted to play with the bear. He jumped over the bench and licked Anna's face.

Anna screamed and pushed the dog away. She was angry and afraid. She thought the dog wanted to hurt Brownie. She shouted, "Go away! Don't touch my bear!"

The dog was confused and sad. He didn't mean to scare Anna. He just wanted to be friends. He whimpered and walked away.

A lady came over and saw what happened. She was the dog's owner. She said to Anna, "I'm sorry, sweetie. My dog didn't want to harm your bear. He likes bears too. He has one at home. His name is Spot. He was just curious and playful. He wanted to say hello to you and your bear."

Anna looked at the lady and the dog. She saw that the dog was calm and gentle. He had a bear in his mouth. He looked like he was sorry. Anna felt bad for yelling at him. She said, "I'm sorry too. I was scared. I love my bear very much. He is my best friend. I didn't want to lose him."

The lady smiled and said, "I understand. It's okay to love your bear. But you don't have to be afraid of dogs. They can be your friends too. They can be kind and loyal and fun. You just have to be calm and gentle with them. Do you want to pet Spot and see his bear?"

Anna nodded and said, "Yes, please." She put Brownie down and reached out her hand. She touched Spot's fur and felt how soft and warm it was. She said, "Hi, Spot. You're a nice dog. I'm sorry I was mean to you. Can I see your bear?"

Spot wagged his tail and dropped his bear. He nudged it with his nose and gave it to Anna. Anna picked it up and saw that it was brown and fuzzy, just like Brownie. She said, "Wow, your bear is cute. What's his name?"

The lady said, "His name is Buddy. He is Spot's best friend. He takes him everywhere with him, even to the park."

Anna smiled and said, "That's funny. Brownie is my best friend too. He goes everywhere with me, even to the park. Maybe we can be friends too. Do you want to play with us?"

The lady said, "Sure, that would be lovely. Come on, Spot. Let's play with Anna and Brownie."

Anna, Spot, Brownie, and Buddy played together at the park. They had a lot of fun. They learned to share and be nice to each other. They became good friends.

The moral of the story is: Don't judge others by their appearance. Be calm and gentle with animals. They can be your friends too.

Tim and Sam felt scared and sorry. They did not know the toys were broken or belonged to the man. They thought they were trash.

"Please, mister, we did not mean to steal. We just wanted to play. We are sorry," Sam said. He looked at the man with big eyes.

He sighed and said, "Okay, okay, I guess you did not know. But you can't keep these toys. They are not safe or good. They might hurt you or break more. You have to give them back to me."

Tim and Sam nodded. They gave back the toys to the man. They felt sad to lose their new toys.

"Wow, these are awesome!" Tim said.

The man smiled too and said, "You're welcome. Now, go and play. And remember, don't take things that are not yours. And have fun with your toys."

The bus driver is a nice lady. She says hello to everyone. She tells them to put on their seat belts. She says the bus will take them to see ancient things. The bus starts to move. Lily and Ben look out the window. They see the museum, the park, the shops and the cars.

The bus stops at a big gate. The gate has a sign that says "Ancient Park". The bus driver says they are here. She says they can get off the bus and see the ancient things. She says she will wait for them. Lily and Ben are excited. They hold Mom and Dad's hands and get off the bus.

They see many ancient things in the park. They see bones, rocks, pots, coins and statues. They see a big skeleton of a dinosaur. It is very tall and long. Lily and Ben think it is amazing. They take pictures with the dinosaur. They have fun in the park. They learn a lot about ancient things. They thank the bus driver for the tour. They go back to the bus. They are happy and tired. They go home and tell their friends about their adventure.

Lily liked to sort her toys by color. She had a big box with many small boxes inside. She put the red toys in one box, the blue toys in another, and so on. She was very careful with her toys, because some of them were fragile and could break easily.

One day, she found a new toy in her box. It was a long, thin, white thing. She did not know what it was, but it looked like a toy. She tried to bend it, but it did not bend. She tried to squeeze it, but it did not squeeze. She wondered what it could do.

She decided to put it in the white box, with the other white toys. But the white box was full, and there was no room for the new toy. She pushed and pushed, but the new toy did not fit. She pushed harder, and then she heard a loud snap.

The new toy broke in half. Lily was shocked and sad. She looked at the broken pieces, and saw that they had a dusty powder on them. She touched the powder, and it felt soft and smooth. She rubbed it on her hand, and it made a white mark. She rubbed it on the floor, and it made another mark.

She realized that the new toy was not a toy, but a chalk. She had seen her teacher use chalk to write on the board at school. She felt silly for breaking the chalk, but also curious. She wondered what else she could write with the chalk. She picked up the pieces, and started to draw on the floor. She drew a big heart, and wrote her name inside. She smiled, and forgot about the broken chalk. She had found a new way to play.

Ben was a boy who liked to take things that were not his. He took toys from his friends, books from his teacher, and snacks from his mom. He did not say sorry or share with anyone. He hid all the things he took in his room, which was very filthy.

One day, his dad took him to his office. His dad worked with computers and papers and pens. Ben saw many things he wanted to take. He took a mouse from a desk, a pen from a drawer, and a paper from a printer. He put them in his pocket and smiled.

But his dad saw what he did. He was very angry and sad. He said, "Ben, you cannot take things that are not yours. That is wrong and rude. You have to give them back and say sorry. How would you feel if someone took your things?"

Ben felt bad. He knew his dad was right. He took out the things he took and gave them back to the people who owned them. He said sorry to each one. They were surprised and glad. Ben felt better too.

He learned that taking things that are not yours is not nice or fun. He learned that sharing and being honest is better. He decided to clean his room and give back the things he took from his friends, his teacher, and his mom. He said sorry to them too. They were happy and proud of him. Ben was happy and proud of himself. He did not take things that were not his anymore.

Tim likes to design things with his crayons and paper. He makes cars, houses, animals and people. He wants to be a cop when he grows up, like his dad. His dad is a cop who helps people and catches bad guys.

One day, Tim and his dad go to the park. Tim brings his crayons and paper. He sees a big tree and decides to design a tree house. He draws a ladder, a door, a window and a flag. He shows his dad his design.

"Wow, Tim, that's a great tree house!" his dad says. "You are very good at designing things. Maybe you can be a cop and a designer when you grow up."

Tim smiles and says, "Thank you, dad. I want to be like you. You are a good cop and a good dad."

They hear a siren and see a police car. A cop gets out of the car and walks towards them. He has a badge, a hat and a radio. He looks at Tim and his dad.

"Hello, sir. I'm Officer Mike. I'm looking for a lost dog. Have you seen a brown dog with a red collar?" he asks.

Tim and his dad shake their heads. They have not seen the dog.

"No, Officer Mike. We have not seen the dog. We are sorry," Tim's dad says.

"That's okay, sir. Thank you for being polite. I hope you find the dog soon," Tim says.

Officer Mike smiles and says, "Thank you, Tim. You are very polite too. And I like your tree house design. It's very creative. Maybe you can help me find the dog. Do you want to use my radio?"

Tim nods and says, "Yes, please. I want to help you."

Officer Mike gives Tim his radio and shows him how to use it. Tim holds the radio and says, "Hello, this is Tim. I'm a cop and a designer. I'm looking for a brown dog with a red collar. If you see the dog, please tell me. Over."

He hears a voice on the radio. It says, "Hello, Tim. This is Officer Lisa. I'm a cop too. I have found the dog. He is safe and happy. He is with his owner. Over."

Tim is happy and says, "That's great, Officer Lisa. Thank you for finding the dog. You are a good cop. Over."

Officer Mike and Tim's dad are proud of Tim. They clap and cheer. Tim gives the radio back to Officer Mike and says, "Thank you, Officer Mike. You are a good cop too. And thank you for letting me use your radio. It was fun."

Officer Mike says, "You're welcome, Tim. You are a good cop and a designer too. And thank you for helping me. It was fun too."

They all hug and say goodbye. Tim and his dad go home. Tim tells his mom about his adventure. He shows her his tree house design. She says, "Wow, Tim, that's a wonderful tree house. You are very good at designing things. And you are very brave and helpful. You are a good cop and a good son."

Tim smiles and says, "Thank you, mom. I love you."

The end.

Tom and Lily were playing on the beach. They liked to build sand castles and dig holes. Sometimes they would run to the water and splash each other. They had a lot of fun.

One day, they saw a big boat on the sea. It was white and had a flag. They wondered who was on the boat and where it was going. They decided to imagine a story about the boat.

"Maybe the boat is full of pirates," Tom said. "They have swords and hats and parrots. They are looking for treasure on an island."

"Or maybe the boat is full of princesses and princes," Lily said. "They have crowns and dresses and jewels. They are going to a ball at a castle."

They both liked their stories. They pretended to be pirates and princesses. They made a treasure map and a crown out of shells and seaweed. They sang songs and danced.

Suddenly, they heard a loud horn. It was the boat. It was leaving the sea and going to the harbor. They waved to the boat and shouted goodbye.

A man on the boat waved back. He had a beard and a smile. He looked wise and kind. He shouted to them: "Hello, children! I like your stories. You have great imaginations. Keep dreaming and playing. You never know what adventures you might find."

Tom and Lily smiled. They felt happy and curious. They thanked the man and asked him who he was and where he was going.

The man said: "I am a writer. I write books for children like you. I travel around the world and get ideas for my stories. I am going to a new place now. Maybe I will write a story about you and your stories."

Tom and Lily were amazed. They wanted to read his books. They asked him his name.

The man said: "My name is Jack. Jack the Writer. Maybe you will see my books in the library or the bookstore. Look for my name and my flag. It has a star and a moon. Goodbye, children. Have a wonderful day."

The man waved again and the boat sailed away. Tom and Lily waved back. They felt proud and excited. They hoped to see his books someday. They wondered what stories he would write. They decided to keep imagining and playing. They had a lot of fun.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They hop on the grass and the swings. They have fun.

One day, Anna sees a big bunny in the park. The bunny is white and fluffy. It hops very fast and high. Anna wants to play with the bunny. She runs after it.

"Wait for me, bunny!" Anna says. "You hop so well. I want to hop with you."

But the bunny is scared of Anna. It hops away from her. It hops over the fence and into the woods. Anna is sad. She cannot hop over the fence.

Ben sees Anna. He runs to her.

"What is wrong, Anna?" Ben asks. "Why are you sad?"

"I saw a bunny, Ben. A big, white, fluffy bunny. It hops so well. I wanted to play with it. But it ran away from me. It hopped over the fence. I cannot hop over the fence." Anna says.

Ben hugs Anna. He is a good friend.

"I am sorry, Anna. The bunny was not nice. It did not want to play with you. But I want to play with you. You are my friend. You hop very well too. You hop better than the bunny." Ben says.

Anna smiles. She feels better. She is not envious of the bunny anymore.

"Thank you, Ben. You are my friend too. You are very kind. Let's hop together. Let's hop on the grass and the swings. Let's have fun." Anna says.

Anna and Ben hop together. They hop on the grass and the swings. They have fun. They do not need the bunny. They have each other. They have a dream. They dream of hopping all over the world. They are happy.

One day, they went to the park with their moms. They saw a big hill. They wanted to climb the hill and see the sunset. The sunset was when the sky turned red and orange and yellow.

The man saw them. He was angry. He did not like them. He shouted at them and chased them. Tom and Sam were scared. They ran away. They tripped and fell. They hurt their knees and elbows. They cried.

Tom and Sam were sad. They said they were sorry. They said they only wanted to match. They said they liked the sunset. But their moms did not listen. They took them home. They did not see the sunset. They did not have fun. They had a bad day.

Tim and Liz were scared of the big dog. They ran to the slide and climbed up. The big dog ran after them. He barked and jumped. He wanted to play with them. The figure followed the big dog. He called his name and pulled the rope.

Tim and Liz reached the top of the slide. They looked down. The big dog was at the bottom. He looked up and wagged his tail. He waited for them to slide down. Tim and Liz did not want to slide down. They leaned back and held on to the slide.

The figure came to the slide. He smiled and said hello. He told Tim and Liz that the big dog was friendly and gentle. He said that the big dog just wanted to say hello. He asked Tim and Liz if they wanted to pet the big dog.

Tim and Liz looked at the figure. They looked at the big dog. The big dog looked happy and calm. He did not bark or jump. He sat and tilted his head. He looked cute and curious.

"Wow, this is fun!" Tom said.

Tom and Mia nodded. They understood. They said sorry to Mom and Dad. They helped to clean up the mess. They learned their lesson. They never played with the razor again.

Mia and Ben felt alone and unhappy. They wished they had never had a picnic. They wished they had stayed inside and watched TV. They wished the mosquito had never come. They wished Spot had never spilled their juice.

They hugged each other and cried. They had a very bad day.

Tom and Mia are playing in the park. They see a big boat on the lake. The boat has a flag with a picture of a sailor on it.

"Look, a sailor boat!" Tom says. "I want to go on it!"

"Me too!" Mia says. "But how can we get there?"

They run to the edge of the lake. They see a man with a hat and a whistle. He is the sailor. He has a small boat with seats for children.

"Hello, children!" the sailor says. "Do you want to ride on my boat? I have some seats available."

"Yes, please!" Tom and Mia say. They give the sailor some coins. He helps them get on the boat. He gives them life jackets and tells them to sit still.

The sailor blows his whistle and starts the boat. The boat goes fast on the water. Tom and Mia feel the wind and the spray. They see the big boat with the flag. They wave to the people on it.

"This is fun!" Tom says.

"I love it!" Mia says.

But then, Tom sees a ball floating on the water. He likes balls. He wants to kick it.

"Look, a ball!" Tom says. He stands up and tries to reach it.

"Tom, no!" Mia says. "Sit down!"

But Tom does not listen. He leans over the boat and kicks the ball. He kicks too hard. He falls off the boat and into the water.

"Help!" Tom cries. "I can't swim!"

The sailor hears Tom. He stops the boat and turns around. He throws a rope to Tom and pulls him back on the boat.

"Are you okay, Tom?" the sailor asks.

"I'm sorry, sailor," Tom says. "I was silly. I wanted to kick the ball."

"That was very dangerous, Tom," the sailor says. "You could have drowned. You must never stand up or kick on the boat. You must always listen to me and Mia."

"I know, sailor," Tom says. "I won't do it again. Thank you for saving me."

"You're welcome, Tom," the sailor says. "But now we have to go back to the shore. The ride is over."

Tom and Mia hug the sailor and say goodbye. They get off the boat and go back to the park. They are wet and cold, but they are happy. They learned a lesson. They will never kick on the boat again.

"Let's play couch fort!" Lily said. "We can use pillows and blankets and make a secret hideout."

They ran to the couch and started to build their fort. They spend a long time making it cozy and strong. They used cushions and sheets and chairs and books. They made a door and a window and a flag.

They crawled inside their fort and pretended they were spies. They whispered and giggled and told each other secrets. They had a lot of fun.

But then they heard a harsh voice. It was Mom. She was angry.

"What have you done to the couch?" she yelled. "You made a big mess. You ruined the pillows and the blankets. You have to clean it up right now."

Lily and Ben felt scared and sad. They did not mean to make Mom mad. They just wanted to play.

"Sorry, Mom," they said. "We were just playing couch fort. We did not know you would be upset."

Mom sighed. She saw their faces. They looked sorry. She felt sorry too.

"I know you were just playing," she said. "But you have to be careful with the couch. It is not a toy. It is for sitting and resting. You have to respect it and keep it clean."

She helped them clean up the mess. She hugged them and kissed them.

"I love you, Lily and Ben," she said. "But next time, please ask me before you play couch fort. OK?"

"OK, Mom," they said. "We love you too."

They learned their lesson. They still liked to play couch fort, but only with Mom's permission. And they always cleaned up after themselves. They did not want to make Mom angry again. They wanted to make her happy.

One day, Lily and Ben are playing with the aeroplane in their room. They pretend to fly to different places and have fun. But then, they hear their mom calling them.

"Kids, it's time to clean up your room. Put your toys away and come downstairs for lunch."

Lily and Ben do not want to stop playing. They want to fly the aeroplane more.

"Mom, can we play a little more? Please?" Lily asks.

"No, Lily. You have played enough. You need to eat and rest. And your room is very messy. You need to be organized and tidy." Mom says.

Lily and Ben are sad and angry. They do not like to clean up. They think it is boring and hard. They have an idea.

"Let's lock the door and hide the aeroplane. Then mom can't make us clean up." Ben whispers to Lily.

"OK, let's do that." Lily agrees.

They run to the door and turn the key. They lock the door. Then they put the aeroplane under the bed and cover it with a blanket. They think they are very clever.

But mom is not happy. She knocks on the door and tries to open it. She can't.

"Lily, Ben, open the door right now. This is not funny. You are being naughty." Mom says.

Lily and Ben do not answer. They giggle and hug the aeroplane. They think they are safe.

But mom is not giving up. She goes to get the spare key. She unlocks the door and opens it. She sees Lily and Ben and the aeroplane. She is very angry.

"Lily, Ben, how could you do this? You disobeyed me and locked the door. And you hid the aeroplane. That is not nice. You need to say sorry and give me the aeroplane. And you need to clean up your room. Now." Mom says.

Lily and Ben are scared. They see mom's face and hear her voice. They know they did something bad. They feel sorry.

"Sorry, mom. We were wrong. We won't do it again. Here is the aeroplane. We will clean up our room. Please don't be mad." Lily and Ben say.

Mom takes the aeroplane and puts it on the shelf. She hugs Lily and Ben and kisses them.

"I love you, kids. But you need to listen to me and follow the rules. Cleaning up is important. It helps you to be organized and responsible. And locking the door is dangerous. What if there was a fire or an emergency? You need to be careful and respectful. Do you understand?" Mom says.

Lily and Ben nod and say yes. They understand. They are sorry. They love mom too.

They start to clean up their room. They put their toys in the boxes and the books on the shelf. They make their bed and sweep the floor. They work together and help each other. They are organized and tidy.

Mom is proud of them. She smiles and says:

"Good job, kids. You are doing great. When you finish, you can come downstairs for lunch. I made your favorite. Sandwiches and juice. And maybe, after lunch, you can play with the aeroplane again. But only if you promise to put it away when you are done. Do you promise?" Mom says.

Lily and Ben promise. They are happy. They finish cleaning up and go downstairs for lunch. They eat and drink and talk to mom. They thank her for the food and the aeroplane. They are good kids. They are happy.

"Hello, mule!" Sara said. "Do you want to play with us?"

The mule looked at Sara and Ben and nodded. He seemed harmless and friendly. Sara and Ben invited the mule to join them. They ran around the field, played hide and seek, and picked flowers.

But there was a problem. The mule was bigger and stronger than Sara and Ben. He did not know how to be gentle and careful. Sometimes, he bumped into them, stepped on their toes, or ate their flowers. Sara and Ben got hurt and sad.

"Ouch, mule! You are too rough!" Sara cried.

"Sorry, mule! You are too greedy!" Ben said.

The mule did not understand why Sara and Ben were angry. He thought they were having fun. He tried to make them happy by nuzzling them and making funny noises. But Sara and Ben did not like it. They pushed the mule away and ran to the barn.

"Go away, mule! We don't want to play with you anymore!" Sara and Ben shouted.

The mule felt lonely and confused. He did not mean to hurt or upset Sara and Ben. He just wanted to be their friend. He followed them to the barn, hoping they would change their mind.

But when he got to the barn, he saw something scary. A big, mean dog was barking and growling at Sara and Ben. The dog had sharp teeth and claws and wanted to bite them. Sara and Ben were trapped and scared.

"Help, help!" Sara and Ben screamed.

The mule heard their cries and saw the dog. He knew he had to do something. He ran to the dog and kicked him with his hooves. The dog yelped and ran away. The mule had saved Sara and Ben.

"Thank you, mule! You are brave and kind!" Sara and Ben said.

They hugged the mule and apologized for being rude and mean. They realized that the mule was not harmful, but helpful. They learned to appreciate his differences and strengths. They invited the mule to play with them again, and this time, they were more gentle and careful. The mule was happy and smiled. He had found true friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went outside to play in the snow with her friend, Max. Lily wore her favorite pink mittens, but Max forgot his. 

Max said, "I'm cold, Lily. Can I borrow your mittens?"

Lily replied, "I don't know if I trust you with my favorite mittens. They're tough, but they might get lost or dirty."

Max said, "Please, Lily. I promise I'll take good care of them."

Lily thought for a moment and decided to trust Max. She gave him her mittens, and they continued to play in the snow. But soon, Max accidentally dropped one of the mittens in the snow, and they couldn't find it. 

Lily was upset, but Max apologized and promised to buy her a new pair of mittens. Lily forgave him, and they continued to play in the snow, happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a big race in the park. Many people came to watch the race. An elderly man came too. He wanted to watch the race with his grandson.

The race started and the people ran very fast. Everyone was happy. But then, the elderly man's grandson got lost in the crowd. The man looked everywhere for his grandson but he couldn't find him.

He went to the gate and tried to open it but it was locked. He couldn't get out of the park. He was so sad and worried about his grandson. He cried and shouted for help but no one heard him. In the end, the man had to wait until the park opened again in the morning. He spent the whole night alone, waiting for his grandson to come back.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, but her room was getting very messy. Her mommy said, "Lily, let's pack up your toys in a cardboard box so we can clean your room." Lily helped her mommy put all of her toys in the box. 

After they finished packing, Lily started to spin around and around. She got so dizzy that she fell down on the floor and giggled. "Mommy, I feel dizzy!" she said. Her mommy helped her up and they went outside to get some fresh air. 

When they came back inside, they saw that Lily's room was all clean and tidy. "Wow, it looks great!" said Lily. She was happy that they packed up her toys and cleaned her room. From that day on, Lily made sure to pack up her toys after she was done playing with them, so her room would stay clean.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat pears. One day, Lily found a brown pear on the ground. It was dirty, so she decided to clean it. She got a wet cloth and wiped the pear until it was clean. Then, she took a big bite and it was delicious! The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the park to play on the swings and slide. One day, she saw a man selling ice cream. She asked her mommy if she could have some, but her mommy said they didn't have any money to pay for it.

Lily felt sad, but then she remembered something her teacher had told her at school. She could help her mommy save money by not wasting food and turning off the lights when she left a room. So, she started doing those things and soon enough, her mommy had enough money to buy her an ice cream cone.

Lily felt so cheerful and happy that she had helped her mommy save money and they could now pay for the ice cream. From that day on, Lily always remembered to not waste and to help her mommy save money.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. Lily liked to play with her toys and draw pictures. One day, Lily's mom wanted to introduce her to a new friend. Her name was Sarah. Sarah was very nice and played with Lily's toys. Lily thought Sarah was a useful friend to have.

But then, Lily's mom had to go to work. Lily didn't want to be alone, so she asked Sarah to stay and play with her. Sarah said yes, but she had to leave soon because she had work too. Lily didn't understand what work was, but she was sad that Sarah had to go.

Later that day, Lily's mom came home and found out that Sarah had taken some of their things. Sarah had been stealing from them. Lily's mom was very upset and told Lily that Sarah was not a good friend. Lily was sad and didn't understand why Sarah would do such a thing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys on the big cushion in her living room. One day, Lily's friend Timmy came over to play. 

"Wow, that's a really big cushion!" Timmy said. 

Lily replied, "Yes, it's very generous. We can both sit on it and play together." 

They played with their toys for a while, but then Lily's little brother came into the room. He wanted to play too, but there wasn't enough room on the cushion for all three of them. 

"I want to play too!" Lily's brother cried. 

Lily said, "Sorry, there's not enough room. You can look at us playing though." 

Lily's brother got upset and knocked over the cushion, causing all the toys to fall off. Lily and Timmy were sad that their game was ruined. 

The end.

There was a boy named Timmy. He loved to play outside, but it started to rain. Timmy's mom told him to come inside. When Timmy got inside, he saw his dog, Max. Max had a dirty head from playing outside in the mud. Timmy's mom said they could give Max a bath later to clean his head. Timmy was happy to be inside with his dog, even though it was raining outside.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a dog named Max who loved to ride in the car with her. One day, Lily and Max went to visit her friend at her house. Her friend had a big lab who was very smelly.

Lily said to her friend, "Your dog is smelly, but I still like him." Her friend replied, "I know, he needs a bath." Then Lily asked, "Can we ride your bike?" Her friend said, "Sure! Let's go ride it in the park."

So Lily and her friend went to the park and rode the bike together. Max ran behind them and barked happily. They had so much fun riding together and didn't even notice the smelly lab anymore. They were happy just being together and having fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who had a new puppy. The puppy was very small and cute. Lily loved to play with her puppy every day. They would run and jump and have lots of fun together.

One day, Lily's family decided to celebrate her birthday. They had a big party with lots of yummy cake and presents. Lily was very happy and excited. She showed her new puppy to all of her friends and they thought it was very cute too.

After the party, Lily and her puppy were tired from all the excitement. They cuddled up together and fell asleep. Lily thought her puppy was the best birthday present ever. She knew that her puppy was a perfect fit for her family and she loved it very much.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and put on makeup. One day, Lily's mom gave her a purple lipstick to play with. Lily was so happy and put it on right away.

Lily's brother, Max, came into the room and said, "Wow! Your lips look so pretty!" Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Max!"

But then, Lily accidentally dropped the lipstick and it rolled under the couch. "Oh no!" Lily said. "I can't reach it!"

Max saw that Lily was sad and wanted to help. He reached under the couch and found the lipstick. "Here you go, Lily!" Max said, handing her the lipstick.

Lily was so grateful and gave Max a big hug. "You're the best brother ever!" she said.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play hide and seek with his friends. One day, Timmy found a big castle in the woods. He thought it would be the perfect place to play hide and seek. Timmy ran to his friends and told them about the castle. They all agreed to play there.

When they arrived at the castle, Timmy's friends started to hide. Timmy searched and searched, but he couldn't find anyone. He looked high and low, but still no one. Timmy started to feel sad and sorry that he couldn't find his friends.

Suddenly, Timmy heard giggling coming from behind a big rock. He ran over and found his friends hiding there. They all laughed and played together. Timmy learned that sometimes things are hidden, but they can always be found if you look hard enough. He also learned that it's important to say sorry when you make a mistake.

Once upon a time, there was a curious little girl named Lily. She was very interested in the world around her and loved to explore new things. One day, she went to the park and met an old man sitting on a bench.

"Hello, what's your name?" asked Lily.

"My name is Mr. Smith. How old are you?" replied the old man.

"I'm three years old, but I don't know what that number means," said Lily.

"It means you're still very young and have lots of time to learn and grow," explained Mr. Smith.

Lily was very happy to have learned something new and thanked Mr. Smith for his help. She continued to explore the park, feeling even more curious about the world around her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and enjoy the sunshine. One day, she went to the park with her mommy and daddy. Lily ran around and played on the swings and slide. She felt happy and her body felt strong.

But then, Lily met a bossy boy who didn't want to share the toys. He told her what to do and didn't let her have fun. Lily didn't like how he acted, so she went to her mommy and daddy. They helped her talk to the boy and they all played together. Lily was happy again and enjoyed her day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing in the woods near her house. One day, while she was playing, she met a little bird. The bird was very worried because it had lost its way home.

Lily felt sorry for the bird and wanted to help it. She asked the bird where it lived, and the bird told her it lived in a tree. Lily knew the woods very well and she knew which tree the bird was talking about. She took the bird to the tree and the bird was very happy to be home.

Lily felt happy too because she had helped the bird. She learned that it's important to help others when they are worried or in trouble. Lily continued to play in the woods, but she always kept an eye out for any animals that might need her help.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to run and play in the meadow. One day, Benny felt a rumble in his tummy and knew he had to go to the toilet. He ran as fast as he could to find a toilet.

As Benny searched for a toilet, he felt lonely and scared. He didn't know where to go. Suddenly, he saw a big, red building. Benny thought it might be the toilet he was looking for. He ran towards it with excitement.

When Benny got closer, he realized that it was not a toilet, but a fire station. The firefighters saw Benny and knew he was lost. They helped him find his way back home. Benny was so happy and grateful. From then on, he made sure to always remember where the toilet was before he went to play.

Once upon a time, there was a man who was very ugly. He had a big nose and crooked teeth, and no one wanted to be his friend. One day, the man saw a little bird with a broken wing. He felt sorry for the bird and decided to help it.

The man took the bird home and made a cozy nest for it. He gave the bird food and water every day until its wing was healed. The bird was very happy and grateful to the man for helping it.

One night, the man was very tired and he yawned loudly. The little bird saw the man's big, kind heart and flew up to his face to give him a kiss. From that day on, the man was no longer ugly because he had a friend who loved him for who he was. The moral of the story is that true beauty comes from being kind and helpful to others.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to ride her bike in the park. One day, she saw a boy with a bike that had a label on it. She asked him, "What does the label say?" The boy replied, "It says my bike is cheap, but it still works."

Lily felt bad for the boy and said, "Don't worry, my bike is cheap too, but it's still fun to ride." The boy smiled and said, "You're right, it's not about how much your bike costs, it's about the joy it brings you." 

From that day on, Lily and the boy became friends and they rode their bikes together every day. They learned that it doesn't matter how much something costs, as long as it makes you happy. The moral of the story is that true friendship is not based on material things, but on the joy you share together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play in the dirt and make big piles. One day, Timmy had an idea. He wanted to build a pit in his backyard. 

Timmy grabbed his shovel and started digging. He dug and dug until he made a big hole in the ground. He was so proud of his pit! It was big and deep, just like he wanted. 

But Timmy was also humble. He knew he couldn't do it alone. So, he asked his friends to come and play in his pit with him. They all had so much fun together, playing and laughing in the dirt. 

From that day on, Timmy and his friends loved to build and play in their pit. It was their special place where they could be together and have fun. And Timmy was happy that he could share it with his friends. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He liked to watch the birds in the sky. One day, he went to the beach and found a shell. It was an ordinary shell, but Timmy thought it was very pretty. He put it in his pocket and showed it to his mom. She smiled and said, "That's a nice shell, Timmy." Timmy was happy that his mom liked his shell. He kept it in his room and would watch it every day before going to bed. The end.
